blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which choices change the price of a swimsuit most, such as recycled or speciality fabric, underwires, lining, hardware or bonded seams?
items.answer: The biggest factors are how complex the style is, standard or speciality fabric, sublimation, underwires and moulded cups, hardware and packaging. Full lining costs more than front-only lining, and bonded seams cost more than stitched ones. Your quote lists each of these choices. If you remove bonded seams, moulded cups or full lining after sampling, the fit and construction change, so the style needs resampling and another wear test.

items.question: Does a UPF rating such as UPF 50+ cover only the fabric or the finished swimwear, and what standard and supporting evidence address protection when wet or stretched?
items.answer: A UPF rating such as UPF 50+ applies to the fabric, not the finished swimsuit. We only state it when a laboratory report to AS/NZS 4399 or EN 13758-1 backs it up, and we send you that report with your order.

items.question: What care instructions do you put on swimwear care labels so my customers' suits last longer?
items.answer: Your custom care labels can show fibre content along with instructions to rinse in cool fresh water after the pool or sea, hand wash, avoid the tumble dryer, dry flat in the shade and wash off sunscreen promptly so it doesn't stain.

items.question: Can you manufacture with cups, underwires or swim elastics that I supply, and what compatibility limits apply?
items.answer: Yes. We sew with the components you supply as long as the underwires fit our 8–10 mm channelling, the cups match your pattern's cup size and shape, and the elastics are chlorine-resistant swim elastic 6 to 12 mm wide.

items.question: Which children's swimwear safety requirements can you meet for my destination market, particularly for cords, drawstrings and detachable small parts?
items.answer: For the US, we arrange CPSIA testing for lead, phthalates and flammability at a CPSC-accepted laboratory so you can issue the [Children's Product Certificate](/kids-hawaiian-clothing-manufacturer/). For the EU, we make cords and drawstrings to EN 14682. Children's sizes have no hood or neck drawstrings and no toggles. Waist cords are bar-tacked at centre back, and their free ends are no longer than 7.5 cm. Baby sizes have no detachable decorative small parts.

items.question: Beyond checking measurements and seam tension, how do you assess whether cups, straps and leg openings stay secure during swimming?
items.answer: Before bulk, a fit model wears each sample for 30 minutes of swimming and poolside movement. During that time we check that the cups stay secure, the straps don't slip and the leg openings don't ride up or gape. Fabric and elastic must recover at least 90% of their stretch after 50 stretch cycles and a soak in chlorinated and salt water. If they don't, we adjust the patterns or elastic tension before you approve.

visuals.caption: Supplied underwires must fit our channelling; supplied elastics must also be chlorine-resistant.

seo.title: Boardshorts Manufacturer | Custom Cuts | Tapa Works
seo.description: Print options, waist and seam choices and a range of inseam lengths from a boardshorts manufacturer making custom orders.

hero.heading: Boardshorts Manufacturer for Teams, Businesses and Schools
lead: Your team's boardshorts keep their colour through pool training and sea sessions, seam to seam.

cta.label: Request a quote for boardshorts

blocks.heading: Quick-Dry Boardshort Fabrics Made for Salt Water and Chlorine
paragraphs: Our boardshorts are made from lightweight, quick-drying performance polyester that stands up to heavy use and chlorine. You can also choose recycled polyester or water-resistant or UV-resistant options. Polyester-spandex gives four-way stretch and resists salt water, chlorine and UV, and nylon-spandex gives more abrasion resistance. We pick fade-resistant fabrics, thread and stitching for pool and sea use. For swim shorts we use 120GSM microfibre polyester, and for beach shorts we use 110GSM fabric with digital prints.

visuals.purpose: Distinguish the stated fabric weights for swim shorts and beach shorts.
visuals.caption: Fabric weights for swim and beach styles.

blocks.heading: OEM Boardshorts: Fabrics, Samples & Production
paragraphs: We match the fabric weight and base to how your shorts will be used. Then we sample the shortlisted weights side by side so you can test hand feel and drying.
rows: We also offer 90GSM lightweight microfibre, 140GSM polyester peach skin and 160GSM four-way-stretch polyester-spandex. For extra durability there is a heavier 180–200GSM 80% nylon 20% spandex.
From 110 to 160GSM, including nylon taslan, in rigid or two-way mechanical-stretch construction.
From 160 to 220GSM, including polyester-spandex jersey, with four-way-stretch spandex blends for active and compression styles.

We've run our [factory-owned production and export business](/about-us/) since 2011, so we control quality, cost and delivery ourselves. You agree every B2B order with our team, not through an online shop or marketplace.

Our [Product Development service](/product-development/) works to your OEM specifications or develops ODM styles from your design, picture or idea. It covers tech packs, patterns, grading, fit samples, mill coordination and production markers.
Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We agree first-trial quantities with you case by case, within production limits.
A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design and covers its pattern or print in all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against bulk orders.

Our [Sampling service](/sampling/) makes one sample per style in size S or your chosen fit size. You use it to approve fit, stretch and construction and to ask for corrections. You pay for courier delivery, which costs an extra USD 50.
You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

Our [order process](/our-process/) starts by agreeing the price before sampling. For summer or resort launches, you approve the sample and pay the deposit at least 90 days before warehouse delivery, and earlier than that during January–April. Bulk production takes 35 to 40 days depending on size and season. Shipping by sea to the US or Europe takes about 25 to 35 days, and 1 to 2 weeks longer in peak shipping months. For stock in stores in May, you need to approve by mid-January.
Our English-speaking [contact team](/contact-us/) replies within one business day, and you can reach us by phone or video throughout your order.

Once we've reviewed your design, quantity, fabric and its availability, construction, lining, printing, branding, packaging, size ratio and lead time, you get our no-obligation [itemised quote](/request-a-quote/) within 24 hours.

blocks.heading: Custom Boardshorts: Your Prints, Patterns & Styles
paragraphs: We choose the print method to suit your artwork, fabric and order size.

items.heading: Full sublimation
paragraphs: This is our main method. It handles all-over, partial or logo layouts with no colour limit, and on polyester-spandex your artwork runs edge to edge from waistband to hem.

items.heading: Print durability
paragraphs: The dye goes into the polyester fibres, so the print moves with the fabric and doesn't crack.

items.heading: Screen printing
paragraphs: For simple logos and designs with only a few colours, we use screen printing to suit the artwork.

items.heading: Small-run DTF
paragraphs: DTF works on polyester-spandex and nylon-spandex with no screen setup, so it suits smaller runs and nylon fabrics.

items.heading: Patterns and styles
paragraphs: We make solid, women's, floral and tropical boardshorts. We use digital printing or sublimation for all-over designs, and we control floral repeats and colour matching.

items.heading: Exclusive print development
paragraphs: Our [Custom Print Design service](/custom-print-design/) turns your sketches, moodboards or references into exclusive, production-ready repeats. It covers colour separation, scaling for each garment, placement refinement and 3D mockups.

blocks.heading: Private Label Boardshorts: Construction, Branding & Pricing
paragraphs: We quote the standard specification first and price each upgrade separately, so you keep only the options your shorts need.
rows: Every pair comes with two side pockets, one back flap pocket, three eyelets, 2–3 wash labels, 1–2 hangtags and one standard drawcord. Branded cords cost extra.

At the waist, you can choose an adjustable drawstring, a faux fly, a waistband logo, a back label, and custom waistband or drawstring colours. At the hem, you can add an arc slit, contrast binding or a logo.
We triple stitch, flat-finish and reinforce our seams, and the seat stitching is reinforced three times. Concealed pockets, elastic closures and custom pocket systems are available.
You can choose drawstring styles with a back pocket, a side cut, a forward cut, or a forward cut with a back yoke.

Mesh briefs drain fast and give light support, so they suit swimming, beach and resort wear. Compression liners support the legs and limit chafe for surfing, paddling, beach volleyball and training. Going without a liner suits wetsuit or rash-guard use, hybrid walk shorts and wear over separate underlayers.

Your unit price goes up when you choose four-way stretch over non-stretch microfibre, recycled over virgin polyester, compression over mesh, extra pockets, zip or hook-and-loop closures, metal hardware, contrast binding, welded or bonded seams, longer inseams, or full sublimation or multi-colour screen prints over a single logo.
Non-stretch shells, no liner and fewer trims bring the price down. Large repeats or pattern matching use 10–15% more fabric, and that's already included in your unit price.

items.question: Do your UV-resistant boardshort fabrics provide rated UPF protection for the wearer, and which ratings and standards can you supply?
items.answer: A UV-resistant finish protects the fabric and the print. To protect the wearer, you need rated fabric, and we supply it at UPF 30, UPF 40 or UPF 50+. We only claim a rating after laboratory testing under AS/NZS 4399 or EN 13758-1, and the test report ships with your order. For pool and sea use, we offer chlorine-resistant polyester or nylon-spandex. Its colour fastness to sea water and chlorinated water targets Grade 4, a goal rather than a guaranteed grade.

items.question: Do you hold any board shorts in stock as blanks that I can order with just my logo added, and in which colours and sizes?
items.answer: Yes. We keep blanks in black, navy, grey and white in sizes S to XXL. The stock list we send on request confirms what's available now. Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, and you can mix sizes. Once you've paid, plain-blank orders dispatch within 3 business days. Adding a screen-printed or DTF logo takes 5 to 7 days before dispatch. Stock blanks are for quick orders in basic colours. Specific fabrics, cuts or performance ratings need custom production.

items.question: Which of your boardshort configurations are suitable for sustained surfing rather than occasional swimming or beachwear?
items.answer: For sustained surfing, we specify a four-way-stretch polyester/spandex shell with 8–10% spandex, a flat fixed waistband, a lace-up or hook-and-loop fly, a flat drawcord, a gusseted crotch, welded or triple-stitched seams and a zip back pocket with a key loop, all in a 17 to 20 inch outseam. For swimming, beachwear and group or promotional orders, we use non-stretch polyester or nylon microfibre shells with elastic or half-elastic waists and mesh brief liners instead.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What is the difference in construction between your elastic-waist swim trunks and your fixed-waist board shorts, and which one should my line use?
items.answer: Our elastic-waist swim trunks have a fully elastic waistband with a drawcord inside. Our fixed-waist board shorts have a flat or half-elastic waistband that closes with a lace-up, hook-and-loop or mock fly. An elastic waist stretches to fit a wide range of waist sizes. A fixed waistband barely gives, so each size fits a narrower range of wearers. Choose elastic-waist trunks for pool, resort and casual swim lines, where every size has to fit lots of wearers. Choose fixed-waist board shorts for surf and active lines, where the waist has to stay in place in the waves.

items.question: Which rust-resistant zips, eyelets and drawcord tips do you use, and can the aglets or cords carry my branding?
items.answer: For salt water, we use plastic coil or moulded zips, silicone or plastic drawcord tips that don't rust, and eyelets in coated rustproof metal or embroidered thread. Your logo can go on the aglets, and we can also weave or print your branding along the drawcord itself. A branded cord is priced separately from our standard drawcord.

items.question: Which logo methods do you use on swim trunks, and which last best through repeated swimming and washing?
items.answer: We apply logos with sublimation, silicone transfer, embroidery and patches. Sublimated logos and silicone transfers hold up longest through repeated swimming and washing, because they bond into the fabric or flex with it. Embroidery and patches work best on woven board-short fabric and dry a little more slowly.

items.question: How do your standard mesh and compression liners differ in support, ventilation, drying and thigh coverage, and where do sport mesh and power mesh fit among these choices?
items.answer: Our standard mesh liner is a brief-cut lining with light support. It ventilates freely and dries fastest. Our compression liner is a stretch short with firmer support that covers the upper thigh, but it dries a little more slowly. Sport mesh is the open, breathable fabric we use for brief liners. Power mesh is the firmer stretch mesh we use when you want compression-level support with more airflow.

paragraphs: For pools we use chlorine-resistant polyester-spandex or PBT blends. For sea and resort wear we use nylon-spandex, because chlorine breaks down standard elastane faster than seawater does.

items.heading: Sun and colour
paragraphs: A bikini fabric is sold as UPF 50+ only with its AS/NZS 4399 lab report. We aim for Grade 4 colourfastness to chlorinated water and seawater, but that's a target, not a guaranteed result.

items.heading: Lining and hold
paragraphs: You can pick self-fabric lining or a 100–130 GSM nylon/spandex swim lining. Wherever your design needs firmer support, we add front power mesh.

items.heading: Wet opacity
paragraphs: White and pale colours get a doubled front layer or a nude-tone lining. We test each colour wet during sampling so you can see how opaque it is.

items.heading: Pilling resistance
paragraphs: For your swim fabric specification, we pick fabrics rated Grade 3–4 or higher for pilling resistance.

blocks.heading: Bikini Shell Materials and Stretch Specifications
rows: You can choose 80% nylon 20% spandex or 82% polyester 18% spandex knits from 180 to 230 gsm, so your shells contain 18–20% spandex.
Recovery stays at 90% or more after repeated stretching, which keeps shells from sagging and bagging.
We record weight, stretch and recovery on your sampling spec sheet and check incoming lots before cutting. Lighter or less elastic fabric changes how the piece fits and wears.
Through our [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) service, you can pick soft, shape-recovering nylon/spandex, print-focused polyester/spandex and jacquards for your collection.

blocks.heading: Precision Cutting and Reinforced Stress Points

items.heading: Reinforced stress points
paragraphs: Straps, side seams and the crotch get extra stitching, because pulling the suit on and wearing it wet put the most strain there.

items.heading: Chlorine exposure checks
paragraphs: For pools, shells use chlorine-resistant elastane and edges use encased rubber elastic. At sampling, we check that stretch recovery stays at 90% or more after 50 hours in chlorinated water.

items.heading: Customer-supplied materials
paragraphs: For [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/), we cut your custom patterns precisely. Your materials arrive before cutting, with 5–8% extra fabric and 3% spare trims and labels. We inspect what arrives and report any shortages or defects within 2 business days, before anything is used.

blocks.heading: Clean Edges and Lined Bikini Gussets

items.heading: Approved edge finish
paragraphs: On your sample, we agree on visible fold-over elastic binding, lining-encased elastic, or bonded edges and seams, and that finish stays the same in bulk.

items.heading: Ruching and hold
paragraphs: For scrunch-back and ruched bottoms, we sew in elastic shirring as we go. Wherever your approved design needs more hold, we add power-net lining.

items.heading: Enclosed gusset seams
paragraphs: The crotch is fully lined in self fabric or nylon/spandex swim lining. We sew the front seam and enclose the back seam, so no raw edges touch the skin.

items.heading: Period swim construction
paragraphs: Period swim bottoms get an absorbent gusset with a leak-resistant barrier, set under a swim-grade polyamide/elastane or polyester/elastane shell.

blocks.heading: Removable Swim Pads and Secure Tie Finishes
rows: Choose perforated open-cell foam for quick drainage or closed-cell swim foam for very low water uptake. Both are 3 to 5 mm thick, and we check the pad you choose wet during sampling.
Swim-fabric covers keep the pads in shape through repeated wetting and drying, and stitched pockets have cleanly finished openings.
Ties are made from self-fabric tubing, and we seal the ends.

blocks.heading: Bikini Hardware Finishes and Decorative Details

items.heading: Matched metal finishes
paragraphs: Our zinc-alloy O-rings, sliders, adjusters and logo plates come in silver, gold, rose gold or matte black. We match the finish across your set, confirm it on the sample and test the hardware for saltwater corrosion.

items.heading: Decorative options
paragraphs: Tops, bottoms and ties can carry eyelets, lacing, beads, tassels, branded charms, ruffles and crochet, and the crochet can be edge trim or full panels.

items.heading: Skin-contact hardware
paragraphs: Our [metal trims](/trims-accessories/) meet the EU REACH nickel-release limit of 0.5 µg/cm²/week for prolonged skin contact, and nickel-free plating is available if you ask for it.

blocks.heading: Private Label Bikini Packaging and Care Labels

items.heading: Approved care labels
paragraphs: Through [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we draft fibre content based on the materials, origin, wash-tested care instructions and the RN or CA numbers your destination requires, and send it all to you for approval. We then check the labels on every private-label order.

items.heading: Sets or separates
paragraphs: Matched pairs go into one poly bag unless you ask for separates packing. With separates packing, your warehouse can pick each piece by size without opening and re-bagging sets.

items.heading: Hangtag position
paragraphs: Your hangtags go on the bottom side seam or the top strap, in whichever position your order specifies.

items.heading: Cup protection
paragraphs: Foam-cup and underwire tops are packed flat, cups nested, with a card insert, and are never folded through the cup. Each carton holds no more than 50 tops, laid flat in layers.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: For mix-and-match bikinis, does the 50-piece minimum apply to tops and bottoms separately, and can I order tops and bottoms in different sizes?
items.answer: Yes. Each top and each bottom counts as its own style, so you need 50 pieces per style per colour. You can spread each style across 3 to 4 sizes at no extra charge. The two size splits don't have to match. For example, tops can run S to XL while bottoms run XS to L, and each split follows your sales history for that piece.

items.question: Can you produce fully reversible bikinis with both faces wearable and seams, pads and labels concealed?
items.answer: Yes. We make both faces wearable, using either a solid and a print or two prints. The seams are enclosed, so no stitching or overlock shows. The pads sit in an internal pocket between the layers. Labels are either heat transfers or hidden inside the pad pocket.

items.question: Can you apply removable hygiene liners to bikini bottoms that stay attached through handling without leaving adhesive residue?
items.answer: Yes. Every bottom comes with a removable hygienic liner. Its low-tack adhesive stays in place through folding, packing and try-ons, and then it peels off without leaving residue. On orders over 3,000 units, we add your logo.

items.question: Can you build bikini tops around our supplied cups and underwires, and what compatibility limits apply to the pattern and size range?
items.answer: Yes. We adapt the cup patterns and channelling to the B to E cups and underwires you supply. The wires need to fit an 8 to 10 mm channel, and you need to send every size you want graded.

items.question: How do you check that bikini tops and bottoms retain their fit when wet and during swimming, rather than only in a dry fitting?
items.answer: We fit every top and bottom dry, then fit it again after 30 minutes in water. While the model swims and moves, we check for strap slip, cup gaping and leg-line ride-up. Before pattern approval, we also check how the fabric and elastic stretch and recover when wet.

seo.description: Bust support options, plus-size ranges and factory-direct ordering from a one-piece swimsuit manufacturer making custom styles.

hero.heading: One-piece swimsuit manufacturer
lead: We cut each suit to your chosen leg line, from classic coverage to high-cut and sport.

cta.label: Request a quote for one-piece swimsuits

blocks.heading: One Piece Swimsuit Production in China
paragraphs: You set your one-piece swimsuit's neckline, back, cut-outs and leg line separately. For the neckline, choose scoop, square, plunge, halter, one-shoulder or high-neck. For the back, choose open, cross-back, racerback, zip-back or low-back. Cut-outs go at the side, front or underbust, and leg lines come in classic, high-cut, French-cut or sport. We make your one-piece swimsuits ourselves, in a single factory of our own in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Custom Swimsuit Styles and Design Details

items.heading: Base silhouettes
paragraphs: Pick from tank or maillot, plunge, cut-out monokini, asymmetric one-shoulder, long-sleeve or rash-guard, sport racerback, swimdress and skirted styles. Our in-house team works out the pattern, grading and fit from your tech pack, a picture or just an idea.

items.heading: Rear coverage
paragraphs: Every leg height works with full, moderate, cheeky, Brazilian or thong coverage. We shape the seat to the fit reference you've approved, and you check it on the sample.

items.heading: Pattern approval
paragraphs: We settle the silhouette and coverage first and add details after that. If you change the base silhouette later, every detail on its pattern lines has to be reworked and the fit check done again.

items.heading: Decorative details
paragraphs: We add ruching at the sides, front or centre back, self-fabric ties at the shoulders, neck or hips, wrap fronts and contrast panels.

items.heading: Colour-blocked panels
paragraphs: In a colour-blocked swimsuit, we join contrasting fabrics, match each panel to your Pantone references and check the sample for puckering or pulling.

items.heading: Fabric compatibility
paragraphs: We only combine panel fabrics when their stretch differs by no more than 15% in each direction and their weights are within 30 gsm of each other.

items.heading: Artwork ownership
paragraphs: Through our [Private Label service](/private-label/), prints developed from your artwork stay your intellectual property under our NDA, and we never sell them to another client.

items.heading: Matching sets
paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), polyester, rayon and cotton each render Pantone colours differently, so you approve every base side by side before bulk. We scale the artwork from toddler sizes up to 5XL and sample the sets together.

blocks.heading: Wholesale Swimsuit Orders and Delivery

items.heading: Order quantities
paragraphs: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We agree first-trial quantities case by case, and production requirements limit how flexible we can be.

items.heading: Samples and fees
paragraphs: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design and covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Production and payment
paragraphs: Once you approve the sample and pay a 50% deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, with order size and season setting where it falls. You pay the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Shipping terms
paragraphs: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Direct factory orders
paragraphs: [Our company](/about-us/) owns its factory, which has been running since 2011, and controls production, export, quality, cost and delivery directly for business buyers worldwide. You order through our website and team, never through an online shop or third-party marketplace.

items.heading: Sample delivery
paragraphs: [Sample courier delivery](/sampling/) to send your sample costs USD 50, which you pay separately from the sample fee.

items.heading: Separate approvals
paragraphs: [Our process](/our-process/) starts with an agreed quote before sampling, then moves through technical development, sourcing and sample revisions. Design approval is separate from your approval of bulk quantity, size split, quality checkpoints, packing and shipping, all of which happens before production.

items.heading: Contact and response
paragraphs: [Contact our English-speaking team](/contact-us/) by phone or video call at every stage. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

blocks.heading: Swimsuit Fabrics, Weights and Performance
rows: Unless you specify something else, we use 80/20 nylon spandex, and recycled versions are available. You can specify UV protection, chlorine resistance and shape retention.

A 180–200 gsm nylon spandex shell with swim lining makes a light, soft, opaque suit. At around 160 gsm the fabric feels softer but shows through more in pale colours. At 200 gsm and above it feels firmer and gives more coverage and hold.
Shell fabrics run from 180 to 220 gsm, linings from 100 to 130 gsm, and shaping power mesh from 150 to 180 gsm.

A 200–220 gsm shell is paired with a second shell or a power-mesh lining, for a combined build of about 350 to 440 gsm. This heavier double-layer construction gives up lightness, softness and quick drying in return for hold and smoothing.

Our 80/20 nylon spandex stretches 130–170% lengthwise and 170–220% crosswise. It recovers at least 90% in both directions after repeated stretching, measured to EN 14704-1. If you need a tighter specification, we source fabric to match it and check your sample before bulk.
We use chlorine-resistant elastane tested to ISO 105-E03. We aim for Grade 4 colourfastness to chlorinated water and seawater.
Our [Hawaiian Fabrics service](/hawaiian-fabrics/) gives your collection soft, shape-recovering nylon/spandex, print-focused polyester/spandex and jacquard options.

Through [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/), existing jacquard, lurex and recycled swim fabrics keep the 50-piece minimum per style per colour. Custom jacquard or lurex starts at 1,000 metres per quality, confirmed at sampling. Swim colours come from printing or existing shades, not from custom dyeing.

blocks.heading: OEM Swimsuit Construction and Finishing

items.heading: Edges and seams
paragraphs: Your price point decides whether we finish the edges with fold-over elastic or with picot elastic turned and coverstitched. Side seams are sewn flatlock, and so are the joins between colour-blocked panels.

items.heading: Cut-outs and legs
paragraphs: Every stress point around a cut-out gets a bar tack, and high-cut leg openings are finished with silicone-backed elastic to keep the construction secure.

items.heading: Metal hardware
paragraphs: For resort and fashion styles, we use lead-free zinc-alloy rings, sliders and clasps with gold or silver plating. You can have the plating nickel-free.

items.heading: Heavy-use hardware
paragraphs: For training and heavy pool use, we fit acetal plastic rings and sliders, which don't corrode. You give up the polished gold or silver look, but long exposure to chlorine is the hardest test plated metal faces.

items.heading: Crotch gusset
paragraphs: The gusset is a double layer of soft swim lining, overlocked into the front and back body seams and coverstitched flat against the skin. It covers the full crotch, and its side edges are enclosed in the leg elastic.

items.heading: Pattern cutting
paragraphs: With our [Cut & Sew service](/cut-sew/), we work from custom patterns and cut every panel of your swimsuit precisely.

items.heading: Colour coordination
paragraphs: Our [Customisation service](/customization/) matches print and thread colours to your Pantone references, so the finishing is coordinated across the whole swimsuit.

items.heading: Retail packaging
paragraphs: Our [Packaging service](/packaging/) adds hygienic liners, hygiene stickers with your logo and wording, and individual self-seal or heat-sealed polybags closed with branded stickers, ready for hanging or shelf display in retail.

blocks.heading: Bust Support, Fit and Extended Sizing
rows: Decide on support first, then straps and sizing. Removable cups sit in sewn-in pockets, power-mesh shelves support the bust, and cup-sized styles use underwire channels with the strap placement adjusted to match. Deep-V styles get internal power-mesh support.

Removable cups and shelf linings work with adjustable, convertible or removable straps. Convertible straps have 4 attachment points, so they can be worn straight, crossed or as a halter. Underwire cup-sized styles need fixed-anchor adjustable straps with up to 8 cm of adjustment, so you trade convertible and removable styling for structured lift.
We produce XS to 3XL, plus sizes 1X to 5X, and band-and-cup ranges from a 30 to a 40 band in A to G cups. You can choose any size run within these ranges.
We re-grade blocks, add torso length or move the leg line to match your fit. Plus-size and extended-cup ranges get adjusted strap placement, wider back bands and reinforced underbust elastic.

Your chart lists bust, waist, hip and torso girth for every size. It keeps body measurements separate from finished-garment measurements, which are taken flat and unstretched. We also grade to your fit model or size standard.

We cut neckline elastic to 85–90% of the edge length and put power mesh behind plunge and deep-scoop fronts so they don't gape when wet. On classic and sport styles, the back-leg elastic is set firmer so it doesn't ride up, and we check both in a wet movement sample test.
You can choose removable round or triangle moulded foam cups, push-up cups, thin soft cups or sewn-in fixed padding. We scale the cups to each size in your run.

blocks.heading: Swimsuit Builds for Different Uses and Care
paragraphs: We define each style's end use before we settle its build and care wording, because chlorine, sun and sunscreen are what wear a suit out.

items.heading: Training and pool
paragraphs: For lap swimming and club training, we build sport-cut and racerback suits in chlorine-resistant four-way-stretch fabric, with compression panels for an ergonomic fit.

items.heading: Resort and beach
paragraphs: For collections meant for resort and beach wear, we make fashion one-pieces with plunge necklines, cut-outs and shaping layers.

items.heading: Surf and watersports
paragraphs: For surf and water sports, we use a high-neck or long-sleeve build with a zip back and UV-protective fabric.

items.heading: Care instructions
paragraphs: Rinse in cool fresh water after every wear, then hand wash cold or machine wash cold on a gentle cycle. Don't bleach, tumble dry or iron, and dry flat in the shade. Rinse sunscreen off promptly, because it stains the fabric and weakens the elastic.

items.heading: Label approval
paragraphs: Our [Custom Labels & Hang Tags service](/custom-labels-hang-tags/) prepares the fibre content, origin, wash-tested care wording and any required RN or CA numbers, all based on the actual materials and the rules of your destination. We send you the artwork to approve and check the labels on every private-label order.

blocks.heading: Further Information on Quality Checks and Aftercare

items.heading: Certification scope
items.text: Our [quality credentials](/quality-control/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GOTS for organic cotton styles, BCI cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 quality management and WRAP social compliance.

items.heading: Inspection stages
items.text: Our [quality checks](/quality-control/) run from incoming fabric through cutting and sewing to random checks and a full final inspection. You're welcome to bring in independent SGS or BV inspectors before shipment.

items.heading: Aftercare response
items.text: Under our [aftercare terms](/terms-and-conditions/), you report any quality problem within 7 days with photos or videos. We give you a solution within 24 hours: repair, remake, replacement, discount or credit.

blocks.heading: Design Choices That Shape Swimsuit Pricing

items.heading: Support costs
items.text: Removable cups, power-mesh shelf linings, underwire channels and full double-layer lining all raise the production cost of your one-piece.

items.heading: Trim costs
items.text: Custom or plated rings and sliders, nickel-free plating, and branded trims and labels add further cost across the whole style.

items.heading: Itemised decisions
items.text: We price each support and trim option separately from your design and fabric. You keep the additions your customers notice and see exactly how each one changes the total.

items.heading: Print surcharge
items.text: For all-over or placement artwork, our [Custom Printing service](/custom-printing/) uses sublimation on polyester and digital pigment printing on nylon, with a small surcharge for digital printing.

items.heading: Bulk quotation
items.text: [Request an itemised quote](/request-a-quote/) with no obligation. We review your design, fabric, quantity, construction, branding, packaging, size ratio and lead time, then send your bulk price within 24 hours.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Is the suit lined, and will light colours stay opaque when wet?
items.answer: We offer full or front-only lining in nude, white or black. For white and pale shades, we use full lining matched to the shell. A double layer or a heavier shell stops the suit turning see-through when wet, and we check this on your wet sample before bulk. Front-only lining works for darker shades or busier prints. You give up rear opacity and some hold, and in return the suit is lighter and dries faster.

items.question: Will the elastic hold its stretch after repeated chlorine and sunscreen exposure?
items.answer: When it's rinsed in fresh water after each wear, our chlorine-resistant fold-over or picot elastic keeps its stretch and grip far longer than standard elastic. It's enclosed in fabric at every leg opening and edge channel, which cuts down its direct exposure to pool water, salt water and sunscreen.

items.question: How do you stop a one-piece from turning see-through, sagging or losing elastic grip after wear?
items.answer: To stop sagging and loss of grip, we use 80/20 nylon spandex with at least 90% recovery, power mesh in the shaping zones and chlorine-resistant elastic on the edges. High-cut legs get silicone-backed elastic, and the stress points around cut-outs get bar tacks so the seams don't open.

items.question: Can you manufacture fully reversible one-pieces with clean finishing on both wearable sides?
items.answer: Yes. We develop the pattern in-house with two finished faces that can both be worn, and we enclose every seam and all the elastic between the layers, so no stitching or raw edges show. You can pair two prints, a print with a solid, or two solids.

items.question: Can you make bonded or concealed-seam one-pieces instead of the listed elastic-edge and flatlock construction?
items.answer: Yes. We heat-bond the seam allowances with tape instead of stitching them, which gives you smooth seams and edges with no stitches. Bonded construction suits minimal styles in plain or lightly printed fabric. We also turn seams inside a fully lined body to hide them.

items.question: What UPF ratings can you supply for these one-piece fabrics, and under which applicable standards are those ratings supported?
items.answer: We supply fabrics rated from UPF 30 up to UPF 50+. We only state a rating when the fabric has a laboratory report to AS/NZS 4399 or EN 13758-1 that backs it up, and we send that report with your order.

Our [fabric choices](/hawaiian-fabrics/) include natural, regenerated and synthetic fibres, with blends such as 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which fabric do you recommend for boys' shirts that get washed a lot: rayon, cotton poplin or a blend?
items.answer: For everyday boys’ shirts that go through the washing machine often, we recommend 110–130 gsm cotton poplin or a 65% polyester 35% cotton blend. Both hold their shape and print better than rayon. Rayon fibres swell and lose strength when they're wet, so frequent machine washing makes rayon shirts shrink, twist and lose their print brightness faster. If you choose poplin or poly-cotton, you give up rayon’s soft, fluid drape and cool feel. For dress-up styles that get gentle care, 100–120 gsm rayon is the right choice.

items.question: Can you make short and long sleeves, and camp collars as well as band collars?
items.answer: Yes. We make short and long sleeves, with buttoned cuffs or roll-up sleeve tabs, and we make camp, spread, notch and band collars. We adjust the band-collar height and shape to suit your design, and we carry your print across collars, sleeves and cuffs. You can mix sleeve lengths in one order as long as each style reaches 50 pieces in each colour.

items.question: Do you offer slim and regular fits, and how do you grade boys' sizes from toddler to teen?
items.answer: Yes. We offer regular and slim fits, plus a relaxed boxy fit. Our in-house design team develops each fit and grades it to your size specification, from toddler through to youth sizes. Regular fits give about 10–12 cm of ease at the chest, and slim fits give about 6–8 cm.

items.question: Can you line up the print across the front placket and the chest pocket on boys' shirts?
items.answer: Yes. We print all-over patterns on the fabric roll before cutting, so the repeat runs continuously and matches across the collar, front placket, chest pocket and hem. For engineered or placement designs, we cut the panels first, print each one (for example, by sublimation transfer on polyester) and then sew them together, so the motif lands in the same spot on every shirt.

items.question: Which baby styles can you make in Hawaiian prints, like bodysuits, rompers, bibs or headbands?
items.answer: We make Hawaiian-print bodysuits, rompers, bibs, headbands, baby aloha shirts, shorts, shirt-and-shorts sets, sundresses, bloomers and bucket hats. Soft cotton or cotton-spandex suits everyday bodysuits, rompers and bibs because it holds its shape and keeps the print clear through repeated washing. Modal or Tencel gives sundresses and matching sets for hot climates a cooler, silkier drape and a smoother feel on sensitive skin. Compared with cotton, you give up lower cost and sturdier shape after many washes to get that softer, cooler feel.

items.question: Can you use organic or GOTS-certified cotton and skin-safe, water-based inks for baby pieces?
items.answer: Yes. We make GOTS-certified organic cotton styles and print baby pieces with soft-hand, water-based inks that are free of PVC and phthalates. The fabrics and trims we test for baby pieces carry OEKO-TEX Standard 100.

items.question: Are your snaps nickel-free, and how do you test that they stay on?
items.answer: Yes, nickel-free plating is standard on the snaps for our baby Hawaiian clothing. We set the snaps on reinforced backing and pull-test every batch at 90 N for 10 seconds. The snaps have to stay attached without damage. Every US baby order also needs CPSIA tests at a CPSC-accepted lab, and we sew nothing detachable onto newborn to 24-month pieces.

items.question: Which baby sizes do you cover, from newborn to 24 months, and can you add extras like fold-over mitten cuffs?
items.answer:
We cover newborn, 0–3, 3–6, 6–12, 12–18 and 18–24 months, and you can add fold-over mitten cuffs at sampling. Our in-house team grades each style from your size chart or from our baby base pattern. At sampling you can also choose fold-over footies, envelope shoulders and snap-crotch openings.

Which safety rules apply to baby pieces sold in the US and the EU?

US baby pieces need the same CPSIA tests and [Children's Product Certificate](/kids-hawaiian-clothing-manufacturer/) as the rest of our kids' clothing, booked at the laboratory's rate. For the EU, cords and ties follow EN 14682, and on newborn to 24-month pieces we leave out detachable small parts.

How do you set care labels and pack baby pieces?

We wash-test your bulk fabric and print, then write the care label from those results, so the instructions match how each piece behaves in the wash. Every piece is folded and sealed in its own poly bag with your insert card, and our [Packaging](/packaging/) service adds barcodes or branded bags.

paragraphs: Pick sizes by body height, not age. Children of the same age vary in height, so our height-based bands give you a more reliable fit.

items.heading: Toddler height bands

items.heading: Kids' pricing

items.heading: Size allocation

items.heading: Collar options

items.heading: Sleeve lengths
paragraphs: You can choose short, 3/4 or long sleeves. Going with long sleeves doesn't change your print, fit or fabric weight.

items.heading: Gentle neckline finishes
paragraphs: At sampling, you choose soft cotton seam tape, gentle self-fabric or jersey binding, or a seam fully enclosed inside the collar, so no raw edges touch the neck.

items.heading: Collar structure
paragraphs: With [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/), you choose at sampling between standard lightweight fusible interlining for crisp cotton and soft sewn-in or no interlining for drapey rayon. Each option shapes camp collars and plackets without making them stiff.

blocks.heading: Fabric Choices & Care for Kids' Tops
rows: Our 100% cotton poplin at 110 to 130 GSM gives younger children a light, breathable top.
Our 100% rayon (viscose) at 100 to 120 GSM gives younger children a softer drape and a cooler feel than poplin, but it handles hot machine washing and drying less well.
You can choose our 55% linen 45% cotton blend at 140 to 160 GSM.
You can choose our 65% polyester 35% cotton blend at 120 to 140 GSM.
Our 95% cotton 5% spandex at 160 to 180 GSM adds movement for active children who run and climb.
Organic cotton comes in the same cotton weights, and we develop modal, Tencel and other blends at 100 to 200 GSM.

Through our [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) service, you can choose from 580+ fabric bases across natural, performance and sustainable options, with OEKO-TEX Standard 100 on the tested fabrics, including 80% nylon 20% spandex.

blocks.heading: Kids' Top Safety Standards & Market Testing
rows: Tell us your markets at the start of development, so we choose compliant trims and construction before sampling. If you change buttons, snaps or neck construction after approval, it adds time and a risk of re-testing.

We lockstitch every button with a thread-wrapped shank and run pull and tear-strength checks on all functional trims. For babies and toddlers, you can choose snaps or sewn buttons with reinforced backing to secure small parts.
Snaps make dressing babies and toddlers quicker, but they replace the classic look of real aloha-shirt buttons.
We pull each batch of buttons and snaps at 90 N for 10 seconds during sewing and again at final inspection; any detachment or damage counts as a failure.
Our metal buttons and snaps meet the EU REACH limit of 0.5 µg/cm²/week. Nickel-free plating is standard on baby styles, and you can request it for other ranges.

During development, we check your US orders against CPSIA lead and phthalate limits, 16 CFR Part 1501 small-parts rules and 16 CFR Part 1610 flammability requirements, and your EU orders against EN 14682 cord and drawstring rules.

We confirm certificate coverage for every trim before you order. A CPSC-accepted laboratory carries out US lead, phthalate and flammability testing, and we prepare supporting paperwork based on your order so you can issue your Children's Product Certificate, along with permanent tracking labels worded the way you specify.

We book destination-specific tests with accredited third-party laboratories. US children's tests are required and always quoted; other markets' tests follow your approval, all paid in advance at the lab's rate per test item, with each report sent to you.

Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) runs from incoming fabric through full final inspection, and SGS or BV inspectors are welcome. We hold chest, length and waist within ±1 cm and small points within ±0.5 cm, keep residual shrinkage of preshrunk fabric within 3% in both directions after three home washes, and reach washing colourfastness of Grade 4 or above—including high-twist chiffon—with rubbing and light fastness at Grade 3–4 or above.

items.question: Do toddler and older-child sizes use different proportions and movement allowances, or are all children's sizes graded from one base fit?

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which lightweight or pale-coloured fabrics provide adequate coverage without lining, and what lining options do you offer for sheer choices?
items.answer: For most prints, cotton poplin from 110 gsm and rayon challis from 120 gsm give enough coverage without a lining. White and pastel grounds, and lawn or voile under 90 gsm, need lining. For those sheer choices, we line the bodice or the whole dress with 100% cotton batiste at 60–70 gsm or a soft polyester lining at 70–80 gsm, and you pick a matching or white shade at sampling. Before we confirm the lining, we check a sewn sample in your actual print and ground colour against daylight and again after washing. Show-through depends on the specific print, colour and seams, so a flat swatch on its own doesn't tell you how well the finished dress covers.

items.question: How do your cotton and performance fabrics differ in skirt drape and bulk at gathered waist seams?
items.answer: Rayon challis and cotton lawn drape softly and gather into a flat, low-bulk waist seam, which suits full and tiered skirts. Cotton poplin holds a crisper A-line shape and adds bulk at the gathers. Polyester and cotton-spandex knits hang smoothly with less volume. With fabrics heavier than 150 gsm, we bring the gather ratio down to about 1.5:1 and overlock the waist seam so it lies flat against the body. Before we confirm gather fullness, we look at the sewn sample in your actual print and ground colour against daylight and after a wash, because the waist seam’s bulk shows in the made-up dress, not just in a flat swatch.

items.question: How do fabric width and one-way tropical print layouts affect material consumption and cost for full-skirted children's dresses?
items.answer: Our 145–150 cm fabric width fits gathered or circle skirt panels for sizes up to 8 across the width. A one-way tropical print, though, takes 5–10% more fabric than a two-way layout, because we can't turn the pieces head-to-tail. Large repeats or pattern matching use 10–15% more fabric, and we build that extra consumption into your unit price.

items.question: Do any performance fabrics offered for these dresses have a verified UPF rating, and which fabric and colour combinations does that rating cover?
items.answer: We offer a UPF rating such as UPF 50+ on quick-dry polyester-spandex woven and stretch poplin only when a laboratory report to AS/NZS 4399 or EN 13758-1 backs it up, and we send that report with your order. The rating covers only the fabric quality and colour named in that report, not every fabric or shade in the range. Each colourway you want to label with UPF is tested separately before production.

items.question: Can you combine different fabrics for the bodice and skirt, and which combinations are unsuitable because of stretch, weight or wash behaviour?
items.answer: Yes, we combine fabrics in one dress, for example a woven cotton poplin bodice with a knit or rayon challis skirt, or a 95% cotton 5% spandex stretch bodice with a cotton gauze skirt. A heavy knit skirt on a lightweight voile or gauze bodice drags the waist seam, so that pairing is unsuitable, and joining a high-stretch knit to rigid poplin needs a stabilised seam. At sampling, we wash-test every combination to check that the bodice and skirt shrink and recover evenly. Before we confirm the pairing, we look at the sewn dress in your actual print and ground colour against daylight and after washing, because uneven shrinkage between the two parts only shows once the garment is made up and washed.

blocks.heading: Private Label Uniform Shirts With Your Prints and Logos
paragraphs: Your logo stays readable only when it contrasts with what's directly around it, and dense, multicoloured prints take that contrast away faster than thread colour can bring it back.

items.heading: Logos against tropical prints
paragraphs: On dense prints, go for solid patches, sublimated 10 x 10 cm plain zones on the chest or back, or contrast-thread chest embroidery. Pantone-matched logos on calmer patterns lose readability at a distance.

blocks.heading: Collar and Placket Interlining
paragraphs: We match the interlining to your shirt fabric, so the collar and placket hold the shape they're meant to have without the shirt becoming stiffer than it needs to be.
rows: Your collar and placket get lightweight fusible interlining, heat-bonded at 130–150°C so it stays fully attached.

Before bulk cutting, we test-fuse a swatch of your actual printed fabric and match the interlining weight to that shell fabric. We run the test on the material going into your order, not on a substitute fabric.
On light rayon or cotton, interlining that's too heavy shows through or stiffens the fabric. Adding weight doesn't make a better collar or placket.
Without enough support, the collar curls and the placket goes wavy. We pick the weight to suit the fabric instead of using the lightest option no matter how the shirt is built.
With our standard lightweight fusible construction, the collar keeps its shape through at least 30 home washes at 40°C, with no bubbling, peeling or stiffening.

blocks.heading: Uniform Shirt Fabrics and Performance Options
paragraphs: We choose fabric for where your staff work and how their shirts get washed, rather than judging the uniform only by how it looks on day one.
rows: Rayon or cotton suits front-of-house work, where comfort and drape matter. Your choice has to account for how the shirt is laundered as well as how it hangs on the wearer.

Polyester or cotton-poly blends suit frequent heavy washing. Rayon gives you a softer, more classic Hawaiian drape than a cotton-poly blend, but it gives up some wrinkle resistance and toughness in the wash.
For active or outdoor staff, we make shirts in moisture-wicking material. That way, performance is built into your fabric choice instead of being assumed from the shirt's cut or print.

Through [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/), you can choose cotton poplin at 110–140 gsm, rayon at 100–130 gsm, polyester microfibre at 100–130 gsm, silk at 60–90 gsm, cotton-polyester at 120–150 gsm and moisture-wicking polyester at 110–140 gsm. For all-day wear in hot weather, rayon and moisture-wicking polyester are the light, breathable, quick-drying options.

With our [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/) service, we get moisture-wicking, UV-protective, anti-odour and sustainable fabrics from textile suppliers and certified mills we've already found to be reliable.

Fabric that can't stand up to the job's daily wear and laundering fades, wrinkles or loses its shape before the uniform is due for replacement. Choosing for the work and the wash puts service life ahead of first-day looks.

blocks.heading: Reinforced Seams and Finishing for Daily Wear
paragraphs: We reinforce pocket corners, pocket openings and buttons, because that's where staff movement and handling put the most strain. Both top corners of each patch pocket are bar-tacked or reinforced with small stitched triangles, and we double-turn and topstitch the opening so it doesn't fray. Buttons are lock-stitched with 8 to 12 passes through each hole and pull-tested to 90 N during in-line checks.

Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) service verifies that uniform fabrics keep residual shrinkage within 3% in length and width after three home washes, and you're welcome to bring in SGS or BV inspectors before shipment.

With [Garment Dyeing](/garment-dyeing/), custom-dyed cotton and rayon reach Grade 4 or above for washing colourfastness and Grade 3–4 or above for rubbing and light. Our [Embroidery](/embroidery/) logos stand up to repeated washing and hard wear without fraying.

blocks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Will the uniform prints and colours hold up to daily commercial laundering without fading?
items.answer: Yes. For uniforms that go through commercial laundry every day, we suggest a polyester-blend or reactive-dyed cotton base, and we wash-test your sample fabric and print for 20 cycles at 60°C before you approve bulk. Industrial laundries use strong alkaline detergents, bleach and high-heat tunnel drying, and these fade and shrink fabric much faster than washing at home. If keeping colour and shape matters most, go for a polyester blend, because it stands up to fading and shrinking better. The trade-off is that you lose some of cotton's breathability, moisture absorption and soft hand, and staff notice that on long shifts in warm kitchens or workshops. If comfort in the heat matters more, go for reactive-dyed cotton. It breathes better, but it holds up less well to industrial laundry than a polyester blend.

items.question: Do you offer women's cuts and extended sizes so the whole team can wear the same uniform?
items.answer: Yes. Every uniform style comes in a men's cut, a unisex cut or a women's fitted cut with shaped side seams, a narrower shoulder and a shorter sleeve. All three share the same fabric, print and placement, so the whole team matches, and we sample the women's and men's cuts side by side before bulk.

items.question: If we hire new staff next year, can you remake the same print in the same colour for a small top-up order?
items.answer: Yes. Reorders of approved styles skip sampling and are made in 35 to 40 days after deposit, with the same minimum of 50 pieces per style in each colour. For every reorder, we reprint the fabric from your archived print files and colour profiles and match it to your original approved sample within ΔE ≤ 2.0.

items.question: Can you embroider or print our logo and staff names on the uniform shirts?
items.answer: Yes. Through our Custom Printing service, we put your logo on your aloha shirts by screen printing in up to 12 colours, by DTF transfer with unlimited colours and a soft hand feel, or by embroidery.

blocks.heading: Accessories Made in China
paragraphs: We make textile resort accessories printed to match your aloha shirt line: tote bags, bucket hats, caps, scarves, bandanas, scrunchies and smaller add-ons. We make them ourselves, alongside the shirts they match, in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Custom Accessories for Your Range
rows: We cut and sew your totes from cotton canvas or linen, with double-stitched side seams and bar-tacked joins where the handles meet the bag. You can choose flat shoulder-strap shoppers or gusseted beach totes with webbing or self-fabric handles. Large gusseted totes suit beach and holiday ranges.

You can choose 5-panel or 6-panel caps, soft strap-back dad caps, structured snapbacks with flat or curved brims, or bucket hats with short or wide brims. We build them with multi-row stitched brims, taped inner seams and fused front panels. Dad caps and bucket hats suit relaxed resort lines, and structured snapbacks suit collections that lean towards streetwear.
We finish rayon, silk, cotton or polyester with narrow rolled hems on every edge. Squares work as neck and head wear. Long rectangles work as wraps and suit beach and holiday ranges.

For scrunchies, we close fabric tubes over covered elastic. We also make zip pouches, drawstring bags, pocket squares, hair bows and eye masks, and we develop other fabric accessories linked to your apparel range or brand from your brief, sketch or reference picture.

Our [factory-owning business](/about-us/) has operated since 2011 and controls production and export directly for B2B buyers worldwide. You agree orders with our team, not through an online shop or third-party marketplace.

Our [fabric range](/hawaiian-fabrics/) covers cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool, plus blends including 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton.
Through [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/), you can pick from our fabric library or have a custom material developed.

blocks.heading: Private Label Accessories and Branding

items.heading: Branding by price
paragraphs: On lower-priced accessories, we keep branding to woven labels or branded packaging. Full prints and patches suit items whose retail prices cover the extra cost.

items.heading: Printing choices
paragraphs: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-printing/) gives you screen printing in up to 12 colours, soft-feel DTF in unlimited colours, embroidery, heat transfer, silicone printing and sewn-on labels. On aloha shirt blanks, you can have screen printing, DTF or embroidery.

items.heading: Embroidery and patches
paragraphs: Our [Embroidery service](/embroidery/) covers detailed shirt embroidery prepared by designers, plus patches and labels. Embroidered logos hold up to repeated washing and hard wear without fraying.

items.heading: Private label collections
paragraphs: With our [Private Label service](/private-label/), your brand is the only one on your aloha shirt collections. We coordinate approved labels, trims, tags and retail-ready packaging to your specifications.

items.heading: Buttons and hardware
paragraphs: Our [Custom Buttons service](/custom-buttons/) develops buttons and hardware branded with your logo. We quote tooling separately before you approve it, and we keep the moulds for 3 years so identical reorders reuse them.

items.heading: Care label wording
paragraphs: Our [care and content labels](/custom-labels-hang-tags/) are based on wash tests of the fabric and print and on destination rules, including US, EU and Australian requirements. You approve the wording before production, and we run QC checks on every private-label order.

blocks.heading: Matching Accessory Prints and Colours

items.heading: Artwork scale
paragraphs: We rescale your shirt motif for the smaller surfaces of hats, scarves and scrunchies so the design reads clearly on each finished accessory.

items.heading: Printing before sewing
paragraphs: We print accessory fabric flat, then cut and sew it into shape, so the finished construction determines where motifs meet.

items.heading: Visible seam alignment
paragraphs: We line motifs up at the seams people see first, including the front of a hat crown and the joins where a tote's front meets its sides and base.

items.heading: Pattern continuity limits
paragraphs: A pattern cannot run unbroken from brim to crown, across cap backs and top buttons, or along tote gussets and bottom corners. We mark placement on your sample for you to approve before bulk.

items.heading: Matching across fabrics

columns: What it means for your order

items.question: My shirts are made by another factory. Can I order matching accessories from you alone?
items.answer: Yes. We take accessory-only orders as long as the accessories connect to your apparel range or brand, even if another factory makes your shirts.

items.question: Which choices change the price of an accessory the most?
items.answer: Item type and construction have the biggest effect on price. A structured 6-panel cap with buckram and an adjustable strap costs more than a flat hemmed bandana. Fabric is next: silk or linen costs more than polyester or cotton. Print method and coverage come after that, and all-over multi-colour printing costs more than a single placed logo. Moving up from branded packaging to woven labels, patches and custom hang tags adds to the unit cost. When we look for ways to cut cost, we go through these choices in order and leave branding until last.

items.question: Does your textile-only scope allow zippers, snaps, buckles and adjustment hardware within bags and hats?
items.answer: Yes. We fit colour-matched zippers, snaps, buckles, eyelets and cord locks into textile bags and hats, including zip-top totes, snapback closures and adjustable buckle straps.

items.question: What sizes do your totes, scarves, bandanas and hats come in, and can I set my own dimensions?
items.answer: Our standard totes are 38 x 42 cm with a 10 cm gusset. Scarves are 90 x 90 cm or 70 x 180 cm, and bandanas are 55 x 55 cm. Scrunchies come in fabric widths of 1 cm, 3.5 cm and 6 cm. Bucket hats come in S/M (56 cm) and L/XL (59 cm), and adjustable caps fit 56 to 60 cm. You can set your own dimensions for any item, including custom hat head sizes from 52 to 62 cm, and we confirm the final size on your sample.

items.question: Can you use the same fabric batch as my shirts for the accessories, and which accessory constructions would require reinforcement or a different fabric?

blocks.heading: Beach Towels Made in China
paragraphs: We make your beach towels in cotton, microfibre, velour or recycled PET (RPET), including RPET blends, so you can choose the material that suits your programme. Our partner towel mill weaves the terry, and we print, finish and check your towels in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Materials for Custom Beach Towels
columns: What it means for your towels
rows: With pile on both sides, the towel is absorbent and soft. The trade-off is that the looped surface prints less smoothly.

Our partner towel mill shears one terry face smooth and leaves loops on the back. Your print comes out sharper, but the sheared side is less absorbent and less soft than full loop terry. You can have it in 100% cotton or a 65% polyester 35% cotton blend.
Fine split yarn in 80% polyester and 20% polyamide is knitted into flat suede or waffle structures. That gives you towels that are light, dry quickly and pack down easily.
You can choose 100% recycled polyester or a 50% RPET and 50% cotton blend. The recycled yarn makes up either the knitted microfibre base or the blend's pile, with cotton loops on the other side.

Our [factory-owned business](/about-us/) has been running since 2011. It handles both production and export, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control. Orders are agreed only through our team, never through online shops or third-party marketplaces.
Through our [Fabric Sourcing service](/fabric-sourcing/), you can pick from our fabric library or have a custom material developed.

blocks.heading: Private Label Beach Towels With Your Logo

items.heading: Smooth-face printing
paragraphs: On smooth microfibre and velour faces we use sublimation or fine screen printing. Text stays sharp down to 6 pt and lines down to 0.3 mm, and screen-printed designs keep their bold look through repeated washing.

items.heading: Loop-terry artwork
paragraphs: Loops break up fine detail, so your screen prints need bold shapes, text of at least 12 pt and lines of at least 1 mm. Jacquard lettering has to be at least 10 mm high.

items.heading: Reverse-side limits
paragraphs: Double-sided microfibre and RPET towels can carry a different design on each side. Cotton and velour backs stay plain terry and take only a woven label or a screen-printed logo of up to 2 colours, no larger than 30 x 30 cm.

items.heading: Woven and stitched branding
paragraphs: With jacquard and embroidery, your branding becomes part of the towel and won't fade or crack. Neither one can reproduce full-colour photographic artwork. We also offer woven or rubber patches and woven or printed labels at the hems or corners.

items.heading: Retail and resort channels
paragraphs: We make printed towels for your shop, summer promotions or outdoor lifestyle brand, and heavier cotton terry for hotel pools. You choose the material, GSM, size and branding for each channel.

items.heading: Custom digital printing
paragraphs: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-printing/) reproduces your all-over or placement artwork, gradients and shading included, for a small digital-printing surcharge. Polyester is printed by sublimation and nylon by digital pigment printing.

items.heading: Matching collection colours
paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), keep in mind that each fibre reproduces Pantone colours differently. We match every base to one reference and get your approval on a side-by-side sample. Then we scale the artwork across sizes from toddler up to 5XL.

items.heading: Private label options
paragraphs: Our [Private Label service](/private-label/) is open at every order quantity. It covers labels, hang tags, branded metal tags, logo application and silicone branding, and we make the woven labels and heat-transfer artwork in-house.

blocks.heading: OEM Beach Towels: Sizes and Finishes
rows: You can choose standard 70 x 140 cm, oversized 90 x 180 cm, kids 60 x 120 cm, round at 150 cm diameter, or a custom rectangle up to 100 x 200 cm.
Every size and shape comes in cotton terry at 350–500 GSM, velour at 380–450 GSM, microfibre at 200–300 GSM and RPET at 200–320 GSM.
A heavier GSM makes your towel plusher and more absorbent. It also dries more slowly, packs down less easily and costs more per piece.
We quote each material's GSM and absorbency against your end use. Before production, we confirm the weight, fibre type, size, print method and finish with you.

You can choose a dobby border, plain hem or colour-matched bound edge. Add-ons include hanging or corner loops, cotton knotted fringe, woven-label corner tabs, a drawstring pouch in matching fabric and an adjustable carry strap.
With our [Product Development service](/product-development/), your OEM or ODM towel can start from your design, a picture or an idea.

Our [Garment Dyeing service](/garment-dyeing/) custom-dyes cotton and rayon to Grade 4 or above for washing colourfastness and Grade 3–4 or above for rubbing and light. It uses reactive dyes, a fixing after-treatment and lab-dip fastness checks for dark brand colours before bulk approval.

items.question: Can you print my beach towels with the same artwork as my aloha shirts so they sell as a matching resort set?
items.answer: Yes. We print your beach towels with the same artwork as your aloha shirts, so you get a print-matched resort set.

items.question: What dimensional tolerance can you maintain against the ordered towel length and width?
items.answer: For adult, oversized and round towels, finished length and width stay within -2 to 2 cm of the dimensions you order. For kids’ towels, they stay within -1 to 1 cm. Your approved sample sets the target size, and at final inspection we check every towel against it.

items.question: Which towel specifications, such as material, GSM, size or print method, move the price most?
items.answer: Material, GSM and size move the unit price most, because heavier cotton terry, velour and larger towels use more yarn per piece. Print method and the number of screen colours come next, followed by jacquard or embroidery, edge finishes, fringe, loops, carry accessories and retail packaging.

items.question: What wash shrinkage should I expect from each towel construction, and can you supply preshrunk options?
items.answer: Microfibre and RPET towels shrink less than 2%. Every towel construction uses preshrunk fabric as standard, so there's no extra step for you.

items.question: Which towel specifications are suitable for repeated pool exposure and commercial laundering in hotel or resort programmes?
items.answer: For guest comfort and commercial laundering up to 60°C, we specify 100% cotton loop terry up to 500 GSM, yarn-dyed or solid dyed, with double-stitched dobby or bound edges and a hanging loop. Where towels face heavy chlorine and sun, 80% polyester 20% polyamide microfibre or RPET at 200 to 300 GSM holds its colour longer and dries faster, but you give up the heavy, plush feel of cotton. Commercial laundering, chlorine and strong sun wear towels out faster than retail use does, so your washing and exposure conditions decide the construction.

items.question: What colourfastness performance can your towel options meet under sunlight, seawater and chlorinated pool exposure?
items.answer: Against seawater and chlorinated pool water, our sublimated microfibre and RPET towels reach Grade 3–4 or above to ISO 105-E02 and ISO 105-E03. Cotton terry reaches Grade 3 or above.

items.heading: Flat wraps and pareos

blocks.heading: Bring Sarongs to Life with Prints, Batik and Dye Effects

items.heading: Screen printing
paragraphs: This suits bold, flat-colour designs of up to 3 or 4 colours, and every extra colour stage adds cost.

items.heading: Digital printing
paragraphs: Photographic and multi-colour artwork works well with digital printing, which gives you unlimited colours with no extra charge per colour. What you give up is batik's handmade, through-dyed character.

items.heading: Hand-painted batik
paragraphs: We use traditional wax-and-dye techniques to create modern patterns in vibrant colours. Hand-painted pieces and custom batik patterns start at 100 pieces per design.

items.heading: Batik cost drivers
paragraphs: Each extra colour means another round of waxing, dyeing and wax removal. Fine canting lines, detailed painted areas, deliberate crackle and matching both sides all add hand work, and that adds cost.

items.heading: Dye and wash effects
paragraphs: Tie-dye gives a handmade look that goes right through the cloth. Acid-wash, stone-wash and dip-and-wash treatments add colour and texture effects.

items.heading: Matching Family & Group Sets
paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), different fibres take Pantone colours differently, so you approve each base side by side. We scale the artwork and sample the sets together, from toddler sizes up to 5XL.

paragraphs: [Garment Dyeing](/garment-dyeing/) reaches Grade 4 or above for washing fastness and Grade 3–4 or above for rubbing and light fastness on cotton and rayon. We fix dark reactive colours and lab-dip test them before bulk approval.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Where does my brand label or logo go on a sarong, and how are sarongs folded and packed for retail?
items.answer: We sew your woven brand label and care label into one corner, print your logo into the design, or add a hang tag at the corner.

items.question: How wide can you make a sarong from one continuous fabric panel before a joining seam is necessary?
items.answer: We make sarongs from a single panel up to 150 cm wide, which is the full printable width for digital and sublimation prints. Beyond 150 cm, we join two panels with a French or flat-felled seam and line the print up across it.

items.question: Will my design show on the reverse side of the sarong, and can you make a double-sided sarong?
items.answer: How the reverse looks depends on the technique. For a fully double-sided sarong, we sew two printed layers together around the edge. Digital and sublimation prints on lightweight polyester show through lighter on the back, and screen prints on cotton and rayon show through faintly. Batik and tie-dye go right through the cloth, so both sides look nearly the same. Two-layer versions carry either matching designs or a different design on each side.

items.question: How long do batik or hand-painted sarongs take compared with printed sarongs?
items.answer: Batik and hand-painted samples take 15 to 20 days, compared with 10 to 15 days for printed samples, because we apply and dry every wax-and-dye stage by hand. Once you approve the sample and pay the deposit, printed bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Batik and hand-painted bulk takes 45 to 50 days, which is 10 days longer.

items.question: Will batik or tie-dye sarongs bleed or vary in colour from piece to piece, and how do you control this?
items.answer: Handmade batik and tie-dye vary slightly in shade and pattern. We fix the dyes, rinse each batch until the water runs clear and sort the pieces by dye lot against your approved sample. You approve an acceptable range of shade and pattern, not an exact repeat. When each retail delivery comes from a single dye lot, you avoid the stronger differences that show when pieces from different lots are displayed together.

items.question: Which of your sarong constructions suit beach cover-ups, and which suit spa wraps that need to stay secure during movement?
items.answer: For beach cover-ups, flat wraps and pareos in chiffon, voile or rayon are the right choice: they tie several ways, pack small and dry fast. For spa wear that has to stay secure while the wearer moves, we make cotton tubes with elastic top bands, or cotton wraps with built-in waistbands and hook-and-loop or button closures.

blocks.heading: Is This Service Right for Your Brand?
paragraphs: Yes. This service is built for first collections, print-led brands, capsule resort drops and low-MOQ test runs.

items.heading: First-time founders
paragraphs: If you have little factory experience, use the kit to plan your first resort line before sampling starts.

items.heading: Undecided collection direction
paragraphs: If you're still comparing categories or custom print directions, use the materials before you narrow down your first capsule range.

items.heading: Experienced brands
paragraphs: If you already have experience, you don't need the kit and can go straight to selecting styles and requesting a quote.

blocks.heading: Design Support for OEM and ODM Projects
paragraphs: We support both OEM and ODM projects, whether you start from your own design, a picture or an idea. For OEM work, we build to your specifications and tech pack. If you need development support, we prepare the tech pack, coordinate with the mills, run fit-sample rounds and prepare production markers for each size. Our mockup and written-approval process means no fabric is cut until you've signed off on the design.
