items.detail: We cut no fabric until every detail has been approved.

blocks.heading: From Your Brief to a Technical Specification
paragraphs: You can go with fully custom development, pick one of our ready designs that's already graded to international sizes, or combine the two. For a fast first launch, start from a ready design and add your own prints or details. You don't need a tech pack to get started or to receive a quote, though a complete pack does help. In our consultation, we turn whatever you start with into a specification that's ready for sampling. Send change notes, artwork, reference photos, measurements, your target fit, fabric ideas, quantities and packing requests wherever you have them. Our designers will also advise you on logo placement and all-over prints.

visuals.purpose: Explain how incomplete starting references become a detailed technical specification.
visuals.caption: A tech pack is not required to begin.

items.label: Share your starting material
items.detail: Send whatever you have, from a tech pack or reference shirt to sketches, pictures or simply an idea.

items.label: Review the brief
items.detail: We review your material before development begins and help fill in missing details before sampling.

items.label: Settle design and sizing
items.detail: In a design consultation, we help settle styles, sizes, colours and patterns, and work out the pattern and sizing with you.

items.label: Prepare the technical specification
items.detail: Our designers create technical sketches and a detailed specification covering every seam, the lining and all trims.

blocks.heading: Shirt References, Fabrics and Finishing Details
rows: You can start from our base block, your measurements or just a reference shirt. We examine its fit, collar, cuffs, pocket, stitching, fabric and finish, reverse-engineer the pattern, find the closest fabric available and prepare a sample plan. Then we make a counter sample for you to approve before we go any further.
If your construction, fit, fabric, artwork, trims, quantity, logo placement, labels or packaging aren't settled yet, we help you settle them before sampling.

Through our [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/) service, stock fabrics reach our factory within 3 to 5 days. Custom-dyed colours start at 300 metres per colour, and custom yarn-dyed stripes, checks and jacquards start at 1,000 metres per quality. We confirm the exact minimum at sampling, based on fabric type and dye method. Custom fabric adds 15 to 20 days before bulk, and that time includes one yarn-colour lab-dip round for yarn-dyed development.
Through [Garment Dyeing](/garment-dyeing/), we match your Pantone reference or physical swatch, get your lab-dip approval before bulk, and offer finishes and treatments.
Our [Embroidery](/embroidery/) service covers intricate decoration, patches and labels prepared by our designers. The embroidered logos hold up to repeated washing and hard wear without fraying.

Our [Private Label](/private-label/) service keeps your garments under your brand alone. It covers approved labels, branded trims and accessories, tags, and coordinated retail packaging, all packed to your specifications.

Through [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/), we develop logo buttons and hardware. We quote any tooling they need separately before you approve it, and we keep the moulds for 3 years so identical reorders reuse them.

blocks.heading: Exclusive Prints Ready for Production

steps.heading: Coordinate print development
steps.text: One team takes care of your fabrics, styles and prints, from your brand references through sampling and bulk. We engineer the repeats around the pattern pieces so plackets, pockets and every size line up.

steps.heading: Choose fabric effects
steps.text: [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) gives you more than 580 bases. Reverse-print shirts are printed on the inward-facing side. For these we recommend 100% cotton poplin at 110–130 gsm, and you approve a strike-off of both faces plus a sample of the outer effect before bulk.

steps.heading: Develop exclusive artwork
steps.text: With [Custom Print Design](/custom-print-design/), you get mock-ups within 48 hours, repeats within 5 to 7 business days and 3 revision rounds. Any extra rounds you approve cost more. New or adapted designs you pay for become exclusive to you, while unchanged originals from our library stay non-exclusive.

steps.heading: Protect your designs
steps.text: Under our [Terms and Conditions](/terms-and-conditions/), we sign an NDA that protects your designs and business information. Patterns developed from your artwork stay your intellectual property, and we never resell exclusive prints.

steps.heading: Coordinate matching sets
steps.text: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), different fibres render the same Pantone differently. So we match the bases to one reference for you to approve side by side before bulk, scale the artwork from toddler sizes to 5XL, and sample the sets together.

blocks.heading: Shirt Patterns, Fit and Size Grading
rows: Our pattern maker drafts and grades your pattern in CAD to your size specification, and checks the custom grading rules across the full run. We keep the graded master unchanged for your repeat orders.
Our standard range runs from XS to 3XL on US, EU and UK charts, and [extended sizes](/) are available.

Our [aloha shirt range](/) comes in four cuts: unisex/men’s, men’s slim, women’s and women’s vintage. Each one is graded over 47 measurement points, and the vintage cut has a mandarin collar and cap sleeves.

Through [Customisation](/customization/), you choose camp, spread or notch collars; straight or curved hems; vents or closed sides; no pocket, or one or two chest pockets, plain or matched; and coconut, shell, wood or resin buttons. We record every choice in your tech pack and sample it for your approval before bulk.

In [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/), directional or matched prints use 10–15% more fabric. That extra fabric is included in your unit price, and the quote reflects both the extra consumption and the slower single-ply matching. Repeats reach 64 cm for screen printing or the full 150 cm width for digital. If you supply DXF patterns, they go through two sample rounds and adjustments before full regrading. Lightweight rayon gets 1 cm overlocked or French seams, tested to ISO 13936-2 with no more than 6 mm of opening. Fine fabrics can also take flat-felled sides or 0.6 cm French seams. Contrast fabrics stay within about 40 GSM and a shrinkage difference of no more than 2%. They go through wash and colour-bleed tests and keep shrinkage to no more than 3% in either direction after three home washes. Where a print crosses both bases, you approve the shared Pantone side by side.

blocks.heading: Order Minimums, Lead Times and Delivery Terms

items.heading: Order minimum
items.text: Bulk orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so small and growing labels can start at an accessible quantity.

items.heading: Trial quantities
items.text: We agree your first trial run case by case, and how far the quantity can flex is limited by what production allows.

items.heading: Bulk timing
items.text: Production takes 35 to 40 days from sample approval and receipt of your deposit. Where it falls in that range depends on your order size and the season.

items.heading: Payment stages
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Delivery terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Ongoing collections
items.text: We support quarterly capsules and forecast reorders, reserve base cloth for your bestsellers and refine designs based on your sales feedback.

blocks.heading: In-House Development and Factory Oversight

items.heading: One development team
paragraphs: If you're a startup, we handle development, sampling, sourcing, branding and manufacturing together, so the work isn't split between suppliers.

items.heading: In-house design
paragraphs: Our designers handle pattern design, grading and fit development together, which cuts the rounds of design back-and-forth you have to manage.

items.heading: Factory resources
paragraphs: Our [factory team](/about-us/) has been running since 2011. It has more than 290 people, including over 110 production sewers and 62 sampling staff: 7 pattern makers, 20 sewists, 4 artists, 11 development coordinators and 20 assistants.

items.heading: Direct business orders
paragraphs: We serve business buyers worldwide only through this website and our team. We don't run an online shop or a third-party marketplace store. Production and export sit within one company that owns the factory.

items.heading: Quality oversight
paragraphs: Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) covers everything from incoming fabric to final inspection, and we welcome SGS/BV checks. It also includes OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GOTS for organic styles, BCI cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 quality management and WRAP social compliance.

blocks.heading: Sample Costs, Timing and Sign-Off

items.heading: Sample timing
items.text: A standard sample takes us 10 to 15 days from your brief or tech pack.

items.heading: Sample fee
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. This fee isn't refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Design fee
items.text: Each design costs USD 50 for its pattern or print, covering all colourways. This fee isn't refunded or credited against bulk either.

items.heading: Sampling options
items.text: [Sampling](/sampling/) offers seven types: fabric test, first, fit, photo, revised, pre-production (PP) and repeat. There are quick-response lines for fit, photo and PP samples, and courier delivery, which you pay for, costs USD 50 extra.

items.heading: Quote scope
items.text: [Your quote](/request-a-quote/) lists any applicable development charges separately. It excludes unlisted materials, trims, swatches, extra lab dips, decoration, setup, further revisions, extra samples, freight and testing, and any additional costs need your approval.

items.heading: Bulk sign-off
items.text: [Bulk Production](/bulk-production/) starts only once your specifications, quantities, sizing, materials, artwork, branding, packaging and schedule are confirmed. Your approved sample and pre-production record then govern how the order is made.

items.heading: Packaging proposal
items.text: Through [Packaging](/packaging/), we send you a proposal within 24 hours, with digital mockups and clear pricing.

items.heading: Label approval
items.text: With [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we take the content, origin and tested care instructions from the actual materials, add the required RN/CA numbers and follow your destination's rules. Your artwork approval and QC are both required.

blocks.heading: What to Send with Your Kit Request
paragraphs: When you request the starter kit, send us your category, target launch season, rough MOQ, design references and destination market. We review your brief first. Then we pick fabric swatches, print samples and trim options to suit your category and print direction, so you don't get a generic pack. After that, we confirm the next steps for your launch stage. [Contact our team](/contact-us/) and you'll hear back within one business day, with English-language support by phone or video call the whole way through.

blocks.heading: A recent order

items.text: An Australian resort wear label took its first capsule from moodboards to bulk with our in-house design and fit team. Sample rounds per style dropped from 4 to 2, and the time from brief to approved sample fell from 9 weeks to 4.

items.question: Is the starter kit sent to me as a physical pack or digitally, and how long after I request it will I receive it?
items.answer: You get both. We send the fabric swatches with print notes by DHL courier. The pack leaves us within 3 business days and takes 5 to 7 days to reach you. The base style catalogue, shipping guidance and launch guide come by email within 1 business day of your request.

items.question: At the end of development, do I receive the final print files and the tech pack for my styles?
items.answer: The full tech pack documentation we prepare is yours to keep. Once you've paid for a design, we send you its print files whenever you ask for them. We keep the pattern files for reorders, and if you want those files yourself, there's a charge for each pattern.

items.question: Can I commission aloha shirt development and receive the resulting technical specifications without committing to bulk production with you?
items.answer: Yes. We offer tech pack creation and sampling as standalone services. The tech pack documentation you get from them is yours to keep, and you have no obligation to place bulk production with us.

blocks.heading: What We Check in Fabric, Stitching, Prints and Fit

items.heading: Fabric condition
items.text: We check incoming fabric for stains, holes and defects, and we test its colourfastness before it goes into production.

items.heading: Shade grouping
items.text: Before cutting, we check shade variation and sort the fabric by dye lot, so every panel of a single shirt comes from the same shade group.

items.heading: Cutting alignment
items.text: While cutting, we check pattern alignment so the cut panels follow the intended arrangement.

items.heading: Sewing checks
items.text: On the sewing line, we check stitching, seam strength and thread tension, then inspect the garments once they've been trimmed.

items.heading: Production measurements
items.text: During production, we compare key measurements against your confirmed size chart to check the shirt's fit dimensions.

items.heading: Decoration quality
items.text: We inspect print and embroidery quality for peeling, loose threads and stitch density, and we check logo size, colour and placement.

items.heading: Labels and edges
items.text: We check that labels sit in the right position and that edges lie flat and clean, with no flipping or waviness.

blocks.heading: Inspection Standards, Records and Corrections
paragraphs: Before bulk production starts, we agree with you that your approved sample and acceptance level will be the inspection reference. Our in-house QC team checks the bulk against that sample. We check materials on arrival and production in-line, inspect every finished piece at final inspection, and only then draw the pre-shipment AQL sample. Inline print verification has to meet ΔE ≤ 2.0.

We keep a detailed measurement log for each run and send it to you with photos of the finished goods before dispatch. If a piece fails, we reprint or rework it before shipment. We don't ship it and give you a credit later. On [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/) orders, we reprint any substandard printed fabric.

blocks.heading: What We Inspect on Every Finished Shirt
paragraphs: Before packing, we inspect every shirt one by one against your approved spec sheet and sample. We check finished measurements, sizing, symmetry, construction and seam alignment. We also check for skipped stitches, thread trimming, fabric condition and stains, and we make sure the design is reproduced faithfully. We inspect pressing, finishing and overall appearance too, including balanced collars and cuffs, neat edge stitching, trims and buttons.

In our final audit, we check workmanship, measurements, labelling, folding and packaging, and we confirm that the shipment matches your order. Before dispatch, we send you photos of the finished goods, so you can raise any concerns while the goods are still with us. No batch leaves us unchecked.

blocks.heading: Certifications and Safety Testing for Aloha Shirts
paragraphs: Tested fabrics and trims carry OEKO-TEX Standard 100, organic cotton styles carry GOTS, cotton comes through Better Cotton (BCI), and our factory holds ISO 9001 and WRAP.

On [kids’ aloha shirts](/kids-hawaiian-top-manufacturer/), we test batches of buttons and snaps at 90 N for 10 seconds during sewing and again at final inspection, and we reject any piece that comes off or is damaged. Nickel release is limited to 0.5 µg/cm²/week under EU REACH, and we check the applicable CPSIA, 16 CFR Part 1501, 16 CFR Part 1610 and EN 14682 requirements. Destination testing is excluded unless your quote lists it. We arrange it only with your approval and advance payment, at the laboratory’s per-item rate.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What plus/minus tolerance do you accept on chest, body length, sleeve and collar measurements before a shirt fails inspection?
items.answer: On bulk woven aloha shirts, chest width, body length and sleeve length have to fall within ±1 cm of your approved size chart. The collar, cuffs and other small points have to fall within ±0.5 cm. We compare your shirts against your approved sample and reject any shirt outside these limits. We then rework or replace it before packing. Before shipment, we also inspect random samples against your approved sample, at AQL 2.5 for major defects and 4.0 for minor defects. A single critical defect rejects the whole lot. Critical defects are a broken-needle fragment, a sharp or loose metal part, or a missing care or content label. Major defects include pattern mismatches of more than 0.5 cm at the collar, pocket or placket, prints out of registration, shade differences between panels of the same shirt, open seams and missing buttons. Minor defects include loose threads shorter than 1 cm, small marks that can be removed and light pressing creases.

items.question: Which colourfastness tests and minimum grades do your printed rayon, cotton and polyester aloha fabrics have to pass?
items.answer: Our printed rayon, cotton and polyester aloha fabrics have to reach at least Grade 4 for washing fastness under ISO 105-C06. They have to reach Grade 3–4 for rubbing under ISO 105-X12, perspiration under ISO 105-E04 and light fastness under ISO 105-B02. For cotton and rayon, the rubbing test is done both dry and wet. We apply these washing, rubbing and perspiration standards to the rayon, cotton and polyester fabrics we print and dye, and to our printed silk. If your printed rayon is dark or strongly coloured, we advise you to ask for the wet rubbing and perspiration results as well as the washing result.

blocks.heading: Which Shirt Fabric Is Right for Your Collection?
paragraphs: The right shirt fabric is the one that matches the hand feel, drape, structure, stretch and care your collection needs.

items.heading: Fabric range and preshrinking
paragraphs: You can choose from more than 580 bases, including cotton, polyester, rayon, poly/cotton and silk, to match your hand feel, drape and price level. Every fabric is preshrunk, so your shirts keep their washed size and fit.

items.heading: Linen weight and structure
paragraphs: Our linen and linen blends run from 140 to 180 gsm, and we check the GSM in your tech pack before sending swatches. 140–160 gsm gives you cool, easy-draping aloha shirts, while 160–180 gsm gives you crisper, more structured resort shirts.

items.heading: Finished pure rayon
paragraphs: When the soft hand of pure rayon matters most, we apply a crease-resistant finish to cut down creasing. The fibre stays the same, and only the surface changes.

items.heading: Rayon for hard wear
paragraphs: For hard wear or travel, our rayon blend with 30% polyester recovers faster after sitting or packing. In return, you give up some of pure rayon's cool, fluid hand and hot-weather breathability.

items.heading: Weft-only stretch
paragraphs: When your shirt needs crosswise give, our cotton or rayon poplin with 3–5% spandex, including 95% cotton 5% spandex, gives about 10–15% stretch across the width.

items.heading: Four-way or non-stretch
paragraphs: Our four-way polyester or nylon with 8–20% spandex stretches 20–30% in both width and length. For classic non-stretch aloha drape, you can choose 100% cotton, rayon, linen or silk.

items.heading: Linen and polyester care
paragraphs: We specify cold, gentle machine washing, then hanging to dry or low tumble drying, with no bleach or high heat. Iron linen warm while it's slightly damp, and iron polyester only on low if needed.

items.heading: Seams and cutting
paragraphs: Our [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/) uses 1 cm overlocked/French rayon seams tested to ISO 13936-2 (maximum 6 mm opening), or 0.6 cm French seams for fine fabrics. Matched, directional or large-repeat prints take 10–15% extra fabric, and that's included in your price.

items.heading: Fabric-only order minimums
paragraphs: Besides finished shirts, you can buy our Hawaiian printed fabrics by the metre or by the roll. Prints from our existing library and custom prints both start at 300 metres per colourway.

items.heading: Roll size and protection
paragraphs: Each roll holds about 50 to 100 metres. Before shipment, we inspect every roll for shade, defects and width, then pack it on a core in sealed film for export.

items.heading: One colourway, one run
paragraphs: We print the full metreage of each colourway in one run, so every roll in your order comes from the same shade lot.

items.heading: Separate-run shade differences
paragraphs: When the same design is printed in separate runs, the shade varies slightly. You'll see that difference when panels from different runs are sewn side by side.

items.heading: Fabric and detailing costs
paragraphs: Rayon costs more per shirt than polyester. Your unit price also depends on your fabric choice, the complexity of your embroidery and print, and custom labels, and we itemise each of these in your quote.

paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), each fibre renders Pantone differently. So we match every base to one reference, and you approve the strike-offs/samples side by side before bulk. We also scale the artwork from toddler sizes up to 5XL and sample the whole set together.

rows: You can order a separate swatch pack for USD 80 with DHL Express delivery included. We credit that amount against your first bulk purchase order.

Handle, crumple and hand-wash the swatches before you choose your base. Photos and specifications don't show hand feel, drape, wrinkle recovery or true colour, and finding these differences at the sampling stage takes longer.
Our comfort-stretch fabric is lightweight, breathable and wrinkle-resistant, and the swatches let you judge those qualities for yourself.
We work with cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool. Other blend options include 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton.

Our standalone [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/) starts at 300 metres per colour for stock or custom-dyed fabrics and keeps garment item minimums for trims. We deliver inspected materials to your factory anywhere in the world, with reports and photos.

With [Garment Dyeing](/garment-dyeing/), you pick Pantone Coated, stock-card or custom shades. Custom minimums depend on the fabric and dye method, and we confirm feasibility during sampling. We keep colour consistent across fabric, lining and trims.

Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) covers OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics/trims, GOTS for organic cotton styles, BCI cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 quality management and WRAP social compliance, and we welcome SGS/BV inspection. We test printed/dyed rayon, cotton and polyester, plus printed silk, to minimums of ISO 105-C06 washing Grade 4, ISO 105-X12 rubbing Grade 3–4 (dry and wet for cotton/rayon) and ISO 105-E04 perspiration Grade 3–4. Rayon, cotton and polyester also meet a minimum of ISO 105-B02 light Grade 3–4.

Our [Custom Labels & Hang Tags service](/custom-labels-hang-tags/) prepares the fibre content, care instructions based on wash tests, origin and any required RN/CA details for you to approve. We follow the rules of your destination market, including US FTC, EU/UK fibre-name and Australian care-labelling requirements, and we check the labels on every private-label order.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which lightweight fabric bases remain sufficiently opaque for unlined shirts with white or pale print backgrounds?
items.answer: Cotton poplin at 120–140 gsm, rayon at 120–130 gsm and linen at 150 gsm and above stay light, and skin and pocket outlines don't show through them on white or pale print grounds. We choose the weight by garment type and climate, then check it against your background colour. A weight that suits a flowing muumuu or a breathable work shirt isn't automatically opaque enough for an unlined pale-ground shirt. Silk under 90 gsm and rayon under 110 gsm show through on pale grounds, so before sampling we send you swatches printed in your background colour so you can check the opacity.

items.question: What fabric weights are available for each uniform shirt fabric, and which weight suits all-day wear in hot weather?
items.answer: Our uniform shirt fabrics come in cotton poplin at 110–140 gsm, rayon at 100–130 gsm, polyester microfibre at 100–130 gsm, silk at 60–90 gsm, cotton-polyester blends at 120–150 gsm and moisture-wicking polyester at 110–140 gsm. For all-day wear in hot weather, we choose 100–130 gsm rayon or moisture-wicking polyester. Both stay light and breathable and dry quickly between shifts. Before you commit, we check the chosen weight against your print's ground colour.

blocks.heading: Your Shirt Brief & Design Options
paragraphs: For custom-tailored or unlisted requests, we make a prototype from your reference garment or tech pack for you to approve before bulk production, so fit, construction and material problems surface before they repeat across the order.

Our [standard ordering process](/our-process/) starts with a quotation, and sampling follows once you agree the price. In your [quote request](/request-a-quote/), send your fabric choice, artwork, colour direction, quantities and delivery schedule.

blocks.heading: Shirt Cuts, Collars & Sizes

items.heading: Collar shape and proportions
paragraphs: We adjust camp, spread or notch collars to suit your print scale. A camp collar gives a relaxed look, while a closed spread collar looks more structured and dressy.

items.heading: Four shirt cuts
paragraphs: Our [aloha shirt cuts](/) are unisex/men’s, men’s slim fit, women’s and women’s vintage, and each one is graded over 47 measurement points. Women’s vintage shirts also come with mandarin-collar and cap-sleeve options.

items.heading: Coordinated size runs
paragraphs: [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/) run from toddler sizes up to 5XL. We scale the artwork to each garment size so the prints match consistently.

blocks.heading: Woven Stripes, Checks & Jacquard
paragraphs: Yarn-dyed patterns show on both sides and stand up to repeated washing. The trade-off is that you lose the freedom printing gives you for detailed, many-coloured artwork such as florals.
rows: Our partner mills dye the yarn before weaving, and we adjust stripe width, spacing and colour combinations to your order.
We develop check, plaid and flannel-style patterns using your check size, repeat spacing and colour layout.

Our partner mills weave subtle textures, mini geometrics, tone-on-tone dots and stripes right into the cloth. It takes extra loom setup and sampling time, so it suits confirmed collections and bulk programmes.

With our [Cut & Sew alignment](/cut-sew/), we match stripes and checks across the placket, pocket, camp collar and side seams to within 0.5 cm. We also place bulk chest, pocket and placket motifs within 0.5 cm of your approved sample.

blocks.heading: All-Over Patterns & Print Methods
paragraphs: We develop floral, icon, geometric, seasonal and branded all-over prints for resort, event and promotional shirts. We choose the fabric before we finalise colours, and we make the strike-off on that same base.
columns: What it means for your shirts
rows: Cotton, rayon, polyester and blends each take ink differently, which changes the colour, texture and hand. Rayon gives a softer drape and richer colour than cotton, but it needs more careful washing and shrinkage control.

[Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) offers more than 580 bases, including yarn-dyed fabrics at 100 to 140 GSM and jacquards at 110 to 160 GSM. For a muted outer pattern, there's reverse-print cotton poplin at 110–130 gsm, approved through a two-sided strike-off and sample.
Through [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/), you choose library or custom materials from 60 to 200 GSM. Sampling swatches let you compare weights, drape and hand before you approve.

With [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/), screen printing gives deep spot colours and solid white on dyed grounds, but overlapping heavy layers feel firmer and reduce airflow. Digital printing keeps the drape of natural fibres and suits shading or more than 8 colours. Digital detail reaches 0.3 mm lines and 6 pt lettering (about 2 mm cap height), and screen detail reaches 0.5 mm and 8 pt. Crisp logos on rayon need at least 0.5 mm and 8 pt. Each screen colour adds setup cost, while digital cost stays the same whatever the colour count. Sublimation needs light-coloured polyester or blends with at least 60% polyester. Screen repeats reach 64 cm, while digital and sublimation use the full 150 cm printable width. Large repeats or pattern matching use 10–15% more fabric, and that's included in your unit price.

items.question: What limits on motif size, repeat size and fine detail should my designer follow when preparing a custom jacquard?
items.answer: Motifs should be between 0.5 cm and 8 cm, and repeats no bigger than 16 cm wide by 20 cm high. Use no more than 4 yarn colours. Lines need to be at least 1 mm and gaps at least 1.5 mm, because anything finer blurs in the weave. We check your artwork and adapt it before the mill weaves the sample. Simpler designs come out sharper and cost less in setup and yarn.

items.question: Which choices in yarn-colour count, repeat size and weave complexity change the cost of custom yarn-dyed or jacquard fabric?
items.answer: Every yarn colour after the first two adds cost. Longer repeats take more loom setup, and dense or multi-layer jacquard weaves cost more than plain stripes and simple checks.

steps.heading: Packing requirements

steps.heading: Quality and presentation

blocks.heading: How Your Shirts Are Made and Packed
rows: Before spreading, we relax and steam your printed fabric. Then we match the print across the collar, front placket, pocket and hem.

Our [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/) service cuts with size-specific templates and automated multi-layer cutting. We then assemble the panels, make buttonholes, attach buttons and neck labels, apply logos, trim threads and press your shirts, with inline checks along the way.

With [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/), all-over patterns are printed on the roll before cutting, and placement designs go onto cut panels before sewing. Any screen or plate setup charges that apply are quoted separately for you to approve.

Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) team inspects every finished piece at final inspection and keeps a measurement log for each run. Any shirt outside ±1 cm at chest width, body length and sleeves, or outside ±0.5 cm at smaller points, is rejected and then reworked or replaced. A [pre-shipment AQL sample](/quality-control/) follows, at 2.5 for major and 4.0 for minor defects. We also check that preshrunk rayon and cotton stay within 3% residual shrinkage after three home washes. Your care instructions are tested: cold or 30°C gentle washing, no tumble drying, and cool ironing on the reverse side for rayon. Tested fabrics and trims carry OEKO-TEX Standard 100, organic cotton styles carry GOTS, cotton comes through Better Cotton (BCI), and our factory holds ISO 9001 and WRAP. You're welcome to bring in independent SGS or BV inspections.

Through [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we draft the fibre content, wash-tested care information, origin and any RN or CA details your destination's rules require, all for you to approve. We check the labels on every private-label order.

Our [Packaging](/packaging/) service polybags each shirt individually as standard, or follows your own requirements. A PP reference fixes the folding, hangers, tissue, bags, label placement and carton pressure. On top of that come the sorting, stickers, carton marks and packing lists we've agreed with you.
For [Shipping](/shipping/), we agree the bulk quantities, packing method and a combined shipping plan with you before anything is dispatched.

Then we reprint from archived files and colour profiles so the colour matches that sample within ΔE ≤ 2.0.

lead: We stitch flat, 3D puff or patch embroidery on our own multi-head machines.

cta.label: Talk to us about embroidery

blocks.heading: Custom Embroidery for Hawaiian Shirts
paragraphs: We make your aloha shirts in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, and decorate them with flat embroidery, 3D puff embroidery or custom patches on our in-house multi-head machines. For embroidered patches, we stitch your design onto a separate fabric base and then apply it to the shirt. This method suits thin fabrics. We also cut custom die-cut shapes and attach your patches by sewing or heat transfer.

blocks.heading: Embroidery Techniques, Fabrics and Placement Options
paragraphs: Dense fills stiffen a lightweight shirt. Appliqué keeps the drape because the fabric is secured only at its edges. We cut and adhere your pattern and add cotton padding to give it a raised effect.

items.heading: Fabric and technique
paragraphs: We embroider directly onto cotton, rayon from about 100 gsm, linen and blends with up to 5% spandex, using cut-away backing. Silk and fabrics under 100 gsm need embroidered patches so they don't pucker.

items.heading: Placement and alignment
paragraphs: We embroider the flat panels before the shirt is assembled, so your design can go on the chest, pocket, back, sleeve, collar points or front hem. A design that crosses the pocket lines up within 3 mm, and collar stitching stays clear of the roll line. A design that crosses the opening splits at the placket edge, clear of the buttonholes.

items.heading: Your manufacturing partner
paragraphs: Our [company](/about-us/) has run its own factory since 2011 and handles production and export directly for business buyers worldwide. You agree your order with our team, not through an online shop or marketplace.

items.heading: Developing your shirt
paragraphs: Our [Product Development service](/product-development/) supports OEM and ODM work. You can bring your own custom designs, choose ready designs graded to international sizes, or combine the two. We do pattern, grading and fit work in-house, and you don't need a tech pack to start.

items.heading: Wider fabric choices
paragraphs: Our [fabric range](/hawaiian-fabrics/) covers cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool. It also includes blends such as 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton.

items.heading: One coordinated process
paragraphs: Our [production process](/our-process/) keeps fabric, embroidery, printing, sewing and finishing on one timeline with one contact. We agree your quote before sampling, and you approve the sample before bulk production starts.

items.heading: Direct English-speaking contact
paragraphs: You can [contact our English-speaking team](/contact-us/) by phone or video call at any point in your order. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

items.heading: Individual uniform details
paragraphs: Our [Hawaiian uniform shirts](/hawaiian-uniform-shirt-manufacturer/) pair shared prints and branding with individual names, titles, initials or numbers. We add these in embroidery or heat-transfer vinyl from your spreadsheet. This adds 3 to 5 production days, and then we pack by department, branch or name list.

blocks.heading: Thread Colours Matched to Your Brand
columns: What it means for your shirts
rows: We match your palette from hundreds of stock colours. If your colour isn't in our library, we source custom thread.

We judge each match on a stitched sample in daylight. Thread sheen reflects light differently from ink or a screen, so colours look lighter or shift in tone. This is strongest with glossy polyester or rayon.
This is our standard thread. It has a bright sheen and stands up well to frequent washing and bleach, so it's the choice for uniforms and shirts that get washed often.
We use rayon when a softer hand and a silk-like lustre matter most to you.
We use matte cotton to give your shirts a vintage look.
We keep metallic thread to small accent areas because it feels stiffer against the skin.
We record your thread colours on your production specification, so your reorders use the same colours as your first run.

blocks.heading: Embroidery Order Minimums and Production Capacity
paragraphs: Your order starts at 50 pieces per style in each colour. Your test batch and the bulk run that follows use the same setup. That way the test shows how placement, fabric and stitching behave on real shirts before you commit to the full quantity. We keep thread tension, stitch density and Pantone matching consistent the whole way through. We agree your first-trial quantity with you case by case, within our production capacity.

Before each run, we match sharp needles, cut-away backing, bobbin length and frame tension to your fabric. Dull or unsuitable needles cut fine rayon and linen fibres, and the wrong hoop tension causes puckering or stitch misalignment.

Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers incoming fabric, cutting, sewing, random checks and a full final inspection, and you're welcome to arrange independent SGS or BV inspection before shipment. It also includes OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GOTS for organic cotton styles, BCI for cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

Our [Cut & Sew service](/cut-sew/) uses size-specific panel templates. We assemble, button, label, trim, press and measure your shirts with inline checks throughout, then pack each one in its own poly bag.

blocks.heading: From Artwork to Approved Embroidery Preview

steps.heading: Send your artwork
steps.text: We accept AI, EPS, PDF, PNG and JPG files, and we prefer AI or EPS vectors. We review your files for design issues before digitising.

steps.heading: Check design dimensions
steps.text: Embroidery fields reach 30 x 30 cm, and chest, pocket and sleeve logos fit within 10 x 10 cm. Letters need to be at least 5 mm and lines at least 1 mm, and we flag any finer details for thickening.

steps.heading: Digitise for placement
steps.text: Digitising is included. We set density, underlay and stitch sequence for your specific fabric and placement instead of scaling one file across chest, sleeve and back.

steps.heading: Approve your preview
steps.text: We prepare your free digital embroidery preview within 24 hours of receiving your artwork. Production starts only after you approve it.

steps.heading: Retain your file
steps.text: We archive your approved digitised design, so your future reorders run from the same stitch file.

steps.heading: Protect your designs
steps.text: Our [confidentiality terms](/terms-and-conditions/) include an NDA covering your designs and business information. You keep ownership of aloha patterns developed from your artwork, and the terms prohibit us from selling your exclusive print to another client.

steps.heading: Receive your sample
steps.text: We prepare a standard sample in 10 to 15 days so you can inspect it before you approve bulk.

steps.heading: Review shirt details
steps.text: Before you sign off, you check the collar shape, fit, button position, stitching, label placement, logo size and finish against your requirements.

steps.heading: Confirm sampling terms
steps.text: Under our [Sampling service](/sampling/), you approve the fit, fabrics and technical details of every sample before bulk, and your approved shirt becomes the benchmark. Courier delivery costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

blocks.heading: Wash Performance and Combined Decoration Options

items.heading: Printing limits
paragraphs: [Custom printing](/custom-printing/) limits sublimation to light-coloured fabrics with at least 60% polyester. Screen repeats reach 64 cm, and digital and sublimation widths reach 150 cm. Large repeats or matching use 10–15% more fabric, and that's already included in your unit price.

items.heading: Wash and care
paragraphs: The thread is stitched through the fabric, so it won't crack or peel in the wash. Wash your embroidered shirts inside out on a gentle cycle and iron them from the reverse.

items.heading: Combined decoration
paragraphs: We combine embroidery on the same shirt with a screen-printed back graphic, an all-over sublimation print or heat-transfer elements.

items.heading: Stitching over prints
paragraphs: We embroider straight over screen, digital or sublimation prints. For example, we outline a printed hibiscus or add texture to your printed logo.

blocks.heading: Embroidery Costs and Design Choices

items.heading: Price drivers
items.text: Your price per shirt goes up with higher stitch counts, larger designs, more colours or placements, 3D puff instead of flat stitching, patches, appliqué and specialty threads.

items.heading: Lower-cost design choices
items.text: A single flat placement with fewer colours costs less. Swapping large fills for outlines cuts down the stitching, so you don't have to shrink your logo until it's no longer legible.

items.heading: Sample fee
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. We don't refund this fee or credit it against your bulk order.

items.heading: Design fee
items.text: We charge USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. We don't refund this fee or credit it against your bulk order either.

items.heading: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Quotation scope
items.text: Our [quotation terms](/request-a-quote/) list any applicable development charges separately. They exclude materials, trims, swatches, decoration, setup, further revisions, extra samples, freight and testing unless these are listed, and any additional cost needs your approval first.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you provide embroidery-only service on finished aloha shirts we supply, and what garment restrictions apply?
items.answer: No. We only embroider, print, heat-press or garment-dye aloha shirts that we've cut and sewn ourselves. Send us your logo or artwork, and we'll manufacture and decorate your shirts in the same run.

items.question: Does adding embroidery add extra days to the sample or bulk production time?
items.answer: Embroidered samples still take our standard 10 to 15 days. In bulk, embroidery adds 5 to 7 days to our standard 35 to 40 days of production, which depends on order size and season.

items.question: How many different thread colours can you use in one embroidered design?
items.answer: We use up to 15 thread colours in one design, and we stitch a strike-off for you to check before bulk. Approve that stitched strike-off on your actual shirt fabric, not just from the digital preview.

items.question: Can you use our existing digitised embroidery file, and which stitch-file formats do you accept?
items.answer: Yes. We accept DST, PES, EXP, JEF and EMB files. We check your file, adjust the density or underlay where lightweight aloha fabrics need it, and send you a digital preview to approve before production.

items.question: How do you stop embroidery from puckering thin rayon or linen, and will the backing feel stiff or scratchy inside the shirt?
items.answer: On rayon, linen and stretch fabrics, we use a soft cut-away stabiliser sized to each embroidered area. On thin fabrics we also lighten the stitch density so they don't pucker. We trim the backing close to the stitches and finish the reverse neatly, so it feels soft rather than stiff or scratchy.

hero.heading: Aloha Shirt Packaging
lead: We run tissue, boxes, bags, labels and tags in one coordinated production.

cta.label: Talk to us about packaging

blocks.heading: Hawaiian Shirt Packaging Options
paragraphs: We make your complete aloha shirt packaging set to your specifications, from poly bags, hang tags and woven labels to rigid boxes and mailers. The shirts come from our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, where we make them ourselves. Tissue, boxes, bags, labels and tags all go through one coordinated production run, so you work with one contact and receive everything in one delivery.

blocks.heading: Coordinated Packaging Sets for Retail-Ready Shirts
paragraphs: For retail-ready orders, our packing line folds and finishes each shirt with tissue, brand cards, hang tags, barcode labels, paper inserts and collar support. The outer packaging goes on after that.

For tissue, you can pick 17 gsm or 22 gsm acid-free logo tissue, recycled tissue or translucent glassine-style tissue. It comes in white, ivory, black, kraft brown and about 30 stock colours, and you can also choose Pantone-dyed options. We print your logo as a repeat in 1 to 4 colours, and metallic gold or silver ink is one of the choices.
We answer every [enquiry](/contact-us/) within one business day.

items.heading: Trial quantities

items.heading: Focused customisation
items.text: On a trial, you can customise one or two brand-critical pieces and use stock components for everything else, so the custom work stays concentrated.

items.heading: Quote first

items.heading: Packaging proposal

items.heading: Artwork timing
items.text: Packaging lead time starts when you approve the artwork, so signing off during garment sampling starts that clock before sampling ends.

items.heading: Standard and rush

items.heading: Bulk production
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, with order size and season setting where your order falls in that range.

blocks.heading: Export Cartons Ready for Warehouse Receiving
paragraphs: We pack your goods in 5-ply export cartons that meet shipping standards. Every carton carries shipping marks and a breakdown by style, colour and size, so your 3PL warehouse has the information it needs to receive it directly.

blocks.heading: Freight Packing Plans and Buyer-Supplied Materials

items.heading: Buyer-supplied materials
paragraphs: For [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/), your materials arrive before cutting with 5–8% fabric above the calculated consumption and 3% spare trims and labels; we inspect what arrives and report any shortages or defects within 2 business days, before anything is used.

items.heading: Written packing specification
paragraphs: Before production, we agree the label content, packing method, delivery plan and carton marks with you, then put the specification in writing and pack to it.

items.heading: Freight identification
paragraphs: Your bulk cartons carry custom PO numbers and destination notes, and each packing list shows style, quantity, size ratio and destination.

items.heading: Long sea transits
paragraphs: For long sea journeys, we use stronger cartons and properly sealed bags, and we add moisture-control packing where the transit requires it.

items.heading: Brand specifications
items.text: With [Private Label](/private-label/), you decide the materials, finishes, attachment methods and designs for your hang tags and labels.

items.heading: Fabric-safe fastening
items.text: Our [tag attachment methods](/custom-labels-hang-tags/) go through seams, labels or buttonholes instead of piercing the shirt body, and we match the fastening to your fabric and packing.

items.heading: Tag stock weights
items.text: [Trims & Accessories](/trims-accessories/) carries resort-wear tag stock from 300 to 800 gsm, which is roughly 0.4–1.2 mm thick. Laminated double-layer card goes up to 1,200 gsm.

items.heading: Core-line bags
paragraphs: Our peel-and-seal bags hold folded shirts securely without extra tape. Each bag is ready for your size, SKU or barcode stickers.

items.heading: Resealable shirt bags
paragraphs: For premium shirts, samples and bundles, zip bags leave room for inserts or small accessories, and you can open and reseal them.

items.heading: Shirt bag films
paragraphs: Individual bags, including frosted zip bags, are made from CPE, EVA or GRS-recycled PE at 60 to 140 microns. Lightweight clear OPP self-seal bags are 40 to 60 microns.

items.heading: Shipping mailer films
paragraphs: For e-commerce, we supply mailers in several grades and opacity levels, made from co-extruded LDPE/HDPE film at 60 to 120 microns.

items.heading: Custom bag printing
paragraphs: We print your logo, colours and artwork on poly bags and mailers, and both can take full-surface coverage.

items.heading: Printed component minimums

blocks.heading: Collar Inserts, Curved Bands and Clips
paragraphs: Structured collars get firm inserts, and soft rayon or silk camp collars get curved card bands. The curved band follows the open collar, so the lapel keeps its natural roll and isn't held upright. Clips go only on the inner collar stand, with folded tissue between the clip and the fabric so the clip leaves no marks.

items.heading: Dimensions from packing

items.heading: Board and finish

items.heading: Closure and inserts
items.text: For your rigid box, you can choose ribbon pulls, foam inserts and magnetic closures.

items.heading: Printed decoration
items.text: We offer full-colour lithography and debossing, plus foil stamping in copper, silver or gold.

items.heading: Recycled film content
paragraphs: You can have your bags and mailers made with 30%, 50%, 70% or 100% recycled PE content, and GRS-certified options are available.

items.heading: Resin appearance trade-off
paragraphs: Post-consumer resin is our default because it gives the strongest recycled-content claim. Pre-consumer post-industrial film gives you a clearer, more even-looking bag.

items.heading: Industrial composting option
paragraphs: We also offer biodegradable bags for industrial composting. They go through a separate disposal route from the recycled-film packaging choices.

items.heading: Recyclable kraft formats
paragraphs: Uncoated recycled kraft works for tags, tissue, mailers and folding boxes. When these are printed with water-based inks and no lamination, they stay recyclable as paper.

items.heading: Rigid box restrictions
paragraphs: A rigid box with laminated wraps, foil, soft-touch coating, magnets or foam inserts can't go into paper recycling as supplied.

items.heading: Paper-recyclable box construction
paragraphs: When you want a fully recyclable pack, we build it with uncoated wraps, blind debossing in place of foil, card inserts, and paper ribbon or tab closures.

blocks.heading: Pantone-Matched Packaging and Patterned Tissue

items.heading: Shared brand references
paragraphs: We match your tags, woven labels, bags, tissue and rigid boxes to your Pantone palette, choosing materials and finishes that fit your brand.

items.heading: Material-specific colour checks
paragraphs: We check each material against a physical Pantone swatch under the same light, and we adjust the inks separately for tissue, poly film and coated board.

items.heading: Tropical repeat tissue
paragraphs: Working from your print file, we print your shirt pattern across the tissue sheet in water-based inks, using up to 4 spot colours. Artwork with many colours is simplified to its key colours.

blocks.heading: Packaging Dielines and Artwork Proofs

steps.heading: Separate confirmed requirements
steps.text: In your [quote request](/request-a-quote/), show which artwork, wording and retail requirements are confirmed and which fabric, printing, trim and fit decisions are still open.

steps.heading: Send vector artwork
steps.text: Send your logos as vector files with the fonts outlined, and we'll place the artwork clear of folds, glue flaps and closures.

steps.heading: Check supplied dielines
steps.text: We give you an AI or PDF dieline for every box, mailer, bag, tag and insert. Each one marks the 3 mm bleed, a 3 mm internal safe area, folds and glue lines.

steps.heading: Approve the layout
steps.text: We fit your artwork to each dieline and send you digital proofs, so print problems are caught before you approve production.

blocks.heading: Text and Line Sizes for Print, Foil and Debossing
paragraphs: If any detail is too small, we flag it on your proof and suggest thicker artwork before production.
rows: Small taglines, care text and fine outlines

blocks.heading: Shirt Sorting, Retail Packing and Barcode Labels

items.heading: Unit and sorting rules
paragraphs: We pack by the unit or by the dozen. Confirm your sorting before bulk production, whether you want packing by style, size, colour, name list, department or branch.

items.heading: Standard folded packing
paragraphs: Your rayon and linen shirts ship steam-pressed and folded, each in its own polybag with collar support and clips. We fix the method in the PP packing reference before bulk.

items.heading: Retail display alternatives
paragraphs: Folded polybags work for e-commerce and warehouses. Direct retail orders can have flat packing or garments-on-hanger. Hanger packing is charged per piece and adds carton volume and freight.

items.heading: Labels before packing
paragraphs: Send us your label details or approved artwork before packing, and we'll prepare your SKU labels, size stickers, carton labels and barcode stickers.

items.heading: Amazon FBA preparation
paragraphs: Working from the FNSKU files you supply, we place polybag labels where scanners can read them, seal the bags, add suffocation warnings and label the cartons to Amazon FBA requirements. UPC or EAN labels are available instead.

items.heading: Checks and certification
paragraphs: Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) team checks order and packing details against your approvals. Before you order, we confirm which certificates apply, including OEKO-TEX Standard 100 and ISO 9001, and we send current copies when you ask for them. We welcome SGS or BV inspection.

blocks.heading: Delivery Terms, Payment and Split Destinations

items.heading: Carton size ratios
items.text: Mixing 3 to 4 sizes within one style and colour costs nothing extra. A typical ratio is S:M:L:XL at 1:2:2:1. Stores get mixed-size cartons and central warehouses get single-size cartons.

items.heading: Delivery terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Sample courier charge
items.text: [Sample delivery](/sampling/) by courier costs USD 50, which you pay on top of the sample fee.

items.heading: Group order destinations
items.text: For corporate and event batches, [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/) offers individual size labels and shipping to multiple destinations.

items.heading: DDP customs handling
items.text: When you use our DDP [Shipping service](/shipping/), your cartons carry none of our branding, and the shirts and packaging clear customs together on one invoice.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can I order hang tags, labels or boxes from you without a shirt order, for example to restock packaging for a reorder?
items.answer: Yes. We supply packaging on its own, whether you're restocking or your shirts were made elsewhere, and the item minimums are the same as for orders that include garments. We ship it straight to your factory on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.

items.question: How do you prevent coloured tissue and printed packaging from transferring colour onto the shirts?
items.answer: We use acid-free, colourfast tissue and fully cured water-based inks. Before bulk, we press damp coloured tissue and printed inserts against white cotton for 24 hours. We print bags on the outside only, and plain white tissue keeps dark printed cards apart from light shirts.

items.question: Which packaging choices raise or lower my cost per shirt, such as box type, print coverage, foil, inserts or eco materials?
items.answer: Rigid boxes cost more than bags or mailers. Your unit cost goes up with full-surface printing, extra colours, foil, debossing, extra pieces in the pack and retail-ready kitting. It comes down with plain or one-colour bags, fewer inserts and larger quantities per design. Recycled and biodegradable materials cost more than standard film.

items.question: Can your rigid gift boxes serve as the outer parcel for direct-to-customer shipping, or do they need a protective mailer or carton?
items.answer: For direct-to-customer delivery, our rigid gift boxes need a protective poly mailer or corrugated shipping carton around them, and we can print your logo on that outer packaging. If you want a box that ships on its own, we make printed E-flute corrugated mailers that take the shipping label directly.

items.question: Can you supply a fully plastic-free shirt packaging set, including closures, collar supports and protective inserts?
items.answer: Yes. Shirts go into glassine or kraft bags closed with paper tape or printed paper stickers, with card collar bands in place of plastic clips, plus paper inserts, tissue and cotton tag string. Boxes and mailers are made from recycled kraft board or paper, with water-based inks and no lamination.

items.question: Besides digital proofs, can I get a physical prototype of my box or printed bag to check before bulk production?
items.answer: Yes. A physical prototype of your rigid box or printed bag comes after digital approval and before bulk production. Check it with your actual folded garment sample instead of approving the fit from dimensions alone.

items.question: What are your biodegradable bags made from, and which documented degradation or compostability standard and disposal conditions apply to them?
items.answer: Our bags are made from a PBAT and PLA blend with corn starch, and we send the film supplier's test report with your order. They break down under industrial composting conditions, not in home compost or landfill. They don't break down in landfill or ordinary plastic recycling. We can add a compost-only disposal note to each bag.

seo.title: Aloha Shirt Sampling: Approve Before Bulk Runs | Tapa Works
seo.description: Aloha shirt sampling before bulk runs: prepare your design brief, order direct from the factory and approve your sample.

hero.heading: Aloha Shirt Sampling
lead: You check construction, fit, fabric, print scale, labels, trims and packing in one sample.

cta.label: Talk to us about sampling

blocks.heading: Hawaiian Shirt Samples: Your Options
paragraphs: Before you sign off on bulk production, our aloha shirt sample lets you check construction, fit, fabric, print scale, labels, trims and packing all at once. We make the shirts ourselves in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. If you start from one of our base styles, your sample covers fit, fabric and construction, plus a first check of your labels.

blocks.heading: Custom Samples From Our Factory

items.heading: Custom print checks
paragraphs: We go through motif scale, colour, seam alignment, shrinkage risk, fabric hand, packaging and label placement with you, and we confirm the fit suits your customers.

items.heading: Recorded decisions
paragraphs: We look over the physical sample with you and note every agreed point on a sample comment sheet, which stays with your style into bulk.

items.heading: Direct factory relationship
paragraphs: You deal directly with our [factory-owned business](/about-us/). We handle production and export ourselves, and you agree orders with our team, not through an online shop or third-party marketplace.

items.heading: Development starting points
paragraphs: Our [Product Development service](/product-development/) handles OEM and ODM sampling from your design, picture, idea, measurements, base block or reference shirt, and we do the pattern, grading and fit work in-house.

blocks.heading: Your Approved Sample Sets the Bulk Standard
paragraphs: The sample you approve becomes the standard for bulk. We sample on the bulk fabric base with the bulk print method, so a screen-printed design gets a screen-printed sample, not a digital stand-in. Bulk follows the same colour reference, with printed colour held within ΔE ≤ 2.0 and placement within 0.5 cm of the approved sample. Because the ink and fabric stay the same, the hand feel stays the same too. We keep a signed counter-sample and compare bulk fabric and finished shirts under the same lighting. Any change needs your written approval.

blocks.heading: Sample Types and Lead Times
paragraphs: Send your final artwork, fabric direction and the sample types you need at the same time, and we'll plan all the rounds on one schedule.

items.heading: Standard sample timing
items.text: Your sample is ready 10 to 15 days after you confirm the artwork and fabric direction.

items.heading: Seven sample types
items.text: You can choose fabric test, first, fit, photo, revised, pre-production (PP) and repeat samples. Our quick-response lines handle fit, photo and PP work.

items.heading: Fabric and trims
items.text: Confirming your fabric and trims takes 1 to 3 days.

items.heading: Print plate preparation
items.text: Making the print plates for your sample takes 3 to 5 days.

items.heading: Your approval window
items.text: Once the sample is delivered, your fit review and sample approval take 3 to 7 days.

items.heading: Garment dyeing allowance
items.text: For [Garment Dyeing](/garment-dyeing/), lab dips add about 5 to 7 days to the standard sample schedule.

blocks.heading: Sample Fees and Delivery

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. Design costs USD 50 per pattern or print, and that covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Courier cost and timing
items.text: Courier delivery of your sample costs USD 50 on top of the sampling fees. Tracked DHL delivery reaches your door in 5 to 7 days.

items.heading: Dispatch information
items.text: Before we dispatch, we need your full delivery address, a contact phone number and any import details.

items.heading: Quoted development scope
items.text: Our [quotation](/request-a-quote/) lists any development charges separately from bulk and leaves out extras that aren't listed. We don't commit to any additional cost until you approve it.

items.heading: Upfront sample payment
items.text: Under our [payment terms](/terms-and-conditions/), we invoice sample and design fees in USD. You pay them before sampling by T/T bank transfer or PayPal.

items.heading: Export shipping paperwork
items.text: Our [Shipping service](/shipping/) packs your goods securely and handles all the export paperwork, including the commercial invoice, packing list and customs documents.

blocks.heading: Fit Checks and Sample Testing
rows: We make one sample per style in size S or your chosen fit size to test fit, stretch and construction. Then we correct anything that needs it.
Before dispatch we measure the sample against your measurement sheet, and the results go out with the sample. Fit approval is based on measurements, not photos, and we offer live fitting videos.

Before sampling, our [Quality Control service](/quality-control/) wash-tests the fabric for shrinkage and colour bleed. After three home washes, dimensional change has to stay within 3% in both length and width.
On [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/) orders, we add a sample in every size you order before bulk, each at the sample fee. You can review the sewing and finishing before sampling or production.

blocks.heading: When to Request a Sample

items.heading: Compare fabric choices
paragraphs: If you haven't chosen a base fabric yet, sampling lets you compare cotton, rayon, nylon-spandex, quick-dry polyester or a linen blend on your actual shirt.

items.heading: Check print scale
paragraphs: For a new custom print, we sample on the real silhouette so you can see how the motif works on the finished shirt.

items.heading: Prepare marketing samples
paragraphs: We finish photo samples with final labels, buttons and retail packaging so they match your production shirts. You can supply these items, or we source them to your artwork.

items.heading: Feel fabrics first
paragraphs: Through [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/), you can order a separate swatch pack for USD 80, DHL Express delivery included. We credit that amount against your first bulk purchase order.

items.heading: Choose your cut
paragraphs: Our [aloha shirt range](/) covers men, women and children in 4 cuts: relaxed men's/unisex, shaped women's, men's tailored slim and women's vintage.

items.heading: Approve matching sets
paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), different fibres render Pantone colours differently. So we match each base to one reference and get your approval with the pieces side by side. We also sample the artwork scaled from toddler sizes up to 5XL together.

blocks.heading: Your Sample Brief and Materials
rows: You don't need a tech pack. Send us a reference shirt or base style code, artwork references, size targets, fabric direction and trim notes. High-resolution or layered artwork leaves less to interpretation.
For one aloha shirt, send about 2 metres at 140–150 cm width. A large repeat, or a print matched across the front placket and pocket, needs 3 metres.
Our [Customisation service](/customization/) offers camp, spread or notch collars, and we adjust the size and shape to suit your design.
[Contact our English-speaking team](/contact-us/) and you'll get a reply within one business day. We're available for phone or video calls throughout your project.

blocks.heading: From Quote to Sample Approval

steps.heading: Agree the quote
steps.text: Our [ordering process](/our-process/) begins with a quotation, and we start work on your sample once you agree the price.

steps.heading: Preview your artwork
steps.text: With [Custom Print Design](/custom-print-design/), you get a 3D mockup from us within 48 hours of sending your artwork.

steps.heading: Confirm sample requirements
steps.text: We confirm the fabric, print method, sample and design fees, label requirements and timing with you. Before we cut, you approve the artwork scale, placement, colour direction and construction.

steps.heading: Approve colour proofs
steps.text: You approve either a lab dip for plain grounds, which is fabric dyed to your Pantone reference or swatch, or a strike-off, which is a trial print on the actual shirt fabric that shows the ink, colours and hand feel.

steps.heading: Review the garment
steps.text: You see the finished sample on a body and mark your corrections point by point, and we work through each one.

steps.heading: Choose the next stage
steps.text: You either approve the style for bulk or ask for another sample round. We carry out a full final inspection before shipment.

blocks.heading: Bulk Order Minimums and Timing

items.heading: Sample quantity and rush
items.text: There's no minimum for samples, whether you're using a base style or a custom print. A single sample piece confirms your style before you commit to bulk, and rush work depends on our schedule.

items.heading: Bulk order minimum
items.text: Bulk orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which gives small and growing labels a way in.

items.heading: First trial quantities
items.text: We agree your first trial quantity case by case, and we flex as far as production allows.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

items.heading: Bulk payment stages
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Delivery terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Fabric preparation allowance
items.text: With [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/), stock fabric arrives within 3 to 5 days. Custom-dyed or custom-developed fabric adds 15 to 20 days before bulk starts.

items.heading: Reorder colour approval
items.text: On [Bulk Production reorders](/bulk-production/), a new colourway keeps the bulk minimum and needs a strike-off rather than another full sample. The strike-off adds 5 to 7 days.

blocks.heading: Label, Trim and Packaging Samples
paragraphs: Send your final label, hangtag and packaging artwork with your sample request, and we'll make the mockups alongside the garment so we can check them all together.

items.heading: Private label options
paragraphs: Our [Private Label service](/private-label/) is available at every order quantity. We make woven labels and heat-transfer artwork in-house, along with other branding options.

items.heading: Care label approval
paragraphs: Through [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we work from the actual materials to prepare fibre, origin and wash-tested care information for your destination. We add any required RN or CA details and get your approval on the artwork.

items.heading: Embroidered branding
paragraphs: Our [Embroidery service](/embroidery/) develops detailed designs, patches and labels, and the embroidered logos hold up to repeated washing and hard wear without fraying.

items.heading: Packing reference
paragraphs: Our [Packaging service](/packaging/) puts each shirt in its own polybag as standard, or packs to your specification. Before bulk, a PP reference fixes the folding, hangers, tissue, bags, label placement and carton pressure.

items.heading: Custom trim timing
paragraphs: With [Trims & Accessories](/trims-accessories/), woven labels take 7 to 15 days alongside shirt sampling, and custom buttons add 7 to 10 days to bulk production.

items.heading: Button minimums
paragraphs: [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/) need 1,000 pieces per design per colour, and we store the spares for your reorders. Colour-matched stock buttons have no separate minimum and work for a 50-piece shirt run.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What deviations from my measurement sheet are acceptable for the sample's chest, shoulder width, body length and sleeve length?
items.answer: Chest and body length stay within ±1 cm of your size chart. Shoulder width stays within -0.5 to 0.5 cm, and sleeve length within -1 to 1 cm. If any point falls outside these limits, we correct it before you approve the style.

items.question: If the fabric I choose isn't available in time for the sample, do you sample on a substitute, and how is that handled when bulk fabric arrives?
items.answer: Yes. If you agree, we use the closest fabric we have in stock for the first fit sample. Bulk approval is based on the pre-production sample made with your bulk fabric and bulk trims, not on the substitute.

items.question: If I'm buying from your in-stock styles, can I get a sample of those faster than a custom sample?
items.answer: Yes. An in-stock wholesale sample comes straight from stock and ships within 3 business days of payment, while a custom sample takes 10 to 15 days to make. Ask us for our current stock list, and you can pick styles, colours and sizes and check our workmanship before you pay for custom sampling.

paragraphs: We accept your own buttons, labels, hang tags, other trims, fabric and packaging, including deliveries from a supplier you nominate. We then sew, attach or pack them into your shirts.

items.heading: Delivery quantities and timing
paragraphs: When you supply materials, they have to arrive before cutting, with 3% spare trims and labels and 5–8% extra fabric beyond the consumption we calculate. We report any shortages or defects within 2 business days of receiving them.

items.heading: Button compatibility checks
paragraphs: For Custom Buttons, the buttons you supply have to be 14L to 24L, with two or four holes at least 1.5 mm wide. We attach them to your sample before bulk to confirm they fit the buttonholes and sew on securely.

items.heading: Delicate shirt tagging
paragraphs: With our [Packaging service](/packaging/), rayon and silk shirt bodies stay free of holes and marks. We put fasteners only through the underarm seam or inner neck label, or tie cotton string through a buttonhole.

items.heading: Linen and tag guns
paragraphs: For Packaging, linen gets a string loop through a buttonhole or woven label, or a small safety pin through the label. Tag-gun pins go only into seam allowances or care labels, never into the shirt body.

blocks.heading: Label Specifications and Related Resources
paragraphs: Our [Trims & Accessories specifications](/trims-accessories/) list the size and detail limits for each label type. Woven labels run from 10 × 30 mm to 60 × 100 mm with lettering of at least 1.5 mm, or 1 mm lettering and 0.3 mm lines on high-definition damask. Printed satin and taffeta labels run from 15 × 30 mm to 50 × 150 mm with 1 mm text, roughly 5 pt. Printed cotton takes lettering from 1.5 mm and lines from 0.2 mm. Heat-transfer neck labels go up to 60 × 60 mm, with lettering no smaller than 1.5 mm and lines of 0.2 mm or more so they stay readable through washing. If your artwork goes past these detail limits, it has to be simplified or moved to a larger label, and you approve its legibility on a proof before production.

steps.heading: Prepare your brief
steps.text: In your [quote request](/request-a-quote/), list your confirmed logo files, repeat artwork, label artwork, care wording, packaging references and retail requirements apart from the fabric, printing, trim and fit decisions that are still open.

steps.heading: Agree the quote
steps.text: Under [our process](/our-process/), we quote before any sampling. We then coordinate fabric, sewing, embroidery, printing and finishing on one timeline with one contact, and you can go straight to our production team with technical questions.

steps.heading: Approve label development
steps.text: For [custom labels and hang tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we create any missing artwork free of charge and send digital proofs in 3-5 days for you to approve before production. We then make physical samples in 7-15 days, alongside your shirt sampling.

steps.heading: Review shirt samples
steps.text: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50. Design costs USD 50 per pattern or print and covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

steps.heading: Arrange sample delivery
steps.text: For [sampling](/sampling/), courier delivery costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

steps.heading: Discuss your decisions
steps.text: You can [contact our team](/contact-us/) in English by phone or video call at every stage, and we reply to every enquiry within one business day.

blocks.heading: Label Production, Finishing, and Packing
paragraphs: Before production starts, we need your final artwork, the content for your care and size labels, and your folding and bagging instructions.

steps.heading: Confirm production funding
steps.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order. Bulk production starts once you've approved the sample and we've received that deposit.

steps.heading: Produce and attach labels
steps.text: Bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, and order size and season decide where in that range your order falls. We make the labels alongside your shirts and sew the neck and care labels into the seams during assembly.

steps.heading: Avoid late label changes
steps.text: Adding labels after assembly means opening finished seams or adding an extra, visible attachment step, which lowers quality and delays shipment. We deliver your shirts tagged, labelled, folded and bagged the way you specify.

steps.heading: Check production quality
steps.text: Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers fabric, cutting, sewing, random checks and final inspection. OEKO-TEX Standard 100 covers the tested fabrics and trims, along with GOTS organic cotton, BCI cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 management and WRAP social compliance. You're welcome to bring in SGS or BV inspections.

steps.heading: Settle and dispatch
steps.text: You pay the remaining 50% before shipment, on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

steps.heading: Clear branded goods together
steps.text: With our DDP [Shipping service](/shipping/), the cartons carry none of our branding, and your shirts and packaging clear customs together on one invoice.
