Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Where on the shirt can my labels be placed, can I add an outside flag label, and which label folds can I choose?
items.answer: Your labels can go at the inside neck or back yoke, in the left side seam or at the inside hem, and you can add an outside flag label on the chest pocket, side hem or sleeve. Woven labels come centre-folded, end-folded, loop-folded or straight-cut, and we also make hem tabs and sleeve flags in damask, satin or taffeta.

items.question: How do you keep sewn or heat-transfer labels from puckering, itching or showing through on lightweight rayon shirts?
items.answer: On lightweight rayon and polyester we use soft satin or fine damask labels with heat-sealed edges, sewn only along the top edge into the back neck seam with a fine needle and eased thread tension so the fabric does not pucker and no stiff edge rubs the skin, and on pale or sheer prints we choose a label base colour close to the ground so it does not show through. Heat-transfer labels go on at about 150 °C for 10 to 12 seconds with a low-temperature adhesive film suited to rayon and polyester, and we wash-test them on your fabric at sampling so they stay intact for more than 50 washes.

items.question: Which of my label, tag, button and packaging choices will push up the cost per shirt?
items.answer: Woven damask labels cost more than printed satin or cotton labels. Cost also rises with label size and with each extra thread colour, and a denser weave for finer detail needs more time on the loom. End-fold, loop-fold and mitre-fold labels need an extra folding step that straight-cut labels do not. A label sewn down on all four edges takes longer to attach than one caught in a seam. Your price per shirt already includes a standard printed neck label and care label. Woven or embossed labels are not part of that standard and increase the cost per piece. Tagless heat-transfer labels also add to the cost per shirt, as do hang tags with foil stamping, spot UV, embossing, die-cut shapes or thicker card. If your custom branded buttons need a mould, that charge appears as its own line on your quote, and you see it before you approve.

items.question: Can you develop care-label instructions that account for the shirt's fabric, print and applied branding rather than using generic washing instructions?
items.answer: Yes: we base care instructions on wash tests of your fabric and print together with any applied branding, such as embroidered logos, heat-transfer labels or printed artwork, and add lines like "wash inside out" or "do not iron on decoration" where that branding needs it. You confirm the final care wording before production, and our QC checks it on every private-label order.

blocks.heading: Apparel Trims That Complete Your Shirts
paragraphs: We fit every trim on your aloha shirts ourselves, in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Your garment trims start at the collar, where we put in collar stays, either sewn in place or slide-out, in plastic or metal. When your design has roll-up sleeves, we add button tabs to hold the rolled sleeve, and the tab buttons can match your main front buttons. Before we go ahead, you approve the tab length and the height where the tab sits.

blocks.heading: Buttons, Zippers & Shape-Supporting Trims
paragraphs: For pockets and other fashion details, you can choose metal, nylon coil or concealed zippers. Wherever the construction needs it, we reinforce the area around the zipper.
columns: How we use it on your shirts
rows: The lightest and most flexible option. It bends with soft rayon or cotton pocket fabric, so the pocket lies flat. That's why we recommend it for most lightweight aloha-shirt pockets.
The same fine coil, hidden behind the seam to give a clean, flat finish.

Heavier and stiffer, so it can drag a thin pocket out of shape. We recommend it only when you want a deliberately rugged look with a stiffer pocket. On lightweight fabric we back it with a 2 cm fusible interlining strip, and you confirm the drape on your sample.

Through our [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/) service, you get resin, urea, plastic, shell, coconut, wood, metal and fabric-covered buttons from 14L to 24L. Custom-dyed or engraved designs start at 1,000 pieces per design in each colour. Stock buttons matched to your colour have no separate minimum.

When we make your shirts through our [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/) service, camp collars and plackets get a lightweight fusible interlining as standard. At sampling you can switch to a soft sewn-in interlining or leave it out. Soft interlining suits drapey rayon, and light fusible suits crisp cotton.

items.heading: Custom trims on samples
items.text: Custom woven labels take 7 to 15 days, and custom-dyed or logo-engraved buttons take 10 to 15 days.

items.heading: Custom trims in bulk

items.heading: Checked, approved, kept

blocks.heading: Checks for Trim Strength, Comfort & Consistency
paragraphs: On lightweight aloha fabric, buttons can work loose and snaps can tear through thin plackets, so we build strength into every trim.

steps.heading: Reinforce each trim
steps.text: We lock-stitch buttons with a thread shank and back snaps with interlining and a reinforcing washer. Zippers go onto edges stabilised with stay tape, so the seam doesn't pucker.

steps.heading: Fit soft-edged labels
steps.text: Neck labels on thin fabric itch against the skin, so we use soft-edged ones.

steps.heading: Wear the sample
steps.text: We judge comfort on a sample that someone has actually worn, and we check that the inner trims stay flat and smooth, with no bulk or rubbing.

steps.heading: Pull-test the hold
steps.text: We test how well each functional trim holds up to pulling and daily wear, first on samples and again during production.

steps.heading: Match the approved standard
steps.text: Throughout your order we check logo details, colour, finish, label position and packing style, so every shirt matches the approved standard.

steps.heading: Inspect and test
steps.text: Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers every stage, up to a full final inspection. You're welcome to bring in SGS or BV inspectors, and you can request paid lab tests.

blocks.heading: Nickel-Safe Metal Snaps & Hardware
paragraphs: Our metal hardware meets the EU skin-contact limit for nickel:

items.text: They meet the EU REACH nickel-release limit of 0.5 µg/cm²/week for parts in prolonged skin contact.

items.heading: Nickel-free plating
items.text: You can request nickel-free plating on metal snaps and metal buttons.

items.heading: When to request it

items.question: Which trim choices change production cost, including button material and finish, zipper construction, trim quantity per shirt and attachment reinforcement?
items.answer: Compared with stock resin or coconut buttons, each of these raises your cost per shirt: genuine shell, custom-dyed colours, engraving, custom-moulded buttons and hidden snaps. Metal and concealed zippers cost more than nylon coil. Every trim you add, such as sleeve tabs, spare buttons, collar stays or concealed snaps, adds to the cost. So does every reinforcement, such as fusible patches, snap washers or bar-tacks. Each of these items is listed in your quote. Custom-moulded buttons and other custom hardware carry a one-time mould or tooling charge for each design. The charge has its own line in your quote. You pay it with the deposit, and you don't pay it again when you reorder. To keep this cost down, use one design across several styles and keep using it when you reorder.

items.question: Which recycled or plastic-free button and label materials can you supply for an eco-focused aloha-shirt collection?
items.answer: For an eco-focused aloha-shirt collection, we supply plastic-free buttons in coconut shell, wood, corozo and genuine shell, and we also supply buttons made from recycled polyester. We make woven or printed labels in recycled polyester or organic cotton too.

items.question: How long does trim sourcing take, and how do you make sure buttons, labels and interlinings arrive together with the fabric?
items.answer: We order your trims at the same time as your fabric, and we check in each trim before cutting. We don't cut anything until the fabric and every trim have arrived.

items.question: How do you determine whether the selected buttons, stays, labels and zippers require restrictions on washing, tumble drying or ironing?
items.answer: When we source each button, collar stay, label and zipper, we check how well it handles washing, tumble drying and ironing. Before bulk finishing, we wash, dry and press your pre-production sample with every trim attached. This brings any limit to light early. For example, you can't tumble dry natural shell buttons, and you need a cool iron near resin buttons.

items.question: Can you install concealed snaps in lightweight rayon or silk plackets without visible reinforcement or puckering, and which constructions are unsuitable?
items.answer: Yes. On lightweight rayon and silk plackets, we fit concealed snaps over a small, lightweight fusible patch pressed at a controlled temperature. We sew with fine needles and put a reinforcing washer behind each snap. You confirm the drape on your sample. Snaps aren't suitable for single-layer plackets without a facing, for sheer chiffon or georgette, or for any spot within 5 mm of a seam or edge. In those cases we recommend sewn buttons instead.

blocks.heading: Cut and Sew Hawaiian Shirts, From Raw Materials to Finished Garments
paragraphs: We make your aloha shirts from raw materials rather than printing onto blank shirts. Your custom patterns, the fabric you select and the sewing itself all stay under the control of one team, working in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Print Matching, Cutting Layouts & Fabric Allowances
paragraphs: At sampling, we agree with you where the main motif sits on the chest, pocket and back, and only then do we finalise the cutting marker. Large repeats, one-way motifs and matched pockets or plackets take 10–15% more fabric so the panels stay aligned and face the same way. That allowance is already in your unit price, and your quote shows fabric consumption per shirt so you can compare layouts. We build the marker around your repeat, which runs up to 64 cm for screen printing or the full 150 cm printable width for digital printing. Collars, front plackets, pockets and hems are matched with no visible break, and each pocket is cut at its exact position in the repeat. Matched panels are cut one ply at a time instead of stacked, and your quote already covers this slower cutting.

visuals.purpose: Explain the additional fabric allowance included in the unit price for demanding print layouts.

blocks.heading: In-House Production & Direct Ordering Options

items.heading: Order quantities
paragraphs: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which suits small and growing labels. For a first trial, we agree the quantity with you case by case within our production capacity.

items.heading: Product development
paragraphs: Through [Product Development](/product-development/), we offer OEM/ODM and wash-tested contrast panels. The fabrics we pair are within about 40 GSM and 2% shrinkage of each other, and remaining shrinkage is no more than 3% after three home washes.

items.heading: Direct factory relationship
paragraphs: [Our factory](/about-us/) has been running since 2011 and handles sublimation in-house. We sell B2B only, through this website and our team, and have no online shop or third-party marketplace store.

blocks.heading: Pattern Creation, Revisions & Size Grading
paragraphs: We develop your base-size pattern and revise it before any grading begins, so every change to the fit has to go in before you approve the base size. Our patterns follow the sizing standards of major fashion labels as well as international sizing standards.

blocks.heading: Back Pleats & Yokes for Your Preferred Fit
paragraphs: Where the main motif of your back print sits decides which back construction keeps the artwork intact.
rows: Keeps a large back print in one unbroken piece.
A 2–3 cm pleat gives you relaxed room across the back. The shoulders stay narrow, and the shoulder seam stays true to your size chart.
Two 1.5 cm pleats near the shoulder blades give you more back room without widening the shoulders you specified.
We make each of these back constructions with or without a yoke.

blocks.heading: Your Pattern Files, Shirt Cuts & Collar Choices

items.heading: Your DXF patterns
paragraphs: Send us your DXF files with a measurement chart. If you also send a reference shirt, we can check the fit you're aiming for. Pre-production covers two sample rounds and pattern and machine adjustments, and then we regrade across the full size range.

items.heading: Pattern storage and release
paragraphs: We keep your patterns on file for reorders. Releasing the actual pattern files to you costs USD 580 per pattern.

items.heading: Shirt cut options
paragraphs: Our [aloha shirt range](/) comes in unisex/men's, men's slim, women's and women's vintage cuts. Each one is graded across 47 measurement points, and there's a mandarin-collar, cap-sleeve option for women.

items.heading: Custom collar shapes
paragraphs: Through [Customisation](/customization/), you pick a camp, spread or notch collar, and we adjust its size and shape to suit your design.

items.heading: Coordinated size ranges
paragraphs: Through [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), we run your print from toddler sizes up to 5XL and scale the artwork so its placement stays the same on every garment.

blocks.heading: Fabric, Trim & Button Selection with Material Checks
rows: Allow about 1.6–1.8 m for each standard short-sleeve shirt at a usable width of 140–150 cm. We work out your exact consumption, including the matching allowance where it applies. Send 5–8% extra before cutting. Sticking to a single dye lot means lots don't get mixed, and roll labels keep everything traceable.

Before anything is used, we inspect shade, direction and quality and wash-test for shrinkage. Within 2 business days, we report any shortages, defects, shade variation or shrinkage over 3%. You then choose between replacement fabric and cutting around the flaws using the allowance. We also sort shade lots so each shirt stays consistent, or preshrink the fabric before cutting.

Through [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/), we check fabrics, trims and accessories for quality, consistency and compliance. We offer bases from 60 to 200 GSM matched to your printing method, and we send you swatches so you can approve the drape and hand.

Through [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/), we supply coconut, wood, shell or resin buttons from 14L to 24L (about 9 to 15 mm). If you supply your own trims, send them with 3% spares before cutting. Buttons need two or four holes at least 1.5 mm wide. We report delivery shortages or defects within 2 business days and sample-test the attachment. Branded tooling is quoted separately, and we keep the moulds for 3 years.

Through [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/), we make reverse-print shirts with the printed face turned inside, which gives the outside a muted look. We use 100% cotton poplin at 110–130 gsm, once you approve strike-offs of both faces and a sample of the outer effect.

Through [Trims & Accessories](/trims-accessories/), sourcing takes 7 to 15 days. Trims are ordered along with the fabric and arrive at least 3 days before cutting, so we can check them against the approved card. Cutting doesn't start until all the fabric and trims are in.

blocks.heading: Tech Pack & Fit Sample Sign-Off Before Production
paragraphs: Before we cut any fabric, we prepare a detailed tech pack for you to approve, and you keep that documentation. Ahead of bulk production, we make a physical fit sample in every size you've ordered. We try these samples on real people, which checks the fit in ways the chart measurements can't. You can review the sewing and finishing details before sampling or bulk production. Bulk only starts once you've approved the measurements, fabrics and specifications.

blocks.heading: Sample Lead Times, Fees & Delivery Costs

items.heading: Sample timing
items.text: A standard sample takes us 10 to 15 days to prepare.

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: You pay USD 50 for each sample. Design costs USD 50 per pattern or print, and that covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Courier delivery cost
items.text: For [Sampling](/sampling/), courier delivery costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

blocks.heading: Industrial Equipment for Precise Cutting & Sewing
paragraphs: We cut on industrial cutting machines and sew on single-needle lockstitch lines fitted with specialised presser feet. During sampling, we pick the folders and hemming attachments that suit your fabric and your cuff and hem widths.

Our [Bulk Production](/bulk-production/) floor covers 5,800 square metres. It holds 13 production lines, 6 automatic cutting lines and more than 580 sewing machines. When your timeline requires it, we run 24/7.

Through [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/), we print all-over repeats on rolled fabric before cutting, so the pattern matches continuously across collars, plackets, pockets and hems. Engineered or placement designs are printed on cut panels before sewing, including sublimation transfer on polyester. This puts the motif in the same position on every shirt.

visuals.purpose: Distinguish the production order for all-over prints from engineered or placement designs.
visuals.caption: The print layout determines when fabric is printed and cut.

rows.label: Printing stage
values: Cut the panels first, then print each panel before sewing.

rows.label: Placement objective
values: Continuous repeat matched across collar, placket, pocket and hem.
Motif in exactly the same spot on every shirt.

blocks.heading: Stitch Specifications, Seam Reinforcement & Quality Checks
rows: At sampling, we choose French seams where sheer fabric shows the inside, or overlocking for a lighter, softer seam. We overlock cotton, polyester blends, rayon and other lightweight fabrics. We also offer double-needle stitching for casual shirts, including twill and chambray.

Armholes, side seams, pocket corners, yokes and sleeve openings that take stress get stronger thread, double stitching, extra fabric layers or bar tacks, depending on the construction. Bar tacks go at pocket corners, sleeve plackets, side vents and bottom openings.

Main seams run at 10 to 14 stitches per inch and topstitching at 8 to 12 SPI, and we set the exact specification at sampling. Lightweight rayon is sewn at 12 SPI. Each automatic buttonhole has 80 to 100 stitches.

Lightweight rayon gets 1 cm overlocked or French seams, tested to ISO 13936-2 with a seam opening of no more than 6 mm. Silk and very fine fabrics can also have flat-felled side seams or narrow 0.6 cm French seams, which finish flat with little bulk.

Through [Quality Control](/quality-control/), we check fabric on arrival and then check cutting and sewing. We carry out random checks and a full final inspection against your approved sample. Any shirt outside ±1 cm on chest width, body length and sleeves, or ±0.5 cm on collars, cuffs and small points, is rejected and then reworked or replaced. You're welcome to bring in SGS or BV for inspection. Tested fabrics and trims carry OEKO-TEX Standard 100, organic cotton styles carry GOTS, cotton comes through Better Cotton (BCI), and our factory holds ISO 9001 and WRAP.

blocks.heading: Construction Choices for Collars, Fronts & Hems
rows: You set the stitch and seam finishes, collar and cuff construction, button attachment, pockets, reinforcement, pressing, trimming and packing.
We cut the collar in one piece with no collar stand and join it to a 3.5 cm self-faced front. Then we turn and press it and topstitch at 0.6 cm, so it falls open and lies flat.

You choose a folded-back camp facing, a separate sewn-on placket, a concealed-button fabric fly or a French front. The French front folds under with no separate placket seam, which keeps large artwork intact. Sewn-on or concealed plackets give a more structured front.

Fine needles in sizes 9 to 11, low thread tension and a walking foot stop puckering. Straight-grain facings backed with light fusible or soft non-fused interlining keep plackets flat before edge-stitching and gentle, low-heat steam pressing.

You choose a straight hem with 4–6 cm side vents, a curved shirt-tail hem or a straight hem without vents. Each one is finished with a 1 cm double-turned narrow hem. Vented straight hems sit level at the hip when worn untucked, and curved hems suit tucked or loose wear.

At sampling, you choose standard lightweight fusible, which gives crisp cotton shape without stiffness. For drapey rayon, you choose soft sewn-in non-fused interlining or none at all, which gives an unstructured, softer roll.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you assemble aloha shirts from pre-cut panels we supply, rather than handling the whole manufacturing process?
items.answer: Yes. We sew the panels you supply and add your trims, buttons and labels, or ours. Then we finish, press and pack the shirts in our factory. Bundle and label the sets by size and shade lot so each shirt's panels come from the same lay, and send 3% spare panels per size. We count and inspect each delivery and report any shortages or defects within 2 business days, before sewing starts.

items.question: Your lines run lockstitch machines. How do you sew knit or stretch aloha shirts so the seams stretch without popping?
items.answer: For interlock, pique and poly-spandex shirts, we sew the main seams with 4-thread overlock and the hems and sleeve openings with 2- or 3-needle coverstitch. We use textured polyester looper thread, so the seams stretch without popping. Single-needle lockstitch is only used on plackets, collars and topstitching, and clear elastic or tape stabilises the shoulders.

items.question: How do you keep lightweight rayon or silk panels from slipping or stretching out of shape during cutting?
items.answer: We take rayon and silk off the roll and let them relax for 12 to 24 hours. Then we spread them without tension over a paper underlay, in lays of no more than 30 plies, and vacuum hold-down keeps them from moving. Very fine silk is cut one ply at a time against the pattern so it keeps its shape and grain.

blocks.heading: Who Handles Import Clearance, Duties and Transit Risk?

items.text: With FOB or CIF, you or your customs broker handle import clearance at the destination, and you pay the duties and import taxes.

items.heading: Choosing your term
items.text: DDP suits first-time importers and buyers who don't have a regular customs broker. FOB or CIF suits buyers who import routinely and already work with an established broker.

items.heading: Direct factory orders
items.text: Our [factory-owned B2B business](/about-us/) handles both production and export. Your order comes directly through our team rather than through online shops or marketplaces, and our shipments have reached over 55 countries.

items.heading: Developing your shirts

paragraphs: Under FOB and CIF, the risk of loss or damage passes to you once the goods are loaded aboard the vessel at the agreed loading port. With FOB, you arrange cargo insurance from that port. With CIF, you claim any transit loss on the policy we provide. With DDP, transit risk stays with us until your shipment reaches your door, ready for unloading.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What loss or damage does the cargo insurance you arrange under CIF cover?
items.answer: Our standard CIF insurance covers 110% of the invoice value under Institute Cargo Clauses (C). That protects you against fire, explosion, the vessel sinking, stranding or colliding, jettison and general average. It doesn't include the extra cover for theft, non-delivery, water damage and handling damage that Clauses (A) give you. If you want those risks covered, ask us for all-risks Clauses (A) cover before shipment and we'll arrange it.

items.question: Roughly how many aloha shirts fit in one export carton, and what are the usual carton dimensions and weight I should use to estimate air or sea freight?
items.answer: A standard 60 × 40 × 40 cm carton holds about 50 to 60 folded aloha shirts, each in its own polybag. It weighs around 12 to 15 kg gross and takes up about 0.096 m³. For air freight, its volumetric weight comes to about 16 kg. Before shipment, our packing list confirms the exact carton counts, dimensions and weights.

items.question: Does choosing rayon, cotton, polyester or a blend, or a men's versus women's cut, change the import duty and the DDP price for my aloha shirts?
items.answer: Yes. Men’s woven aloha shirts come under HS heading 6205 and women’s under 6206. The subheading follows whichever fibre makes up most of the weight, whether that's cotton, a man-made fibre such as polyester or rayon, linen or silk. Your fabric and cut set the duty rate that applies in your country. We work out DDP duty from your exact fabric and cut, so changing either one changes the price, and we confirm the code with you before bulk production.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: In what format should I send the list of people, sizes and garment types for each family or group?
items.answer: Send us one Excel or CSV spreadsheet with a row for each person. Give the family or group name, the person’s name, garment type, size and colourway, and add a count of each size for every style and colour. Include the spreadsheet with your sample approval, and we'll check the quantities against it within 1 business day. Before cutting starts, we check every name row against the size counts for each style and colour and flag any mismatches to you. You can change names and sizes up to 5 days before cutting starts. If a size or colourway is wrong, the set ends up with a missing or incorrect piece, and that is costly to fix after cutting.

items.question: How do you keep the print matching across pieces made from different fabrics, like an adult rayon shirt and a baby cotton romper?
items.answer: We match every fabric base to the same Pantone reference. Before bulk production, you approve a strike-off or sample of each base side by side. The same Pantone colour never looks identical on rayon shirting, cotton and polyester swim fabric, because each fibre takes dye and reflects light differently. Matching to one reference gives you a coordinated set. It does not make the colour look identical across different fibres.

seo.title: Aloha Shirt Print Design: Artwork Layouts | Tapa Works
seo.description: Production-ready aloha shirt print design: artwork layouts, print methods suited to your fabric and library prints adapted for you.

hero.heading: Aloha Shirt Print Design
lead: You can test a new print in a small run before ordering larger quantities.

cta.label: Talk to us about custom print design

blocks.heading: Hawaiian Shirt Print Design for Your Label
paragraphs: You can start with 50 pieces per style in each colour, so our aloha shirts are open to small and growing labels. We make them ourselves at our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. For a first trial run, we agree the quantity with you case by case, and we are as flexible as production allows. When you come back for [bulk reorders](/bulk-production/), we keep your print's colour profiles and pattern specifications on file and use those records to match your original run.

blocks.heading: From Your Brief to Samples and Delivery
rows: Our [order process](/our-process/) begins with a quote. Once you agree the price, we move to sampling so you can judge the quality, and bulk production follows when you approve the sample.

To get an [itemised quote](/request-a-quote/) within 24 hours with no obligation, list your confirmed logos, repeats, label artwork, care wording, packaging references and retail requirements separately from any fabric, print, trim and fit decisions that are still open. We then review your design and fabric choice and price the quantity, construction, design complexity, fabric type and availability, lining, print method, logo application, labels, branding, packaging, size ratio and lead time.
A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days.
With our [Sampling service](/sampling/), the lead time starts once your artwork and fabric direction are confirmed. Courier delivery of the sample costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order. Once you've approved the sample and we've received that deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, with the exact timing set by order size and season. You pay the remaining 50% before shipment.

Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers incoming fabric, cutting, sewing, random checks and a full final inspection, and you're welcome to bring in independent pre-shipment inspectors such as SGS or BV. It's backed by OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GOTS for organic cotton styles, BCI for cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.
We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.
[Contact our English-speaking team](/contact-us/) by phone or video call at any step. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

blocks.heading: Need Help Turning Your Ideas into Shirt Prints?
paragraphs: Yes. We can turn your ideas into production-ready shirt prints, or we can support your own designer with templates and artwork guidance.

items.heading: Design support
paragraphs: Our graphic designers create new prints every day, develop custom patterns and forecast trends, and sample turnaround is fast. We take your sketches, moodboards and references and create exclusive resort prints for your collection.

items.heading: Repeat and placement development
paragraphs: We separate colours, build repeats, scale the artwork to the garment and refine placement. Before any strike-off, you approve both the flat repeat tile and the 3D placement on the collar, placket and pocket. Changing a screen costs less than reprinting a sample.

items.heading: Your first previews
paragraphs: Send us your logo and ideas and you get 3 mock-ups within 48 hours. If you supply the artwork, we send a 3D mockup within 48 hours. A flat tile can't do this, but the mockup shows where the key motifs land after cutting and sewing.

items.heading: Tropical and novelty themes
paragraphs: You can choose florals with hibiscus, plumeria and tropical blooms; monstera, palm fronds and jungle foliage; beach scenes with sunsets, waves, surfboards and coastline; or quirky novelty prints.

items.heading: Faces, logos and solids
paragraphs: Besides tropical and custom artwork, we offer face prints, logo prints and solid-colour styles. A face-print shirt can show two, three, five or more faces.

items.heading: Personalised photo shirts
paragraphs: We print photo shirts with high-resolution sublimation, with no pixelation. Personalised photo designs are printed with either DTF or sublimation.

items.heading: Coordinated and themed shirts
paragraphs: Couple shirts have coordinated his-and-hers prints. Pet shirts turn your pet into a full-repeat aloha pattern. Retro shirts recreate vintage aloha looks from the 1950s to the 70s.

items.heading: Style development support
paragraphs: Our [OEM and ODM product development](/product-development/) can start from your design, a picture or just an idea. Pattern design, grading and fit development all happen in-house, which means fewer rounds of back-and-forth on the design.

blocks.heading: Which Fabric and Print Method Fit Your Design and Budget?
paragraphs: Your fabric, ground colour and repeat size decide which print method works.
columns: What we supply and how we produce it
rows: Our [Hawaiian Fabrics service](/hawaiian-fabrics/) offers cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool, including 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton blends, as finished shirts or as fabric by the metre or roll. Library and custom fabric prints start at 300 metres per colourway, in rolls of about 50 to 100 metres. We inspect each roll for shade, defects and width, then pack it on a core in sealed film for export.

Sublimation handles repeats across the full 150 cm printable width and up to 150 cm long. We plan matching at the marker stage and cut each panel from its matching point on the printed roll instead of nesting panels freely. That extra fabric gets you unbroken matching across the collar, front placket, pocket and hem.

Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-printing/) prints rayon, cotton, linen and silk on the roll by screen or digital printing before cutting for all-over patterns. Sublimation is limited to light-coloured polyester and blends with at least 60% polyester. Engineered or placement designs are printed on cut panels before sewing, so the motifs land in the same position on every shirt. We make reverse prints on cotton. For dark grounds, we either dye the fabric before screen printing or print the full ground digitally. Screen repeats go up to 64 cm and digital repeats up to 150 cm wide. Large repeats or pattern matching need 10–15% extra fabric, which is built into your unit price. We don't change the approved sample's method, fabric base or colour reference unless you approve it in writing. Colour stays within ΔE ≤ 2.0 and placement within 0.5 cm. Send 300 DPI PNG, JPG, JPEG, PSD, PDF, AI or EPS artwork or a reference sample. Vector EPS or AI with outlined text and expanded strokes is best, or else high-quality JPG or PDF. We check files for clarity, durability and compliance, and you confirm the layout before production.

Alongside screen printing, our [Embroidery service](/embroidery/) offers intricate custom work, patches and labels made by skilled fashion designers. Our embroidered logos hold up to repeated washing and hard wear without fraying.

blocks.heading: Prepare Your Artwork for All-Over and Border Prints
paragraphs: If your artwork is built on repeating motifs, it suits an all-over resort-shirt layout printed on the roll. If it has a natural band or edge, it suits a border along the hem or a design that frames the placket. We set the layout for your artwork based on that difference.

Send us the repeat tile and any border element as separate layered files. Our designers then build a seamless repeat and place the border on each size’s panels without redrawing your artwork. With a border print, you give up the relaxed, continuous look across the whole shirt and get a framed focal design instead.

blocks.heading: Design Fees and Artwork Rights: What You Need to Know
paragraphs: Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design, covering all its colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against bulk orders. Before development, we need your written confirmation that you own or are licensed to use the designs, logos or pictures you supply. When you send someone else's reference, we use it only for its mood and draw an original print.

visuals.purpose: Distinguish the sample fee from the design fee and clarify what each covers.
visuals.caption: Sample and design fees are separate; neither is refunded or credited against the bulk order.

blocks.heading: Adapt a Library Print and Make the New Design Yours
paragraphs: Our library prints and base aloha shirt styles are non-exclusive as they stand: another brand can order the same print or shirt unless you change its print, fit or trims. For a look of your own, we adapt a library print by adding your logo and branding, recolouring or rescaling it, or swapping or reworking its motifs and layout.

An adapted library print gives you a new finished design, but it doesn't give you a completely original starting concept, because the unchanged base stays in our library. If the print is central to your brand identity, we develop a fully custom print from your own artwork instead.

Once you pay the design fee for an adapted or fully custom print, the finished design belongs to your label alone under our NDA, and we never sell it to another client. That protection doesn't cover the unchanged library original.

seo.title: Fabric Sourcing to Match Your Specs | Tapa Works
seo.description: Fabric sourcing to match your specs, with a shortlist, quote and samples for approval before bulk production.

hero.heading: Fabric Sourcing to Match Your Specs
lead: You only see swatches that already meet your tech pack, so fewer rounds go back and forth.

cta.label: Talk to us about fabric sourcing

blocks.heading: Fabrics Matched to Your Brand
paragraphs: Before any swatches go out to you, we check each fabric against your tech pack for GSM, hand feel, stretch and intended end use. When you need Hawaiian fabric sourcing for your aloha shirts, we source the fabric and make the shirts in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. We source knits, wovens, performance and technical fabrics, sustainable and specialty materials, and the trims and accessories to match. Every material is checked for quality, consistency and compliance before production starts.

blocks.heading: Fabric Blends, Weaves & Finishes
columns: What it means for your shirts
rows: We develop blends such as 55% linen 45% rayon or 70% rayon 30% linen. They come in plain, twill, dobby, seersucker or jacquard weaves, at weights from 80 to 200 GSM. Custom development starts at 1,000 metres per quality, and we confirm the exact minimum for your fabric type at sampling.

Peach, enzyme and silicone softening, easy-care wrinkle resistance and UV finishes add cost. The price per metre also goes up with finer combed or long-staple yarns, denser or more complex weaves and heavier GSM.

When a lower-cost fabric and a higher-spec fabric both meet your spec, we show you them side by side. An upgrade is worth paying for where wearers see or feel it, such as softening on a resort shirt. The lower-cost choice gives up some softness, drape or easy-care performance for a lower shirt cost.

Our [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) range covers cotton poplin at 110–140 GSM; cotton lawn at 80–110 GSM; rayon challis, rayon crepe and other viscose at 100–130 GSM; silk crepe de chine at 60–90 GSM; linen, linen-cotton and linen-rayon at 140–180 GSM; and polyester or poly-cotton peachskin and other light polyester blends at 100–130 GSM. For lighter or heavier specifications, we source from 60 to 200 GSM.

When you order printed fabric only through [Hawaiian Fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/), existing-library and custom prints both start at 300 metres per colourway. We supply the fabric in rolls of about 50 to 100 metres. Each roll is inspected for shade, defects and width, then packed on a core in sealed export film.
With [factory ownership](/about-us/), production and export stay inside one company, so we control quality, cost and delivery directly.

blocks.heading: Custom Colours & Yarn-Dyed Patterns
rows: We develop stripes, checks and jacquards, and one round of yarn-colour lab dips is included. Before the yarn is dyed for weaving, we compare each dip with your physical colour standard under daylight and under store lighting. After weaving, the colour is fixed and can't be corrected the way a print can.

Custom colours start at 300 metres per colour. We confirm the exact minimum at sampling based on fabric type and dye method. One lab-dip round is included, and in-stock colour-card shades have no fabric minimum.

For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/) from toddler sizes to 5XL, polyester swim fabric, rayon and cotton each look different against the same Pantone reference. So we match each base separately for you to approve side by side, scale the artwork by size and sample the whole set together.

blocks.heading: Library Fabrics vs. Custom Material Development
paragraphs: We start with our fabric library. When no library quality meets the drape, stretch or fibre content your design needs, we develop custom material.

items.heading: Resort fabric options
items.text: Beyond our core range, we offer drapey rayon and performance stretch fabrics, so you have different options for how a resort shirt moves and feels.

items.heading: Ready for sampling
items.text: Library fabrics are already tested, so we sample and produce them straight away with no separate material-development round.

items.heading: Custom material development
items.text: Developing your own quality takes its own sampling round and a larger fabric commitment than picking an existing library fabric.

items.heading: Exclusivity trade-off
items.text: When you choose a library quality over custom development, you give up having a cloth exclusive to your brand.

blocks.heading: Sustainable Fabrics & Printing Options

items.heading: Start with your claim
paragraphs: First we ask what sustainability claim you plan to print on your labels or hang tags. Then we choose a fabric whose certification backs that claim up.

items.heading: Certified purchasing route
paragraphs: Certification documents only come with fabric bought through a certified supply chain. They can't be added after the fabric has been bought.

items.heading: Sustainable material choices
paragraphs: We use sustainable fabrics wherever we can, including organic cotton, recycled polyester, certified recycled nylon and Better Cotton (BCI). Eco-friendly dyes and sustainable packaging are also available.

items.heading: Recycled polyester documentation
paragraphs: We hold GRS (Global Recycled Standard) certification for recycled polyester and send the documentation with your order. Other certified fabrics are supplied on request, and the fabric you select decides which certificates you get.

items.heading: Plain-colour dye selection
paragraphs: Our partner mills use OEKO-TEX certified dyes for plain colours. We choose the fabric and its supporting certification to meet your collection's requirements.

items.heading: Printing limits and consumption
paragraphs: With our [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/), we use sublimation only on light-coloured polyester or on blends with at least 60% polyester. Screen-print repeats go up to 64 cm and digital/sublimation repeats go up to 150 cm.

blocks.heading: Buttons, Labels & Other Material Details

items.heading: Trims & Accessories
items.text: With our [Trims & Accessories](/trims-accessories/) service, we order trims along with your fabric and allow 7 to 15 days for them, so they arrive at least 3 days before cutting. We only start cutting once the trims have been checked against the approved card and every material has arrived.

items.heading: Custom Buttons
items.text: Through [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/), we supply resin, urea, plastic, shell, coconut, wood, metal and fabric-covered buttons, matched to your design, fabric and order.

items.heading: Custom Labels & Hang Tags
items.text: With [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we write the fibre, wash-tested care and origin information from the materials you're actually using. We add any required RN or CA numbers, follow the rules of the country you're shipping to and get your approval on the artwork.

blocks.heading: Materials Only or Finished Shirts
paragraphs: Finished-shirt orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Full-package responsibility
paragraphs: With [Bulk Production](/bulk-production/), we source the materials and do the cutting and sewing in our workshops. That means one team is responsible for any shrinkage or shade problems. We also offer design and development.

items.heading: Sourcing-only orders
paragraphs: If you already trust another sewing factory, we can source just the fabric and trims. Stock and custom-dyed fabrics start at 300 metres per colour, and trims have the same minimums as garment orders.

items.heading: Separate sourcing fee
paragraphs: We charge separately for finding and coordinating your materials. Fabric, trims, labels and shipping each get their own line on the same itemised quote, so the fee isn't hidden in the material prices.

items.heading: Inspection and delivery
paragraphs: We inspect sourcing-only materials and send you reports and photos when we deliver them to your factory. We ship to any country by express, air or sea on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.

items.heading: Development and trial orders
paragraphs: Through [Product Development](/product-development/), we support OEM and ODM working from your design, a picture or just an idea. We agree first-trial quantities case by case, within what production allows.

items.heading: Your supplied materials
paragraphs: For [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/), your materials have to arrive before cutting, with 5–8% extra fabric and 3% spare trims and labels. We inspect everything on arrival and report any shortages or defects within 2 business days, before anything is used.

items.heading: Your design ownership
paragraphs: Under our NDA, [Custom Print Design](/custom-print-design/) keeps prints developed from your artwork exclusive to you. You own the finished design once it's paid for, and the tech packs are yours to keep. Paid print files are available on request, and we release stored pattern files for a charge per pattern.

items.heading: Package selection
paragraphs: If we sew your shirts too, the full package keeps all material corrections in one place. With sourcing-only, your existing factory does the cutting and sewing.

blocks.heading: From Your Brief to Fabric Options & Pricing
paragraphs: We narrow your shortlist by technical specification, target retail price and how the shirts will be worn.

steps.heading: Send your brief
steps.text: Send your tech pack, reference samples and fabric requirements through our [enquiry page](/contact-us/). We reply within one business day and sort out any questions before sourcing starts.

steps.heading: Receive your shortlist
steps.text: Within 5 business days of getting your brief, we send you 3 to 5 fabric options that meet your specification. Physical swatches reach you by courier 5 to 7 days after that.

steps.heading: Compare fabric specifications
steps.text: Each option lists fibre composition, GSM, usable width, weave or knit construction, available colours, and the mill's shrinkage and colourfastness data.

steps.heading: Calculate material requirements
steps.text: Within 2 business days of receiving your patterns, we send you the fabric consumption per size and for the total order quantity, plus an extra 3% cutting allowance.

steps.heading: Agree itemised pricing
steps.text: Our [quotation](/request-a-quote/) includes fabric recommendations, a timeline and line-item pricing. You get a full itemised quote before production, with no hidden fees.

steps.heading: Approve and track
steps.text: Under [Our Process](/our-process/), we agree the price before sampling and agree timing before production, based on fabric availability, artwork readiness, trims and shipping. Then we place the order and track it.

blocks.heading: Samples, Approval & Production Timelines
paragraphs: If you settle on the final fabric before you approve the sample, bulk production uses exactly the material you signed off.

steps.heading: Confirm fabric availability
steps.text: Stock fabrics reach our factory in 3 to 5 days. Custom-dyed or custom-developed fabrics add 15 to 20 days before bulk production starts.

steps.heading: Make your sample
steps.text: A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days, so you have the garment in hand to review before you approve production.

steps.heading: Account for development fees
steps.text: Each sample costs USD 50. Design costs USD 50 per design and covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

steps.heading: Arrange sample delivery
steps.text: [Sample courier delivery](/sampling/) costs USD 50, which you pay on top of the sample fee.

steps.heading: Release bulk production
steps.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season set the exact schedule.

steps.heading: Control changes and shipment
steps.text: If you switch to custom-dyed or custom-developed fabric after approval, the fabric lead time starts again and bulk production is delayed. Every completed order goes through a full final inspection before it ships.

blocks.heading: Fabric Certifications & Quality Checks
paragraphs: We check your fabric when it arrives, check the cutting and sewing, and carry out random checks during production.

items.heading: Verify certificate coverage
items.text: Before we order, we get the supplier’s current certificate and check that it covers your specific fabric and the production site, not just the mill in general.

items.heading: Check certificate validity
items.text: Certificates expire and cover only the products and sites named on them. Where it applies, we work with suppliers holding recognised organic-textile and chemical-safety certifications.

items.heading: Confirm style-specific evidence
items.text: Through [Quality Control](/quality-control/), we confirm that the certificates cover your fabric, trims, dyes and inks, children’s styles included, and we send you current copies on request.

items.heading: Support UPF claims
items.text: We state a rating such as UPF 50+ only when a fabric report to AS/NZS 4399 or EN 13758-1 backs it up, and we supply that report with your order.

items.heading: Test shrinkage before sampling
items.text: Our preshrunk printed rayon and cotton must stay within 3% shrinkage in length and width after three home washes, and we check colour bleed before sampling.

items.heading: Check finished measurements
items.text: Your garments stay within ±1 cm at chest, length and waist, and within ±0.5 cm at the collar, cuff and other small measurement points.

items.heading: Measure colourfastness performance
items.text: Printed and dyed fabrics, high-twist chiffon included, reach Grade 4 or above for washing and Grade 3–4 or above for rubbing and light.

items.heading: Arrange independent testing
items.text: You’re welcome to bring in SGS or BV for inspection. If you ask for testing at an accredited lab, including US flammability testing to 16 CFR Part 1610, you approve the booking and prepay the lab fee for each item.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you source fabric from a specific origin I ask for, such as Japanese or Korean mills, and give me proof of where it came from?
items.answer: Yes. We source from the country you ask for, Japanese rayon or Korean polyester included, and give you the mill’s commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin for the lot. Imported fabrics add 10 to 20 days to the fabric lead time before cutting.

items.question: Can you supply sample-length fabric cuts for my factory to make trial shirts before I commit to bulk fabric?
items.answer: Yes. We courier cuts of 3 to 5 metres per fabric to your factory within 7 to 10 days of your request. That’s enough for one or two trial shirts.

items.question: Can you source our specified fabric directly from a mill we nominate rather than asking us to purchase and supply it?
items.answer: Yes. Send us the mill’s contact, the article number and the minimum. We order directly, track the delivery so it arrives before cutting, and inspect the fabric when it arrives.

items.question: If our approved fabric is discontinued before a repeat collection, can you source an alternative that preserves its drape, weight and print appearance?
items.answer: Yes. We let you know when you reorder, then source the closest replacement against the reference swatch we keep with your stored pattern, your approved sample or a previous shirt. We keep the same fibre type and stay within 10 GSM of the original weight. Matching the original Pantone reference doesn’t guarantee the same colour or hand feel on the new base, so you approve a swatch, a strike-off and, when needed, a new sample before bulk. We never substitute without your sign-off.

items.question: Which fabric choices push the price up, for example custom-dyed versus stock fabric, or certified versus conventional materials?
items.answer: Stock fabrics in existing colours cost the least. Custom-dyed and custom-developed fabrics cost more, and so do finer combed or long-staple yarns, heavier GSM, denser or more complex weaves and extra finishing treatments.

items.question: Does the 50-piece minimum apply to swimwear, and do jacquard, lurex or recycled swim fabrics need larger quantities?
items.answer: Yes. Swimwear in jacquard, lurex or recycled swim fabrics from our existing range starts at 50 pieces per style in each colour. Custom-developed jacquard or lurex starts at 1,000 metres per quality, and we confirm the exact minimum at sampling. We don’t custom-dye swim fabrics; the colours come from printing or from existing shades.

items.question: How do usable fabric width, one-way tropical prints and large repeats affect fabric consumption and material cost per shirt?
items.answer: A short-sleeve aloha shirt uses about 1.6–1.8 m at 140–150 cm usable width, against around 2.2–2.4 m at 110 cm, so wider cloth brings down your material cost per shirt. Large repeats or pattern matching take 10–15% more fabric, and we build that into your unit price.

blocks.heading: Garment Labels and Hang Tags, Direct From Our Factory
paragraphs: Aloha shirt orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, a minimum set for small and growing labels. We put your custom labels and hang tags on shirts we make ourselves in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

We agree first trial quantities with you case by case, within the limits production requirements set. A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days. Once you approve it and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

blocks.heading: Label and Hang Tag Sample Fees and Payment
paragraphs: Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order. You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

Our [factory and company](/about-us/) have been running since 2011, with production and export under one owner, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control. We manufacture for businesses (B2B) and sell only through this website and our own team. Every order is agreed with you directly, and there is no online shop or third-party marketplace store.
Our [product development service](/product-development/) handles both OEM and ODM work, so your new style starts from your own design, a picture or an idea.
With our [Sampling service](/sampling/), sample courier delivery costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee, and we also make mockups of your labels and packaging during sampling.
Our [ordering process](/our-process/) begins with a quotation. Once you agree to the price, we make the sample.
When you [contact our team](/contact-us/), you hear back within one business day, in English, and we're available by phone or video call at every step.
Our [Packaging service](/packaging/) covers hangtags, barcode stickers, logo cards, branded poly bags and printed cartons.

Alongside screen printing, our [Embroidery service](/embroidery/) offers custom shirt embroidery, including intricate work, plus embroidered patches and labels. Our skilled fashion designers prepare the designs.

In your [quote request](/request-a-quote/), keep confirmed logo files, repeat artwork, label artwork, care-label wording, packaging references and retail requirements separate from open decisions about fabric, print method, trims and fit corrections. That shows us what is settled and what still needs development.

Our [Private Label service](/private-label/) is available on every order, and your packaging proposal confirms the minimum for each technique. It covers woven main and neck labels, printed labels, heat-transfer care and size labels, hang tags, branded metal tags, logo application and silicone branding. We make woven labels and heat-transfer artwork in-house.

paragraphs: We develop your label artwork from the materials actually used in the garment, and you approve it before production. If a fabric or trim is substituted, we redraft the artwork and send it back for your sign-off. That way the label describes what is really sewn into the garment, including any change to the content declaration or care symbols.

For our [Custom Printing service](/custom-printing/), send your artwork at 300 DPI as PNG, JPG, JPEG, PSD, PDF, AI or EPS, or send us a reference sample. Vector EPS or AI files with outlined text and expanded strokes work best for us, and we also accept high-quality JPG or PDF files. We check every file for clarity, durability and compliance, then show you the layout to confirm before production.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which label types can you do: woven, printed satin or tagless heat-transfer for kids' and baby pieces?
items.answer: Our Private Label service offers woven labels, printed satin labels and heat-transfer care and size labels, and your packaging proposal confirms the minimum for each technique. Printed satin comes in white, black or cream, 15 to 40 mm wide, printed on one or both sides in up to 4 colours. We cut labels straight, or fold them at the centre or into a loop, for the neck, side seam or hem. You get a proof within 3 to 5 days, and we make the labels alongside your sample so they're ready before bulk cutting starts. For baby clothes, a soft printed satin loop at the side seam keeps the label away from the neck, where it rubs against the baby's skin, and it gives the hang tag's cotton string something to anchor to. The trade-off is that you lose the neck branding shoppers see when the garment is on a hanger or folded.

items.question: Can you print barcodes or UPCs on the hang tags, and how do you attach them safely to baby clothes?
items.answer: Yes. We print UPC or EAN barcodes on your hang tags from the barcode files you send us before packing, and we also print and apply FNSKU or UPC/EAN barcode labels to each polybag. On baby clothes, we attach each hang tag with a soft cotton string loop tied through the label inside the side seam, with no plastic tag pins or metal safety pins. Nothing sharp touches the skin, and a single snip takes the tag off cleanly.

items.question: Can you write the care, fibre content and country-of-origin text for the markets I sell in, or do I have to supply it?
items.answer: We draft the fibre content, care symbols and country of origin for each style from the fabric and trims actually used. We add your RN or CA number where it's needed and send you the artwork to sign off before production.

items.question: Which artwork file format and colour references do you need for labels and hang tags?
items.answer: We work from your artwork file, a Pantone reference, a hex code or an approved colour sample. Before you approve the mockup, we match your colours as closely as the fabric allows. Once you approve the sample, it becomes the standard for bulk production.

seo.title: Custom Buttons with Logo Engraving | Tapa Works
seo.description: Custom buttons for your aloha shirts: matched or contrasting colours, logo engraving and spare buttons for after-sales care.

hero.heading: Custom Buttons for Aloha Shirts
lead: We supply resin, shell, coconut, wood, metal and fabric-covered buttons to suit your design and fabric.

cta.label: Talk to us about custom buttons

blocks.heading: Shirt Buttons for Your Collection
paragraphs: Resin buttons make it easier to keep size, colour and supply consistent from your first bulk order through every reorder. We supply aloha shirt buttons in resin, urea, plastic, shell, coconut, wood, metal and fabric-covered types to suit your design, fabric and order. In resin, you can choose solid colours, horn-like or pearl-like finishes, or a custom colour you specify. Our button makers produce the custom buttons, and we sew them onto shirts made in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Button Materials, Finishes and Hidden Fastenings
columns: What we supply and what your choice means
rows: Resin buttons are cast from polyester resin. Plastic buttons are injection-moulded in ABS, nylon or acrylic and come in white, black, navy and clear.

If your volume range needs a uniform pearly look, we offer polyester resin layered with pearlescent pigment. Its lustre and colour stay the same from batch to batch. The trade-off is that you lose the natural iridescence and premium feel of genuine shell.

For private label and higher-end casual collections, genuine shell gives you a depth and play of light that resin can't fully copy. The trade-off is that colour won't be perfectly uniform across large runs.

Trochus is dense and white, with a soft pink-veined lustre. Freshwater mother-of-pearl has a milky white sheen. Black-lip shows grey to dark iridescence, and abalone gives a vivid green-blue play of colour.
You can choose polished, smooth or horn-like surfaces.
Coconut buttons are available for resort, tropical, linen and casual summer shirts.
Before bulk production starts, we check the washing method, coating and durability of the wooden buttons.
Finishes include shiny, matte, brushed, antique and black. Lightweight fabric can't hold metal buttons or snaps on its own, so those need backing support.
We make covered buttons from your matching, printed or contrast fabric.

Snaps fitted beneath a covered placket keep the fastenings out of sight and hold the front flat and closed so it doesn't gape. This works especially well on women's styles, fitted cuts and uniform aloha shirts. We test snap positions on your samples and use the placement you confirm in bulk production.

blocks.heading: Factory Ordering and Sourcing Options

items.heading: Shirt order minimum
paragraphs: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so small and growing labels have a set quantity to start from.

items.heading: First trial run
paragraphs: We agree each first trial run case by case, and production capacity sets its quantity.

items.heading: Direct factory ordering
paragraphs: As a [factory-owned B2B business](/about-us/), we handle both production and export, which gives you direct control over quality, cost and delivery. Orders are agreed through our website and team, not through an online shop or third-party marketplace.

items.heading: Your development starting point
paragraphs: [OEM and ODM development](/product-development/) can start from your own design, a picture or an idea for a new shirt style.

items.heading: Sourcing without garment production
paragraphs: Standalone [Fabric Sourcing](/fabric-sourcing/) starts at 300 metres per colour for stock or custom-dyed fabrics, and the trim minimums for garment orders still apply. Materials are inspected at our factory and shipped with reports and photos to your factory anywhere in the world, by express, air or sea, on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.

blocks.heading: Button Colour Matching and Logo Details

items.heading: Matched or contrasting colours
paragraphs: Our button maker dyes resin or plastic to match your fabric, or sets a contrast in a dark, light, horn-like or brand colour. The shade is confirmed before production, so you have an agreed reference for reorders.

items.heading: Natural material trade-off
paragraphs: Genuine shell, coconut and wood keep their natural tones and aren't custom dye-matched. Shell comes in white, smoked or dark tones, and wood in a light, medium or dark stain. An exact-match resin or plastic button loses their organic texture and grain.

items.heading: Surface finish choices
paragraphs: Depending on the material you pick, you can choose glossy, matte, smooth, horn-like, pearl-like, wood grain or engraved finishes.

items.heading: Sample logo checks
paragraphs: Before bulk production, we check the engraving depth, the button colour and how clearly your mark reads on the sample.

items.heading: Laser engraving options
paragraphs: Your logo can be laser-engraved on resin, urea, wood, coconut and shell buttons, using a method that suits the material.

items.heading: Moulded and metal marks
paragraphs: For branded detail, logos can be moulded into resin and plastic buttons, or die-stamped or engraved on metal buttons.

items.heading: Coloured logo printing
paragraphs: If your design calls for a coloured mark, we pad-print logos in one or two colours on resin, plastic and urea buttons.

blocks.heading: Button Sizes, Hole Patterns and Stitching
rows: For the front placket, you can choose 18L (approx. 11.5 mm) or 20L (approx. 12.5 mm).
Pockets take 16L (approx. 10 mm) or 18L buttons, so they stay in proportion with the front.
We scale collar and cuff buttons down from the front-placket size: 14L to 16L (9 to 10 mm) on the collar and 16L to 18L (10 to 11.5 mm) on the cuffs.
If you want a different proportion, you can pick any size from 14L to 24L. The front, collar and cuffs don't have to share the same size.
We choose the thickness to suit your fabric weight, your shirt style and how the shirt will be worn.

We develop button size and buttonhole length together, using the actual button chosen for each position, and we confirm the fit on your sample. If a hole is cut for a different diameter or thickness, the button slips out or is hard to push through, and the hole wears faster.

You can have two-hole buttons, or four-hole buttons sewn with a cross stitch, a parallel stitch or another pattern you approve. A cross stitch gives a neat finish and helps the buttons stay on through regular wear and washing. On heavy-use shirts, we confirm the thread quality and sewing strength.

With our [Cut & Sew service](/cut-sew/), your size-specific shirt panels go through assembly, buttonholes, button attachment, labelling, pressing and individual polybag packing, with inline checks along the way and a final inspection at the end.

blocks.heading: Spare Buttons for Customer Care
paragraphs: We can include one or more spare buttons with every shirt to support your after-sales service. If the spare is sewn inside the garment, or attached to or beside the care label, it stays with the shirt for its whole life, but the inside of the shirt is no longer as neat and unmarked. If it's packed separately in a small bag or polybag, or attached with the hang tag, the inside stays neat and unmarked, but when that packaging is thrown away, the spare goes with it. For retail shirts, sewing the spare into the garment keeps a replacement within your customer's reach.

visuals.purpose: Explain the trade-off between keeping the spare with the shirt and leaving the shirt's interior unmarked.
visuals.caption: Choosing how to include spare buttons.

rows.label: Spare retention

items.heading: Enquiries and communication

blocks.heading: Button Selection, Minimums and Quality Checks

steps.heading: Set your requirements
steps.text: Before sampling or bulk production, we pick button options based on your fabric, shirt style, quantity, preferred buttons, logo details and packing requirements.

steps.heading: Start with stock
steps.text: On a small or first run, a colour-matched stock button works at the garment minimum. It has no separate button minimum and no extra cost. The trade-off is that you don't get a branded logo or an exact custom shade.

steps.heading: Commit to custom lots
steps.text: Custom-dyed or logo-engraved buttons need 1,000 pieces per design in each colour, which is a minimum the button maker sets. Ordering that separate lot means you lose the low commitment of a small test order.

steps.heading: Keep surplus for reorders
steps.text: We store the spare buttons from your custom lot for your reorders, so you can keep using them once your style's volumes justify the separate button order.

steps.heading: Approve production details
steps.text: At sampling, we review the material, colour, size, thickness and sewing method with you. Only the button details you approve go into bulk production.

steps.heading: Check quality and compliance
steps.text: Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) covers inspections, function testing and access to SGS/BV. Our credentials cover tested fabrics and trims (OEKO-TEX Standard 100), organic cotton (GOTS), cotton sourcing (BCI), quality management (ISO 9001) and social compliance (WRAP).

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Will natural shell, coconut or wood buttons vary from piece to piece and between reorders, and how do you keep them consistent?
items.answer: Yes. Natural shell, coconut and wood vary slightly in colour, grain and pattern between pieces and between batches. For reorders, consistency means staying within your approved sample range. It doesn't mean every button looks identical. We sort shades against your sample so each batch stays within that range.

items.question: What usable engraving area and minimum text or line sizes can you achieve on each button size?
items.answer: On an 18L (11.5 mm) four-hole shirt button, you can engrave a ring about 2 mm wide around the holes. Shank and snap buttons give you a centre area of about 6 mm, and that grows to about 10 mm on 24L (15 mm) buttons and larger. For laser engraving, text and lines need to be at least 0.8 mm high and 0.2 mm wide. Moulded marks need to be at least 1.2 mm high. A simple mark, monogram or short wordmark works better on shirt-size buttons than full brand artwork. Fine lines and small text fill in or blur around the holes, and that makes the mark hard to read.

items.question: Can I order shank buttons or custom-shaped buttons instead of standard round two-hole or four-hole buttons?
items.answer: Yes. Besides round two-hole and four-hole buttons, we supply shank buttons, snaps and specialty styles, cut or moulded in square, oval, flower, leaf and logo-outline shapes from your drawing. Then we confirm the shape on your sample before bulk production.
