seo.title: Garment Dyeing for Aloha Shirts | Tapa Works
seo.description: Garment dyeing with colour matching, softening finishes and shrinkage control, so finished shirts stay on your size spec.

hero.heading: Garment Dyeing for Aloha Shirts
lead: Your shirts take colour evenly because we sew them from PFD fabric made for dyeing.

cta.label: Talk to us about garment dyeing

blocks.heading: Garment Dyed Shirts From Our Own Factory
paragraphs: Garment dyeing starts with shirts sewn from PFD (prepared for dye) fabric, the standard base for this process. We make your aloha shirts in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. The certified dyestuffs and silicone softeners we use are free from heavy metals, formaldehyde and banned azo compounds, and they meet OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Class I requirements. Before you order, we confirm which certificate covers each dye, softener and fabric. On request, we send you current copies so you can check them against your market's requirements.

blocks.heading: The right dye for each fabric
paragraphs: Before we choose a dye route, we confirm your fabric's exact fibre content from the mill specification.
columns: What it means for your shirts
rows: Cotton, rayon, linen and bamboo take reactive dyes. Silk, nylon and wool take acid dyes. Polyester and polyester blends take disperse dyes.
We garment dye cotton or rayon with up to 5% spandex, and nylon with up to 20% spandex. We control bath temperatures to protect the stretch, and nylon-spandex takes acid dyes.

Any mix of cotton, rayon and linen dyes evenly. A 65% polyester 35% cotton blend turns two-tone in a single bath, so it needs two-step disperse and reactive dyeing for uniform colour, and we agree this with you before sampling.

Your tech pack lists the finished shade of each thread and trim, and we test thread against fabric at sampling. Cotton thread dyes tone-on-tone with cotton, rayon or linen. Polyester thread, coconut or shell buttons and polyester woven labels keep their original colour.
This 110–130 gsm PFD base gives classic aloha styles a fluid, loose resort drape.
This 115–135 gsm PFD base gives tailored, uniform and camp-collar shirts a crisper structure.
These 150–180 gsm PFD bases give washed summer collections a textured, relaxed vintage feel.
As a [factory-owning company](/about-us/), we handle production and export ourselves, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.

Our [OEM and ODM product development](/product-development/) works from your design, picture or idea. Pattern design, grading and fit development all happen in-house, which cuts down the back-and-forth.

Our [shirt fabrics](/hawaiian-fabrics/) cover cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool, plus 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton blends.

blocks.heading: Choose Your Shade and Set the Colour Standard

items.heading: Base and colour together
paragraphs: You pick a standard colour, a physical swatch or a Pantone reference. We then check that your chosen fibre reaches that shade before you commit to the colour standard.

items.heading: Natural-fibre colour depth
paragraphs: Cotton, rayon and linen get their deepest tropical colours from reactive dyes, and direct dyes give them pale and pastel options. On silk and nylon, acid dyes give both brights and pastels.

items.heading: Softer colour limits
paragraphs: In garment-dye baths, polyester and polyester-rich blends reach light to mid shades, not the deepest brights. Pigment dyeing gives softer, washed-down tones.

items.heading: Repeat-order variation
paragraphs: Your reorder comes out very close to the earlier run but not identical to it, because batch-to-batch variation is part of garment dyeing.

items.heading: Lot acceptance standard
paragraphs: Shirts in the same bath match to Grade 4–5 on the grey scale. To pass, a lot must be within ΔE ≤ 2.0 of your approved sample under D65 light. We re-dye or set aside any outliers and send you comparison photos before shipment.

items.heading: Colourfastness minimums
paragraphs: Custom-dyed cotton and rayon reach Grade 4 or above for washing and Grade 3–4 or above for rubbing and light. Pigment-dyed shirts meet the same minimums.

items.heading: Dark-colour lab checks
paragraphs: For navy, black and deep red, we use reactive dyes. Before you approve bulk, we check washing fastness and wet and dry rubbing fastness on the lab dip.

items.heading: Fixing deep shades
paragraphs: Deep, saturated shades are the hardest to hold against rubbing, so dark colours get a colour-fixing after-treatment.

blocks.heading: Finishes that shape the feel

items.heading: Three finish choices
paragraphs: Choose solid garment dye if you want colour that stays rich wash after wash, washed if you want a washed finish, or pigment-dyed if you want colour that fades with wear.

items.heading: Softer shirt hand
paragraphs: Every garment-dyed shirt goes through a softening wash. We use light or heavy concentrations of silicone softener to give your shirts a super-soft, silky feel for many washes.

items.heading: Wash and vintage effects
paragraphs: On top of softening, we offer enzyme, stone, acid and mineral washes, sun-faded and vintage effects, and light distressing. You approve each effect on a sample first.

items.heading: Individual dye patterns
paragraphs: We also do dip-dye and tie-dye patterns, which you approve on a sample first. These finishes make each shirt slightly different from the next.

items.heading: Decoration timing matters
paragraphs: Embroidery and patches go on before dyeing to give a tone-on-tone vintage look. Placement screen prints and puff prints go on after dyeing so the graphics stay sharp.

blocks.heading: Plan for Shrinkage and Keep the Fit
rows: Your spec sheet gives the dimensions after dyeing. We cut the patterns oversized so the shirts shrink to the measurements you intended.
We allow 3–5% for cotton poplin, 5–8% for rayon and 4–6% for linen. A wash test on your sample fabric sets the exact figure.
Whenever you change the fabric base or supplier, we run a new wash test and adjust the pattern, even if the fibre stays the same.
Your shirts leave us dyed, washed and pre-shrunk. After three home washes, residual shrinkage stays within 3% in length and width.

During [Cut & Sew](/cut-sew/) sampling, we decide whether your collar and placket get lightweight fusible interlining, soft non-fused interlining or none. For lightweight rayon, we use 1 cm overlocked or French seams, tested to ISO 13936-2 to open no more than 6 mm.

blocks.heading: Colour approvals and style details

items.heading: Your actual fabric
paragraphs: We make lab dips on your actual shirt fabric, not on generic test cloth. The colour you approve becomes the bulk colour standard on the base you chose.

items.heading: Included colour approval
paragraphs: Pantone matching costs nothing extra, and you get one round of lab dips to approve before bulk production starts.

items.heading: Coordinated style colours
paragraphs: You pick from Pantone Coated cards or our in-stock colour cards, and we coordinate the colour across your fabric, lining and trims.

items.heading: Labels for your market
paragraphs: With [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/), we write the fibre content, origin and wash-tested care instructions to your destination's rules and add RN or CA numbers where they're required. You approve the artwork, and we check every private-label order.

items.heading: Printed collection options
paragraphs: [Custom Printing](/custom-printing/) covers roll printing on natural fabrics and sublimation on light polyester or on blends with at least 60% polyester. Screen repeats go up to 64 cm, and digital and sublimation repeats run the full 150 cm. Large repeats or pattern matching take 10–15% more fabric, and that cost is already in the price.

items.heading: Matching across fabric bases
paragraphs: For [Matching Family & Group Sets](/matching-family-group-sets/), the same Pantone looks different on polyester, rayon and cotton, so you approve each base side by side. We scale the artwork from toddler sizes up to 5XL and sample the whole set together.

items.heading: Button order quantities
paragraphs: [Custom Buttons](/custom-buttons/) need 1,000 pieces per design in each colour, whether custom-dyed or logo-engraved. We order them separately and store the spares for your reorders. Stock colour matches have no separate minimum, so they work with the 50-piece shirt minimum.

blocks.heading: From first sample to production
paragraphs: All garment production happens in our own factory, garment dyeing included, while the PFD base fabric comes from our partner mills.

steps.heading: Review your brief
steps.text: Before we quote, we confirm whether you want garment dyeing or pigment dyeing and review the substrate in your brief or tech pack.

steps.heading: Settle colour decisions
steps.text: We agree the colour references and get your approval on the swatch or lab dip before sampling. Lab dips add about 5 to 7 days to sampling.

steps.heading: Make your sample
steps.text: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days, and you get the shirt to review before you commit to bulk production.

steps.heading: Release bulk production
steps.text: Bulk production starts once you approve the sample and pay the deposit. The base schedule is 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

steps.heading: Dye and finish
steps.text: Garment dyeing adds 7 to 10 days to that bulk schedule for the extra dyeing and finishing work on your shirts.

steps.heading: Inspect and dispatch
steps.text: When production is finished, your order goes through final inspection before we release the shirts for shipment.

blocks.heading: Quotes and quantities for your order

items.heading: Minimum and bath size
items.text: Our minimum is 50 pieces per style in each colour. That fills one bath of about 10 kg, or roughly 50 short-sleeve shirts. There's no separate dye-bath minimum.

items.heading: Shared colours together
items.text: Order styles that share a colour at the same time and they go into the same bath. Larger quantities run across several baths of up to 100 kg each.

items.heading: First trial quantities
items.text: We agree first-trial quantities case by case, with as much flexibility as production allows for your order.

items.heading: Price before sampling
items.text: In [our order process](/our-process/), we quote first. Once you agree the price, we start making your sample.

items.heading: Direct factory contact
items.text: Our English-speaking [contact team](/contact-us/) replies within one business day, and you can reach them by phone or video call throughout your order.

blocks.heading: Costs, payments and checks before dispatch

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: You pay USD 50 for each sample and USD 50 for each design, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Payment split
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Sample courier cost
items.text: [Sample delivery](/sampling/) by courier costs USD 50, and you pay this on top of the sample fee.

items.heading: Pre-dispatch quality checks
items.text: Our [Quality Control](/quality-control/) covers a 100% final inspection over 2 to 3 days and pre-shipment sampling at AQL 2.5 for major defects and 4.0 for minor ones.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you overdye an already printed aloha shirt, or garment dye blank shirts that we send you?
items.answer: We overdye aloha shirts that we've printed in our own factory. The print softens into the new ground colour and gives a sun-faded, worn-in look. We only garment dye shirts we cut and sew ourselves, so we don't take in your blank or finished shirts for dyeing.

items.question: How many standard garment dye colours do you have, and can I get a physical colour card before I choose?
items.answer: Our standard range has 30 shades developed on our PFD shirt fabrics, from washed neutrals and earth tones to ocean blues, tropical brights and deep darks. If you ask, we post you a physical colour card with dyed swatches within 3 business days.

items.question: If my order needs more than one dye lot, how do you stop shirts of slightly different shades ending up mixed together on the shelf?
items.answer: We pack each dye lot separately by shade batch and mark every polybag and carton with its lot number, so different shade batches never share a carton. Every lot also gets its own entry on the packing list, which lets you store, shelve and ship lot by lot.

items.question: Which of my garment dyeing choices make the shirt cost more or less?
items.answer: Your quote itemises each choice: the dye route (reactive, acid, disperse or pigment), shade depth, two-step dyeing for mixed fibres, extra washes such as enzyme, stone or tie-dye, and heavy or light silicone softener. Runs close to the minimum of 50 pieces per colour per dye lot cost more per shirt than full production runs.

items.question: What kinds of aloha shirt collections is garment dyeing best for, and can I hold undyed shirts and dye colours as sales come in?
items.answer: We sew the shirts before we colour them, so garment dyeing suits vintage and lived-in resort lines, tonal solids and core styles you offer in many colours. We hold your sewn, undyed PFD shirts for up to 6 months, and you call off colours as sales develop, starting at 50 pieces per colour per dye lot. Each lot takes 7 to 10 days.

items.question: What quality problems typically come up with garment-dyed shirts, and what do you do to prevent them?
items.answer: The main risks are shrinkage and shade variation, so we compensate the patterns for shrinkage and pack shirts by shade batch. To prevent uneven dyeing and streaks, we scour every shirt before dyeing and load the machine at a fixed fabric-to-water ratio.

seo.title: Custom Printed Hawaiian Shirts: All-Over Prints | Tapa Works
seo.description: Custom printed Hawaiian shirts with logo or all-over printing, placement options and a sample to approve before bulk production.

hero.heading: Custom Printed Hawaiian Shirts
lead: Large all-over patterns and small detailed logos each get the method that renders them cleanly.

cta.label: Talk to us about custom printing

blocks.heading: Hawaiian Shirt Printing Options
paragraphs: You can choose from six printing methods for your aloha shirts: screen printing, sublimation, DTG (direct-to-garment), DTF (direct-to-film), HTV (heat transfer vinyl) and digital printing. When we consult with you, we look over your artwork and recommend the combination that fits your design. We make the shirts ourselves in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Create Distinctive Effects with Discharge, Puff, Foil and Reverse Printing

items.heading: Discharge printing
paragraphs: Discharge takes dye out of 100% cotton to give you a soft, vintage finish. The fabric's dye decides how much colour comes out, so we test your actual fabric lot before bulk.

items.heading: Puff and foil
paragraphs: Puff gives you raised texture. Foil adds gold, silver or custom-colour metallic accents on cotton, polyester, rayon or blends. We use both for spot details only, because large areas stiffen the shirt and wear faster in the wash.

items.heading: Reverse printing
paragraphs: We print on cotton so your design shows through from the back face of the fabric, which gives a muted, sun-faded look. We test the effect on your actual fabric lot before bulk.

items.heading: Direct factory orders
paragraphs: Our [factory-owned business](/about-us/) has been running since 2011. We work directly with business buyers worldwide and have no marketplace stores, so sewing, sublimation, production and export all stay under our control.

items.heading: Embroidery alongside print
paragraphs: Our [embroidery service](/embroidery/) adds designer-prepared, wash-resistant logos, intricate designs, patches and labels. It's only available on aloha shirts we cut and sew ourselves, not on finished shirts you send us.

blocks.heading: Which Printing Method Suits Your Logos and Artwork?
paragraphs: We pick a method based on how detailed your artwork is first and on order size second, because a low unit price can't make up for lost detail.
rows: Bold, solid-colour logos on cotton, polyester and blends, from a one-colour chest logo to a multicolour back graphic. Pantone ink matching and different press configurations support your design. Setup cost is spread across the quantity, so runs of around 500 units or more are the most economical fit.

High-resolution, photo-realistic artwork on cotton, polyester and blends. Production is fast, which suits small and medium runs and quick-turn projects, and the prints are durable and keep shirts lightweight.
Detailed, multicolour small batches on cotton and high-cotton blends, with the best results on 100% cotton. We use water-based inks and need no screen setup.
Tight schedules and almost any fabric type. A single transfer step removes per-colour setup.
Precision-cut names and bold one-colour logos on cotton, polyester or blends, with little setup. You can choose matte, glossy, metallic, reflective or glitter finishes.

Screen printing holds 0.3 mm lines, 6 pt text and 45 to 55 lpi halftones. HTV needs lines of at least 1.5 mm and letters 8 mm tall, and it can't print gradients. DTG and digital hold 0.2 mm lines and DTF holds 0.5 mm lines. All three reproduce continuous-tone gradients at up to 1,200 dpi.
Choosing DTG or DTF over screen printing saves you setup and time. In exchange, you give up screen printing's lower unit cost and exact Pantone spot-colour matching.

blocks.heading: All-Over Prints on Your Choice of Fabric
paragraphs: With all-over prints, your fabric decides the printing method, the colour you get and how the finished shirt drapes.
rows: Sublimation bonds dye into the polyester fibres instead of leaving a layer on the surface, so it can't crack or peel. Extra colours cost nothing. We use light-coloured fabrics only.

Blends need at least 60% polyester. A 60–65% polyester blend gives about 25–30% less colour depth than 100% polyester and has a heathered, vintage finish. For the brightest result, choose 85% polyester or more.
We screen-print rayon, cotton, linen and silk on the roll with repeats up to 64 cm. We can also print them digitally with repeats up to the full 150 cm printable width.

Screen and digital prints on rayon and cotton keep a soft, natural hand and rich colour that comes close to sublimation brightness. Screen printing gives the deepest spot colours, and rayon keeps its fluid drape. Sublimated polyester gives up that natural softness for slightly brighter colours and a smoother, crisper, more synthetic feel.

Our [Hawaiian Fabrics service](/hawaiian-fabrics/) supplies library or custom prints from 300 metres per colourway. They come in rolls of about 50 to 100 metres, each inspected for shade, defects and width and sealed on cores for export.

blocks.heading: Plan Your Print Size, Placement and Pattern Matching
paragraphs: For DTG, DTF and HTV prints, we keep your artwork clear of the button placket so the shirt closes neatly.

items.heading: Continuous repeat patterns
paragraphs: We print the fabric on the roll before cutting, so repeats match across seams, collars, plackets, pockets and hems. The trade-off is that a continuous pattern can't put a single motif in exactly the same spot on every shirt.

items.heading: Fixed motif placement
paragraphs: We cut the panels first, print each one and then sew, so your motif sits in the same position on every shirt. Sublimation transfer on polyester is one way to do this.

items.heading: DTG print areas
paragraphs: DTG prints up to 40 x 50 cm on your front panels, the full back, the left chest or the sleeves.

items.heading: DTF transfer areas
paragraphs: DTF transfers go up to 50 x 60 cm and can also go on the back yoke, sleeves, pocket or near the hem.

items.heading: HTV placement options
paragraphs: HTV covers up to 30 x 40 cm for chest, back or sleeve designs, including names and numbers.

blocks.heading: Prepare Your Artwork, Colours and Branding for Print

items.heading: Artwork files
paragraphs: Send your artwork at 300 DPI as PNG, JPG, JPEG, PSD, PDF, AI, EPS or TIFF, or send us a reference sample. We prefer vector AI or EPS files with the text outlined and the strokes expanded.

items.heading: File and layout review
paragraphs: We check every file for clarity, durability and compliance, then show you the design layout to confirm before production starts.

items.heading: Colour references
paragraphs: Before you approve the mockup, we match your artwork, Pantone reference, hex code or approved colour sample as closely as the fabric allows. Once you approve a sample, it becomes the standard for bulk.

items.heading: Approved care labels
paragraphs: Our [Custom Labels & Hang Tags service](/custom-labels-hang-tags/) prepares content, care and origin artwork that meets the rules of your destination market, based on your actual materials and wash tests. We add your RN or CA number where it's needed, get your approval and check every private-label order.

items.heading: Actual-fabric strike-offs
paragraphs: Rayon, cotton, polyester and stretch fabrics each reproduce the same colour differently. That's why we adjust repeat, scale and placement, calibrate colours on stretch fabrics and ask you to approve a physical strike-off.

items.heading: Branding methods
paragraphs: You can choose screen printing in up to 12 colours, soft-hand DTF in unlimited colours, embroidery, heat transfer, silicone printing or sewn-on labels.

items.heading: Garment add-ons
paragraphs: Our [customisation service](/customization/) offers placement printing, extra pockets and hi-vis tape. Placement printing and pockets are also available as add-ons on standard shirts.

blocks.heading: Bring Your Shirt Ideas to Life with Our Design Team
rows: We plan the collar, short sleeves, front and back together instead of treating your design as one flat tile. That way no motifs get cut off at the seams and the finished shirt looks balanced. Your design doesn't have to be floral.

Our [product development team](/product-development/) takes on OEM and ODM projects starting from your design, a picture or just an idea. Pattern design, grading and fit development all happen in-house, which means less back-and-forth.
Our [confidentiality terms](/terms-and-conditions/) include an NDA. Patterns we develop from your artwork stay your intellectual property, and we can't sell your exclusive print to another client.

Under [our process](/our-process/), we agree on price before sampling. After that, fabric, sewing, decoration and finishing all run on one timeline with one contact, and production management and quality control are coordinated across all of them. You can also talk directly with the production side.
Our English-speaking [team](/contact-us/) is available by phone or video for your whole project and replies to enquiries within one business day.

blocks.heading: Order Minimums and Your Production Timeline

items.heading: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which works for small and growing labels.

items.heading: First trial run
items.text: We agree on your first trial quantity case by case. How flexible we can be depends on what production allows.

items.heading: Library print trials
items.text: Prints from our existing library have no extra minimum, so you can test a style without committing to a custom print. The catch is that the artwork isn't exclusive to your brand.

items.heading: Custom sublimation minimum
items.text: Custom sublimation starts at 50 pieces per print. That's the print-specific commitment for your own design.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Bulk production takes 35 to 40 days after sample approval and deposit. Your order size and the season decide where it falls in that range.

items.heading: Approved-style reorders
items.text: Our [bulk-production reorders](/bulk-production/) skip sampling, keep the same minimum and take 35 to 40 days after deposit. Reprints from archived files match your original approved sample within ΔE ≤ 2.0.

blocks.heading: Your Quote, Payment and Delivery Options

items.heading: Itemised setup costs
items.text: We quote any screen or plate setup that applies separately for each print and method. The quote shows which costs are one-off and which are per shirt, and we get your approval before we charge anything.

items.heading: Setup on reorders
items.text: You pay setup once. When you reorder an approved style, we reuse the archived print files, colour profiles and stored logo digitising files, so there's no second setup charge.

items.heading: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Delivery terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Quote preparation
items.text: Send us your fabric, artwork, colour direction, quantities and delivery schedule, and we'll prepare [a quote](/request-a-quote/) covering sizing, printing, design, labels, packing, sampling and bulk-pricing options.

blocks.heading: Approve Your Sample and Check the Print Before Production
paragraphs: We make your pre-production sample in the fabric and printing method you've chosen, so you can review and approve it. For screen-printed orders, you sign off a physical print sample before bulk printing starts.

During bulk printing, we compare every roll against that approved sample. We check for white crease streaks, bleeding between neighbouring colours, misregistration and shade changes along the roll. Long runs show defects that a single sample doesn't, so we check on the line to keep your colour consistent.

blocks.heading: What Will Your Sample Cost and When Will It Be Ready?
paragraphs: Your standard sample costs USD 50 and is ready in 10 to 15 days.

items.heading: Design fee
items.text: We charge USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print and all its colourways.

items.heading: Non-refundable fees
items.text: Sample and design fees aren't refunded, and they aren't credited against your bulk production order later.

items.heading: Delivery and review
items.text: With [sampling](/sampling/), you pay USD 50 for courier delivery on top of the sample fee. You then check the drape, collar, sleeves, print scale and shrinkage risk before you approve bulk.

blocks.heading: Quality Checks from Printed Fabric to Finished Shirts
paragraphs: We inspect your printed fabric as flat panels before cutting and sewing. We reprint anything below standard and move your order to the front of production.

items.heading: Earlier fault correction
items.text: Reprinting flat fabric is quicker than remaking sewn garments, so corrections don't hold up the rest of your order.

items.heading: Inspection coverage
items.text: Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers incoming fabric, cutting, sewing and random checks. A 100% final inspection follows and takes 2 to 3 days.

items.heading: Pre-shipment evidence
items.text: We sample against your approved sample at AQL 2.5 for major defects and AQL 4.0 for minor ones. We share measurement logs and photos with you, and SGS or BV inspectors are welcome.

items.heading: Measurement tolerances
items.text: Finished chest, length and waist measurements stay within ±1 cm of your chart. Collars, cuffs and other small points stay within ±0.5 cm.

items.heading: Fabric performance
items.text: Preshrunk fabrics keep shrinkage within 3% after three home washes. Washing colourfastness reaches Grade 4 or above, including on high-twist chiffon, and rubbing and light colourfastness reach Grade 3–4 or above.

items.heading: Certification scope
items.text: Our coverage includes OEKO-TEX Standard 100 tested fabrics and trims, GOTS organic cotton, BCI cotton sourcing, ISO 9001, WRAP, BSCI, OCS and GRS recycled polyester. Before you order, we confirm which of these apply to your style.

items.heading: Certificate documentation
items.text: We send current certificates on request, and for certified recycled prints we request each [GRS Transaction Certificate](/about-us/) from our certification body. For plain colours, we use OEKO-TEX certified dyes.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Are your screen and DTF inks plastisol or water-based, PVC- and phthalate-free, and do the prints meet OEKO-TEX or children's product requirements?
items.answer: Our standard screen inks are water-based. For opaque prints on dark grounds, we offer PVC-free, phthalate-free plastisol. DTF prints use water-based pigment inks. If you need OEKO-TEX Standard 100 compliant formulations, we can supply them on request.

items.question: Within the same printing method, which artwork choices—such as print dimensions, separate print locations, spot colours or white underbases—change production cost?
items.answer: Larger prints and extra locations cost you more, because each location needs its own setup and printing pass. With screen printing, each screen and spot colour has a one-off charge that's spread across your quantity. On dark shirts, a white underbase adds a screen or an ink layer. DTF, DTG and digital need no screens, so only size and locations affect the cost. We recommend screen printing for designs with few colours on longer runs, and DTF for designs with many colours on short runs. DTF saves you the screen costs, but it leaves a thin film on the surface instead of the softer, absorbed-ink feel you get from screen printing.

items.question: What positioning tolerance can you hold for a chest logo relative to the pocket or placket across the production run?
items.answer: Throughout production, your chest logo stays within 0.5 cm of where it sits on your approved sample, measured from the pocket edge or placket.

items.question: What wash-durability and rubbing-colourfastness standards can you meet for screen, digital, DTG, DTF and HTV prints?
items.answer: We test washing to ISO 105-C06 and rubbing to ISO 105-X12. Screen, DTF and HTV prints last at least 50 home washes at 40°C. DTG prints last at least 30 washes.

seo.title: About Us | Direct Supply | Tapa Works
seo.description: About Tapa Works: we make aloha shirts in our own Guangzhou factory: who we are, the programmes we run for brands and teams, and how we supply direct.

hero.heading: Meet the company behind your aloha shirt programme
lead: A long-running factory stands behind your program. We make every shirt ourselves rather than subcontracting.

cta.label: Contact us

blocks.heading: Meet Tapa Works: Your Direct Factory Partner
paragraphs: We make your aloha shirts ourselves, in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, which has been running since 2011. You buy straight from the maker at factory-direct prices, whether you need wholesale, private label, OEM or ODM services. We work only with business buyers, through this website and our team. We don't run an online shop or a store on any third-party marketplace, so you agree every order directly with us.

blocks.heading: Shirt Programmes for Brands and Teams
paragraphs: Before we quote, we ask what your shirts are for: resale, staff uniforms, promotion or an event. Then we match the labels, sizes and packaging to that use.

items.heading: Collections for resale
paragraphs: For fashion brands, resort brands, boutiques, wholesalers, distributors, retailers and e-commerce sellers, we develop collections built around the fabrics, prints, sizes, labels and packaging you choose.

items.heading: Staff and branded apparel
paragraphs: For hotels, resorts, companies and schools, we make corporate shirts, uniforms and branded apparel, with specifications set around your programme.

items.heading: Events and groups
paragraphs: We've made tens of thousands of custom shirts worldwide for military units, clubs, corporate teams, events, communities and other groups, as well as for family programmes.

blocks.heading: Our Brand Experience and Confidential Case Studies
paragraphs: Right now we produce for more than 350 independent labels around the world. If you'd like to see evidence of comparable work before you order, we'll share released case examples, but only with those labels' permission. Because of our NDA commitments, we never show you another client's unreleased designs.

blocks.heading: Orders Outside Our Production Scope
paragraphs: We spot requests that fall outside our production scope at the enquiry stage, so we don't accept an order that isn't a good fit.

items.heading: Commodity pricing
items.text: If you're buying ultra-cheap commodity shirts, we're not the right maker for you.

items.heading: Sample coverage
items.text: One sample doesn't cover every fabric and fit you use in later production.

items.heading: Exact colour claims
items.text: We don't accept orders that require an exact colour guarantee before you've approved a sample.

items.heading: Heavy embellishment
items.text: We don't accept heavily embellished programmes unless the timeline leaves room for sampling.

items.heading: Structured formalwear
items.text: Structured formalwear falls outside our resort-wear production scope, so we don't take those orders.

blocks.heading: Our People and Production Under One Roof
paragraphs: Our team is more than 290 people strong, with over 110 garment sewers on the production floor. Sampling happens in a separate, dedicated studio with 62 staff: 7 pattern makers, 20 sample sewists, 4 graphic artists, 11 product development coordinators and 20 assistants. During development, a coordinator puts you in touch with the pattern makers and sample sewists.

Our experienced workforce runs modern production equipment and works with buyers every day on manufacturing and quality control. Production and export both sit within one company that owns the factory, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.

visuals.purpose: Show how the sampling studio’s staff are distributed across development roles.

paragraphs: We handle everything in-house: fabric selection and sourcing, artwork and logo work, design development, sampling, pattern making, cutting, sublimation printing, bulk sewing, finishing, inspection and packing, and we arrange export shipping with our forwarding partners. We do not subcontract garment production to outside workshops; partner mills weave and dye the fabric, button makers produce custom buttons and forwarders carry the freight, with our team coordinating each of them. Since printing and sewing share one roof, we plan your print layouts against the cut patterns, so motifs line up across the front placket, pocket and seams.

blocks.heading: Development Support, Samples and Order Minimums

items.heading: Full-package development
paragraphs: Our full-package service gives you help with your tech pack and fit development, and we get your approval on the fit sample before we grade sizes or start bulk production.

items.heading: Programme finishing options
paragraphs: Full-package programmes can include sustainable production, private label branding and eco-friendly packaging, and we support your logistics through global shipping.

items.heading: Bulk production
paragraphs: [Bulk Production](/bulk-production/) starts at 50 pieces per style per colour, and trial quantities depend on the production. Our 5,800-square-metre floor has 13 production lines, 6 automatic cutting lines and over 580 sewing machines, and it runs 24/7 when required. Production takes 35–40 days after sample approval and deposit, depending on size and season.

items.heading: Sampling costs and timing
paragraphs: [Sampling](/sampling/) takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50 per sample plus USD 50 per design for its pattern or print, covering all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Your design ownership
paragraphs: Under our [confidentiality terms](/terms-and-conditions/), we sign an NDA that protects your designs and business information, you keep ownership of aloha patterns developed from your artwork, and we're prohibited from selling your exclusive prints to other clients.

blocks.heading: Production Certifications and Social Compliance

items.heading: Certified materials
items.text: Our production is GRS certified for recycled polyester and OCS certified for organic content.

items.heading: Transaction Certificates
items.text: When you sell recycled polyester or organic styles with a certified claim, we apply to our certification body, which issues the Transaction Certificate for those goods.

items.heading: Social compliance
items.text: Our production is BSCI approved for social compliance and has passed a SMETA ethical audit.

blocks.heading: Check Our Certificates and Their Scope

items.heading: Style-specific coverage
items.text: Before you order, we match every fabric, trim, dye and ink in your style to the certificate that actually covers it.

items.heading: Documents for verification
items.text: On request, we email your compliance team current certificate PDFs, certificate numbers and scope annexes, so they can check validity with the issuing bodies.

items.heading: Company and factory identity
items.text: Our certificates cover our company and its single factory, and its registered name and full address appear on every quotation and proforma invoice.

items.heading: Tested fabrics and trims
items.text: Our OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification covers tested fabrics and trims, and we check that coverage against your style.

items.heading: Organic cotton styles
items.text: For organic cotton styles, we hold GOTS certification and confirm that it applies before you place your order.

items.heading: Additional management standards
items.text: We also hold WRAP for social compliance and ISO 9001 for quality management.

items.heading: Cotton sourcing
items.text: For cotton sourcing, we source Better Cotton (BCI) and give you the supporting documents for your compliance review.

blocks.heading: Factory Visits and Independent Audits
paragraphs: An on-site assessment lets you inspect the production floor and materials in person. You can visit the factory or run your own independent social or quality audit. Either one needs at least 5 business days' notice. For a faster first look, a remote assessment gives you a live video walkthrough or a 3D virtual tour. For formal supplier evaluations, we share our SMETA audit records.

mainEntity.name: What are your working hours and time zone, and do you close for any long holidays?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work Monday to Saturday, 9:00-18:00 China Standard Time (UTC+8). We close for about 15 days around Chinese New Year and for 7 days over the National Day holiday in early October. We post the exact closing dates at least 30 days ahead so you can plan samples and bulk orders around them. Confirm your samples and bulk orders well before these closures so confirmation stays clear of the shutdown, especially at Chinese New Year. Fabric mills, trim suppliers and logistics partners close around the same holidays and restart slowly afterwards. When a late-confirmed order is held up by those shutdowns and restarts, its delay runs beyond our own closing days.

mainEntity.name: Can I write to you in a language other than English?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Besides English, you can write to us in Chinese, Spanish, French or German, and we answer in those languages. Every quotation, tech pack and order confirmation we send you is in English, so both of us work from one shared reference.

mainEntity.name: How can I send large design files that are too big for an email attachment?

acceptedAnswer.text: For files over 20 MB, send us a download link through Google Drive, Dropbox or WeTransfer and keep it active for at least 7 days. We accept artwork as PNG, JPG, JPEG, PSD, PDF, AI, EPS and 300 dpi TIFF. Once every file has downloaded and opened correctly, we confirm by email.

seo.title: Our Process: From Quote to Shipment | Tapa Works
seo.description: Our Process at Tapa Works: from quote to shipment, with sampling, bulk production, quality checks and delivery terms.

hero.heading: Our Process from Quote to Shipment
lead: One dedicated account manager carries your order from brief to shipment.

cta.label: Request a Quote

blocks.heading: Meet the Team at Tapa Works
paragraphs: We cut and sew every garment in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. The team that develops your styles is the same team that cuts and sews your bulk order, so you talk directly to the people making your shirts, with no middlemen. Your dedicated account manager is your one contact from brief to shipment. We plan embroidery, printing and finishing alongside fabric and sewing, all under one timeline and one production management and quality control process. You can also speak directly with our production team about sizing, fabric, labels, logo work, packing and timing.

blocks.heading: Start With a Quote and Sample
paragraphs: We quote first, make your sample once you've agreed the price, and use your sample approval to set the quality standard before your bulk order.
rows: Your standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days.
Our [OEM and ODM product development](/product-development/) starts from your design, picture or idea. In-house pattern design, grading and fit development cut down the back-and-forth on design.

Our [fabric options](/hawaiian-fabrics/) cover cotton, polyester, spandex, nylon, rayon, viscose, modal, Tencel, linen, silk and wool, plus blends including 95% cotton 5% spandex, 80% nylon 20% spandex and 65% polyester 35% cotton.

Our [sampling fees](/sampling/) are USD 50 per sample and USD 50 per design (its pattern or print, including all colourways). Neither fee is refunded or credited against bulk orders, and you pay USD 50 for courier delivery.
We reply to every [enquiry](/contact-us/) within one business day.

blocks.heading: Approve the Details and Confirm Your Order
paragraphs: Our [bulk orders](/bulk-production/) start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, and we agree first-trial quantities case by case within production limits.

steps.heading: Technical preparation
steps.text: We start with a consultation and technical review, then build the tech pack that defines your project.

steps.heading: Style and materials
steps.text: You choose the silhouette, sleeve, length, size range, fabric, print method, artwork, labels, buttons and packaging, and we source the materials.

steps.heading: Print confirmation
steps.text: We confirm the scale of your artwork and check the print on a real garment before you approve the sample.

steps.heading: Sample approval
steps.text: You review the sample and any revisions until the design, fabric, fit and branding are approved, so changes are settled before they reach the whole run.

steps.heading: Separate bulk approval
steps.text: You then sign off, separately, the quantity, size split, quality checkpoints, carton packing and shipping terms on the final design. We don't start bulk cutting until both approvals are complete.

steps.heading: Order payment
steps.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

blocks.heading: Plan Your Production and Delivery Timeline
paragraphs: We plan backwards from your stock date. The deadline that sets how much time is left for production and transit is sample approval, not shipment.

items.heading: Schedule allowance
items.text: Once you've approved the sample and paid the deposit, production and transit leave no spare time in the schedule, so your allowance sits before approval.

items.heading: Launch deadline
items.text: For a summer or resort launch, approve samples and pay the deposit at least 90 days before you need the goods in your warehouse.

items.heading: Peak production season
items.text: If you order during the January–April peak, you need to approve the sample and pay the deposit earlier than that minimum lead time.

items.heading: Bulk production window
items.text: Once we have your sample approval and deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

items.heading: Sea transit allowance
items.text: Sea delivery to the US or Europe takes about 25 to 35 days, plus another 1 to 2 weeks in peak shipping months.

items.heading: May store stock
items.text: To have stock in your stores in May, approve samples by mid-January. That gives you the planning allowance for production and delivery.

items.heading: Timeline agreement
items.text: We go through timing with you before you confirm the order and agree your production timeline before manufacturing starts.

items.heading: Project timing factors
items.text: The time your project needs depends on fabric availability, how ready your artwork is, the trims you choose and the shipping method.

blocks.heading: Track Production, Quality Checks and Shipment
paragraphs: We look after your custom shirts from design and material sourcing, through garment production, to packing and dispatch, and we keep you informed the whole way.
columns: What it means for your order
rows: Before cutting, we print rayon, cotton, linen and silk on the roll by screen or digital printing, and placement prints go on cut panels.
We check your garments before ironing and packing, so we find faults while they can still be fixed.
You get photos from us at every stage. We monitor progress and warn you in advance about any risk to your deadline.

Our [quality control](/quality-control/) covers incoming fabric, cutting, sewing, random checks and a full final inspection. You're welcome to have SGS or BV carry out an independent pre-shipment inspection. It also includes OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GOTS for organic cotton styles, BCI for cotton sourcing, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.
[We ship](/shipping/) on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.
As soon as your order ships, we send you its tracking number.

blocks.heading: Explore More About Tapa Works

items.heading: Company structure
items.text: We own our factory, so our [production and export company](/about-us/) keeps quality, cost and delivery under our direct control.

items.heading: Factory history
items.text: Our [factory](/about-us/) has been running since 2011, and we serve business buyers around the world.

items.heading: Direct business orders
items.text: You order through our [B2B sales channels](/about-us/), which are this website and our team only. We have no online shop or third-party marketplace store, and we agree every order directly with you.

blocks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Is there an extra charge for rush production or a rushed sample?
items.answer: A close launch date can move your order onto an expedited lane, whose ship date we fix with you when we quote, and we rush samples when our schedule allows. The rush surcharge is quoted as a percentage of the order value before you confirm and is paid with the deposit.

items.question: How can I pay the deposit and balance (bank transfer or other methods), and which currencies do you invoice in?
items.answer: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment, and sample and design fees are paid before sampling starts. We invoice in USD and accept T/T bank transfer, and you can also pay sample fees by PayPal.

items.question: When do I need to place and ship my order so the aloha shirts reach my stores before the summer resort season?
items.answer: For a summer or resort launch, confirm your samples and pay the deposit at least 90 days before you need the goods in your warehouse, and earlier if you order in the January–April peak. That covers 35 to 40 days of bulk production plus about 25 to 35 days by sea to the US or Europe, which can stretch by 1 to 2 weeks in peak shipping months, so for May stock in your stores we suggest approving samples by mid-January.

blocks.heading: How We Handle Your Information
paragraphs: This page explains what information Tapa Works collects through this website and how we use it. When you send an enquiry or request a quote, we collect your name, company, email, any phone number and your message. We use them only to reply, prepare your quote and samples, and run your order. We do not sell your details or share them outside our team, except with couriers and inspection agencies an order needs. Artwork you send stays confidential under our [Terms and Conditions](/terms-and-conditions/). To see, correct or delete your information, email our team.

seo.description: Terms and Conditions for Tapa Works orders: production lead times, sample costs, payment milestones and design confidentiality.

hero.heading: Understand your order timelines, costs and payment terms

cta.label: Contact us

blocks.heading: Our Factory and Minimum Orders
paragraphs: You can order aloha shirts from 50 pieces per style in each colour, a minimum we set with small and growing labels in mind. We make them ourselves in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. For a first trial order, we agree the quantity with you case by case, within what our production requirements allow.

We invoice in USD and take T/T bank transfer. You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment. You pay sample and design fees before sampling starts, and you can also pay these fees by PayPal.

visuals.purpose: Show how the bulk-order payment is divided and when each payment is due.
visuals.caption: Payments are invoiced in USD and made by T/T bank transfer.

blocks.heading: Production Schedules and Delivery Options

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you've approved the sample and we've received your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season decide where it falls in that range.

items.heading: Delivery terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms, and DDP is available worldwide.

items.heading: DDP costs and handling
items.text: [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.heading: Direct ordering only
items.text: We work as a [B2B manufacturer](/about-us/) and sell only through this website and our team. You agree every order with us directly. We have no online shop, third-party marketplace or platform store.

blocks.heading: Sample Fees and Preparation Times
paragraphs: Sample and design fees aren't refunded, and we don't credit them against your bulk order.

items.heading: Sample fee
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. This is charged separately from the design fee and the courier delivery charge.

items.heading: Design fee
items.text: You pay USD 50 per design. That covers its pattern or print, with all colourways included.

items.heading: Preparation and courier
items.text: Your [standard sample](/sampling/) is ready in 10 to 15 days, and courier delivery costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

blocks.heading: Order Stages and Payment Schedule
paragraphs: Our [order process](/our-process/) has a 10 to 15 day sample stage and 35 to 40 days of bulk production.

steps.heading: Brief and quotation
steps.text: You send us your brief or tech pack and we quote first. Once you agree to the price, we make the sample.

steps.heading: Approval and deposit
steps.text: You approve the sample and pay the deposit to confirm the order, and then we start bulk production.

steps.heading: Balance and shipment
steps.text: We do the final inspection before dispatch. You pay the remaining balance before we ship on the delivery terms you agreed.

blocks.heading: Confidentiality and Ownership of Your Designs
paragraphs: We sign a non-disclosure agreement with you before you send any artwork, so your designs and business information stay confidential. That agreement is in place before your designs reach our design and sampling teams.

Any aloha pattern we develop from your artwork stays your intellectual property. We keep a record of which patterns are exclusive to you, so they never appear in our catalogue and are never offered or sold to another client. Because that exclusivity record is clear, your print isn't reused by mistake.

blocks.heading: Quality Checks and Support After Delivery

items.heading: Checks throughout production
items.text: Our [quality checks](/quality-control/) cover incoming fabric, cutting, sewing, random checks and a full final inspection. You're welcome to bring in independent inspectors such as SGS or BV before shipment.

items.heading: Inspection records
items.text: We keep inspection records for every order. When you send us photos or videos, we compare them against those records to tell production defects apart from transit damage, without long back-and-forth.

items.heading: After-delivery contact
items.text: We stay in touch after delivery and act quickly if your goods arrive damaged or have any other issue.

items.heading: Reporting a problem
items.text: If you find a quality problem, let us know within 7 days of delivery and send photos or videos that show it.

items.heading: Solution within 24 hours
items.text: We review your case and come back to you with a solution within 24 hours. Depending on the issue, that's a repair, remake, replacement, discount or credit.

seo.title: Request a Quote – Bulk Pricing | Tapa Works
seo.description: Request a Quote from Tapa Works: minimum quantities, sample fees and payment terms, and what we need to price your order.

hero.heading: Get a quote for your production order
lead: Your quote comes back exact when you send style IDs and expected quantities.

cta.label: Prefer email? Contact us

blocks.heading: Order Minimums and Trial Runs
paragraphs: Our garment orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so small and growing labels can order with us. We agree first trial runs case by case, and we flex quantities only as far as production allows.

To make the minimum-quantity calculation clear before we price samples or bulk, send us your product categories, exact style IDs, expected units for each style and colour, and your size range. Before quoting, we also confirm your print scale and what you need from the sample.

blocks.heading: What We Need to Prepare Your Quote
paragraphs: We also need the following in your quote brief so we can account for your market, delivery requirements and shipping responsibilities.

items.heading: Artwork or references
items.text: Send your artwork or reference images so we have the design information to prepare an accurate quote.

items.heading: Destination and channel
items.text: As part of your product brief, tell us your destination country and market, along with your retail channel.

items.heading: Delivery target
items.text: Give us your target delivery date or delivery window so your brief states when you need the order.

items.heading: Shipping term
items.text: Tell us whether you want FOB, CIF or DDP, and we'll talk them through with you before quoting. The term you choose affects landed cost, carton planning, customs responsibility and the format of your quote.

items.heading: Without freight support
items.text: If you don't have a freight forwarder or customs broker in the destination market, DDP gives you one delivered price instead of freight arrangements to manage.

items.heading: With freight support
items.text: If you already work with a freight forwarder or customs broker in the destination market, FOB keeps those arrangements with your existing provider.

items.heading: DDP trade-off
items.text: Choosing DDP over FOB gets you one delivered price, and in exchange you give up your choice of forwarder and direct control of freight costs.

items.heading: Overall cost comparison
items.text: Who clears customs and pays destination duties decides which shipping term costs you less overall and which is simpler for you to manage.

blocks.heading: Preparing Your Design and Planning Samples
paragraphs: Before we plan your samples, we separate the design decisions you've confirmed from the development questions that are still open.

steps.heading: Identify confirmed details
steps.text: Mark your logo files, repeat artwork, label artwork, care-label wording, packaging references and retail requirements as confirmed wherever those decisions are already settled.

steps.heading: Identify open decisions
steps.text: Let us know which choices are still open, including fabric, print method, trims and fit corrections, so we can work through them in sample rounds.

steps.heading: Review design requirements
steps.text: Send us your fabric choice and colour direction. We then go through your brief with you, covering sizing, fabric, printing method, design direction, private labelling and packing.

steps.heading: Lock settled items
steps.text: We lock the confirmed details first, then settle the open items one at a time. If several items change in one sample, nobody can tell which change fixed or caused a problem.

steps.heading: Plan sample development
steps.text: Once we've reviewed the requirements with you, we map out a sampling route and bulk pricing options.

blocks.heading: When Your Quote Arrives and What It Covers
paragraphs: Your quote is ready within 24 hours of us receiving your style information.

items.heading: Accepted style information
items.text: For each style, send spec sheets, sketches, a tech pack or detailed photos. A description of the garment type, sizes and quantities works too.

items.heading: Quote calculation
items.text: We work out your quote from the style, fabric, quantity, size range and customisation, based on the details you give us.

items.heading: Enquiry reply
items.text: Our reply includes fabric recommendations, a timeline and pricing broken down by style, so you have what you need to review your range.

items.heading: Separate style prices
items.text: Each style has its own price line, so you can drop, add or change one style without a full requote.

items.heading: Price validity
items.text: Your quoted price stays valid for 30 days from the date we issue it, and that is the period the quote covers.

items.heading: Before sampling
items.text: We always quote before making any sample.

blocks.heading: How Bulk Prices and Payments Work
paragraphs: We price bulk after checking your design and fabric against real production needs. Cost depends on construction, fabric availability, lining, print method, logo application, labels, packaging, size ratio and lead time, and we'll show which small tweaks reach your target without changing the core design.
An itemised quote is obligation-free. You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

visuals.purpose: Show how the bulk payment is divided and when each part is due.
visuals.caption: Half is paid at order confirmation; the balance is paid before shipment.

blocks.heading: Sample Charges and Other Costs
paragraphs: At the sampling stage, we'll point out which excluded extras apply to your style, so you can budget for development.

items.heading: Sample charge
items.text: Each sample is USD 50. We don't refund this fee or credit it against your bulk production order.

items.heading: Design charge
items.text: Each design is USD 50, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. It isn't refunded or credited against bulk.

items.heading: Separate development pricing
items.text: If pattern and sample development charges apply, we quote them separately and don't fold them into the bulk price.

items.heading: Materials and colour work
items.text: Materials, trims and swatches aren't part of the quoted charges unless your quote lists them.

items.heading: Decoration and setup
items.text: Decoration and setup aren't included unless they're listed in your quote, and we'll point out the extras that apply during sampling.

items.heading: Additional development costs
items.text: Further revisions, extra samples, freight and testing are excluded too, unless your quote specifically lists them as included.

items.heading: Approval before spending
items.text: We always check with you before taking on any additional cost, so nothing extra is spent without your agreement.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: When is the sample fee refunded: when I place the bulk order, or only above a certain quantity?
items.answer: We don't refund the sample fee or credit it against a bulk order, whatever the quantity. Each sample is USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design and covers its pattern or print in all colourways. It's also non-refundable and isn't credited against bulk.

items.question: Does the quoted price include shipping and duties, and which Incoterms do you quote on?
items.answer: Our all-in DDP price includes shipping and duties. We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms. [DDP delivery is available worldwide](/shipping/), with duties, customs and freight in one price.

items.question: How long is a quoted price valid before I have to ask for a new one?
items.answer: Your quoted price stays valid for 30 days from the date we issue it.

items.question: When is the balance due after the deposit, and which payment methods do you accept?
items.answer: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment. We invoice in USD and take T/T bank transfer for both payments. Sample and design fees are paid before sampling, and you can pay those through PayPal as well. Sampling starts as soon as the fee clears. For these fees, PayPal gets sampling started sooner than T/T but comes with higher transaction fees, and T/T suits larger amounts.
